https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?]
While the Trump administration and RFK Jr. undermine vaccine safety from Washington, states like Colorado are stepping up to protect public health.
And Georgia could be doing the same — with the right leadership.
As a scientist and someone who has spent my time in office fighting for evidence-based policy, it breaks my heart to watch politicians play games with public health. Casting doubt on vaccine safety doesn’t just create confusion — it leads to real harm, especially for children, seniors, and immunocompromised families.
Colorado is showing what responsible leadership looks like: putting science first, protecting access, and ensuring communities stay safe.
Georgia deserves nothing less.
That’s why I’m asking you to add your name to my petition calling on Georgia lawmakers to defend vaccine access, reject political interference, and stand firmly with science.
We can build a state where our leaders protect families instead of pandering to conspiracy theorists — but only if we make our voices impossible to ignore.
Will you add your name today and join me in demanding that Georgia stand up for science? [https://secure.ngpvan.com/Pu8ayb7DR0OXEfSM9edl5w2]

Speaker Mike Johnson came to Southwest Washington to campaign for my opponent, John Braun.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?]
FIGHT BACK [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?]
That tells you everything you need to know.
Mike Johnson didn't come here because he's worried about our roads. He didn't come here because he wants to help small businesses stay open. He didn't come here because he cares about lowering costs for working families.
He came here because Washington Republicans think they can buy, bully, and nationalize this district.
And hey, you don’t just have to take it from me:
Mike Johnson said it himself: "Washington's Third District is going to help decide the fate of the republic." He called this race "a big one" and pointed to the Cook Political Report's list of just 18 toss-up House races , with ours right at the top. Then he made their goal crystal clear: if John Braun wins, Republicans will keep—and grow—their House majority.
This race isn't just on their radar—it's one of their highest priorities.
They want another reliable vote. Another member of Congress who will do what party leaders tell him. Another politician who answers to Washington instead of Southwest Washington.
That's not why you sent me to Congress.
You sent me there to fight for Southwest Washington—even when it's unpopular. To stand up for our timber communities. To protect the right to repair. To support local manufacturers and small businesses. To put this district ahead of any political party.
Now they're sending the Speaker of the House into our backyard because they think this seat belongs to them.
It doesn't.
It belongs to the people who live here.
Today, we have an opportunity to send Mike Johnson, John Braun, and every DC insider a message they won't forget:
Southwest Washington isn't for sale.
We won't be bullied.
And we won't let outside politicians decide who represents our communities.
Will you rush a contribution of $5 or whatever you can right now to help us send that message loud and clear? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?]
Every dollar we raise today is proof that this campaign belongs to the people of Southwest Washington—not the political machine in Washington, D.C.
Let's show them what this district is made of.
Thank you,
Marie Gluesenkamp Perez

Hi, I have to get up early a lot nowadays, and there’s not much that beats the first cup of coffee of the day.

But when you’re running in a high-stakes Senate race like this one – where anything can happen at any given moment – the nights are just as important as the mornings.

Right now, Patrick (my campaign manager) is texting me live updates about where things stand with our fundraising, and I’ve got a list of things we have to do first thing tomorrow. **In the meantime, though, I told him I’d reach out to my top supporters and see if they could lend a hand.**

[**_If you’re able to spare a few bucks before you hit the hay, please chip in here._**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136996713/639333698/-1037742479?amounts=250,100,50,25,5&amount=5&refcode=email_fr_t1nd_jtk5744&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0MGZlNDI5Mi0yNTk1LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=hdbM99HlYlUWu9ZBD4-Ht4ZUzz8UmtpWN-8ss0Sy7bg=)

Reflection comes easy at night, and I’m thinking back to all the conversations I’ve had on the campaign trail so far.

Ohioans, like folks all across the country, are worried about rising costs. They’re fed up with the corruption and power grabs happening in Washington. They’re frustrated with DC politicians like Jon Husted who have left them in the dust.

Yet through it all, so many folks are showing up at our campaign events, or they’re knocking on doors with their neighbors, or they’re stopping for a quick chat with me, because **they believe that we _can_ do better.**

With experts at _The Cook Political Report_ ,_MS NOW_ , and even _Fox News_ calling this race a “Toss Up,” we have an incredible opportunity to flip this battleground seat – and the Senate – but it won’t be easy.

# Your Private Invitation: Waterfront Home Dinner.
Dear Maryland friend, You know it. We know it. Everyone seems to understand it. Maryland is at a cross-roads for our destiny and the future of our families, property, businesses and everything that we've worked hard to build.

The next three months will determine the direction of the next four years.

Wes Moore has in the last few weeks given us a Triple Kick to the Gut.

He lost the Triple Crown, with its exclusion from the Thoroughbred Championship because of failed negotiations. Instead, he sunk over $600 million into buying the Maryland horse-racing industry with your tax money. What a waste.

The Key Bridge is now not likely to be built before 2031. [Come hear ](https://us.list-manage.com/J3ZQkaO97ye?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b)my first-hand knowledge of why that is true.

And now he wants to take our last voice of opposition - the First District Congressional seat.

[Join me tomorrow night](https://us.list-manage.com/fq1QEVOrkba?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b) with Governor Ehrlich, Ed & Cindy Hartman and Jeff & Melanie Dunaway at a private waterfront home dinner.

Come hear me discuss my recent trip to the Republican Governor's Association retreat, my meetings with the nation's top Governors, and my discussions with attendees at that event who have recently met with Wes Moore, providing inside information into important issues and pending matters not otherwise known to the public.

Come also to hear the breaking information showing why we will win this November with your help.

Please [join us](https://us.list-manage.com/NBU_4kHX5SA?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b) tomorrow night. See you there!
For Maryland,

Dan Cox
Republican Nominee for Maryland Governor

| Team,

**Leaders We Deserve is going to be the super PAC to end all super PACs.**

_Citizens United_ has flooded our democracy with corporate cash, dark money, and special interest influence for over a decade. And the only way to fix it permanently is to elect leaders who will fight to overturn it with the urgency it demands.

But until that happens, we can’t send our candidates into races against opponents flush with unlimited corporate money, and tell them to fight with both hands behind their backs. That’s _not_ a winning strategy.

**We play the game we have, and use the tools of a broken system to beat it in its own arena.** And we keep fighting until the system that makes this necessary no longer exists.

Dear Peter,
---
The month of July reminded us that every gathering, every conversation, and every opportunity is ultimately about glorifying Christ and proclaiming the Gospel. Throughout the month, TPUSA Faith traveled across the country to multiple Make Heaven Crowded tour stops, supported the Chapter Leadership Summit in our nation’s capital, and celebrated America’s 250th anniversary under fireworks across the country. Amid every gathering, our prayer remained the same: that Christ would be made known, His Church strengthened, and His kingdom advanced.

### **Make Heaven Crowded**
The Make Heaven Crowded Tour traveled to a new city each week in July, proclaiming the Gospel across the country. Believers were encouraged, churches were strengthened, and lives were impacted in Washington, D.C., Crown Point, Ind., Louisville, Ky., Seattle, Wash., and Anchorage, Alaska.
###
We praise God for the lives He is transforming and are grateful to witness His work across our nation.
###
Attendees heard from many faithful voices proclaiming the hope of the Gospel. At the Crown Point, Indiana, tour stop, Christian country artist Anne Wilson shared this encouraging message on living as a light in a dark world.

### **Chapter Leadership Summit**
At Turning Point USA's Chapter Leadership Summit (CLS), more than 2,500 high school and college students from across America gathered in our nation's capital for one reason. They believe America is worth saving, and they intend to be the generation that does it. Students were motivated and challenged by speakers including Erika Kirk and Bryce Crawford to boldly lead, stand firm in their convictions and make an eternal impact on their campuses. Drawing from Ephesians 6, Erika Kirk reminded students that faithful leadership begins by relying on God's strength, putting on the full armor of God, and standing firm in the face of trials and opposition.

clean_body: From coast to coast, we witnessed the Gospel proclaimed and lives impacted! | Dear Peter, The month of July reminded us that every gathering, every conversation, and every opportunity is ultimately about glorifying Christ and proclaiming the Gospel. Throughout the month, TPUSA Faith traveled across the country to multiple Make Heaven Crowded tour stops, supported the Chapter Leadership Summit in our nation’s capital, and celebrated America’s 250th anniversary under fireworks across the country. Amid every gathering, our prayer remained the same: that Christ would be made known, His Church strengthened, and His kingdom advanced. | Sponsor Highlight: Amazing Grace | Make Heaven Crowded The Make Heaven Crowded Tour traveled to a new city each week in July, proclaiming the Gospel across the country. Believers were encouraged, churches were strengthened, and lives were impacted in Washington, D.C., Crown Point, Ind., Louisville, Ky., Seattle, Wash., and Anchorage, Alaska. We praise God for the lives He is transforming and are grateful to witness His work across our nation. Attendees heard from many faithful voices proclaiming the hope of the Gospel. At the Crown Point, Indiana, tour stop, Christian country artist Anne Wilson shared this encouraging message on living as a light in a dark world. | Chapter Leadership Summit At Turning Point USA's Chapter Leadership Summit (CLS), more than 2,500 high school and college students from across America gathered in our nation's capital for one reason. They believe America is worth saving, and they intend to be the generation that does it. Students were motivated and challenged by speakers including Erika Kirk and Bryce Crawford to boldly lead, stand firm in their convictions and make an eternal impact on their campuses. Drawing from Ephesians 6, Erika Kirk reminded students that faithful leadership begins by relying on God's strength, putting on the full armor of God, and standing firm in the face of trials and opposition. | Make Heaven Crowded Tour The Make Heaven Crowded tour continues throughout the month of August! This month, we will be in El Paso, Texas, and would love for you to join us. Register at the link above and check out our previous events on ! | Faith Forward Pastors’ Summit Santa Barbara, CA This month, we will also be gathering pastors and ministry leaders in Santa Barbara, California, for our second Pastors Summit this year! This event will be centered around fellowship and the equipping of the saints to faithfully serve their churches, featuring Pastor Lucas Miles, Andrew Sedra, Eric Metaxas, Riley Gaines and many more! If you are interested in attending, click the link above to register! | Prep Year Applications Are Open for Fall 2026 is a 9-month residential program for 18- to 20-year-olds focused on faith, leadership, and American history. Hosted at in Elgin, IL, and in Fort Worth, TX, students live on a real college campus and earn college credit. Every accepted student receives a $25,000 scholarship, so families pay only a $2,000 registration fee. If your student is deciding what comes after graduation, encourage them to | Take Part in our Monthly Challenge! Download the graphics below and make this month's verse your phone wallpaper. Read the devotional each day. Memorize the verse. Let the Word of God shape your decisions and your conversations. Will You Pray With Us? Alone, with your family, or with a few believers from your church, pray for revival in America. Pray for bold pastors. Pray for courageous young believers. Pray for God to move in this nation as He has never moved before. One Last Thing... Everything we are doing happens because of faithful partners like you! Your generosity carries the mission forward by allowing us to reach more churches, more campuses, and more young people with a strong biblical worldview at the moment our culture needs it most. If the Lord is stirring you to give, click the link below for more information. Thank you for standing with us. You are family in this movement. The Church doesn't get to sit this one out... we have souls to reach and a nation in which to reach them. Let's make Heaven crowded! name: Jamie Davis
subject: A Black man could never win a statewide Louisiana election
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jamie Davis for U
body:
Don’t tell me what’s “impossible” in Louisiana. My family worked this Delta land when they were slaves. Today my son and I farm the very same fields together - but now we own it.
| | | | | [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001_OpqSgblVp2H1xutZXXTVFeJuq7Ymq1Hc3htgqxgHTjGjkIclHMlF_YJg8-4pKHVvz2Lb8hiWEKYcpxpbL4H4zVDjXS5rVg8L3DyCqE4zlyLG5I3rspF-qhLwLPorbjBip4QS9Pd-XsT6OXq9Zndsd2jh2B-P5uWI4-jeCPUbWM1ftMsngFdZXxKJJRM_vGKxh3PS6OYSit5UQIwlfRrlouVJnwMlxO7I7g0cgRayAU=&c=9V8O6AksF-JGdusZr1P_tdnf73H6t7BFjhDN-OmkvER_fKW1n7tWcg==&ch=tUOkGilPC7PiVa_YLr1GYe1XKqtXlQUx8vrG8R3z-eZBdQOP_whz4g==)
---
| Peter,
Some folks around here still say a Black man can't win a statewide election in Louisiana. I hear it all the time.
We haven't had a black US Senator or statewide elected official since Reconstruction. But I'm a farmer. And I know what grows in this soil.
My family worked this Delta land when they were slaves and then sharecroppers. Today my son and I farm the very same fields together - but now we own it. So don't tell me what's "impossible" in Louisiana.
---
| [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001_OpqSgblVp2H1xutZXXTVFeJuq7Ymq1Hc3htgqxgHTjGjkIclHMlF_YJg8-4pKHVvz2Lb8hiWEKYcpxpbL4H4zVDjXS5rVg8L3DyCqE4zlyLG5I3rspF-qhLwLPorbjBip4QS9Pd-XsT6OXq9Zndsd2jh2B-P5uWI4-jeCPUbWM1ftMsngFdZXxKJJRM_vGKxh3PS6OYSit5UQIwlfRrlp4C3iIbYzFjAGxEBaQyuDE=&c=9V8O6AksF-JGdusZr1P_tdnf73H6t7BFjhDN-OmkvER_fKW1n7tWcg==&ch=tUOkGilPC7PiVa_YLr1GYe1XKqtXlQUx8vrG8R3z-eZBdQOP_whz4g==)
---
My son and I on our farm in 2021. The same soil our ancestors worked for free.
This state was built by Black hands. We cleared the land, built the levees, grew the crops, served in uniform, and helped write the laws that shaped this place.
And history proves something most people forget:
We've done this before. Right after the Civil War, Black leaders here in Louisiana were elected statewide. They expanded public education, protected civil rights, and even elected the first Black governor in American history. Not somewhere else. Right here.
So, when people say it can't happen now, what they're really saying is we shouldn't try. I don't accept that. And I know you don't either.
I'm Jamie Davis -- a farmer, a father, and the Democrat running for the U.S. Senate here in Louisiana-- I'm running to prove that working families, rural towns, and everyday Louisianans still matter. [But campaigns like ours don't run on corporate checks. They run on people. If you believe Louisiana is ready to make history again, will you chip in $30 (or whatever you can) right now to help us reach more voters?](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001_OpqSgblVp2H1xutZXXTVFeJuq7Ymq1Hc3htgqxgHTjGjkIclHMlF_YJg8-4pKHVeOczOoJ9f6wYusNZSt4AuRikmvQRb_ukh-qJDsZAXFQKT33zRhJXGVHDuIYzG5UJpjIUz6Nv90CNrD1vvFmifOwSTFtydjKkRSjifpaahirxSdyRfxVaKWGFsYgQ0OS3hl_n798aS7hrcDAMf2F_kLeo3AbI-E-yeG_r4-XtgEgBu4yEfXQHwg==&c=9V8O6AksF-JGdusZr1P_tdnf73H6t7BFjhDN-OmkvER_fKW1n7tWcg==&ch=tUOkGilPC7PiVa_YLr1GYe1XKqtXlQUx8vrG8R3z-eZBdQOP_whz4g==)

In the river of incoherent "takes" and information we are all made to swim in, this is my life raft: Every so often, I revise a list of facts that seem to point to more durable features of our political terrain. I include facts about public opinion if they appear to reflect a consistent and settled understanding.
I spent some time this week updating my list, so here's a first take on the 2026 Midterm Edition of Essential Facts. These are not meant to be predictive of anything and are listed in no particular order:
This post is free because these facts are important. You can still support more work like this by becoming a paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..5p4owNG1dkQuppObNweC6ykjtNv5HYn9jb2NCKwFXJE?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=210609972)
* Before the Iran War started, [less than half](https://substack.com/redirect/859dc57d-48f5-4b9e-b6ee-89be6812e79e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of Americans had enough cash to cover an emergency $1,000 expense.
* Research [completed just last week](https://substack.com/redirect/a9feaf6a-f9ef-45d4-9e9e-4d4ec5fd935d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) shows Democrats have opened up an 8-point advantage on handling the cost of living. We were even with Republicans at the start of the year. Good, but it's only 35-27 now.
* This year, the share of our national income earned by workers hit a new low, while the share booked as corporate profits hit a new high. (I was surprised coverage of this in the [Wall Street Journal (gift link)](https://substack.com/redirect/9d82492c-fbec-4bfd-a7aa-f08f40306f60?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) was not a bigger story.)
* The most [popular](https://substack.com/redirect/35ac8531-810c-4536-a1ab-95ebde0c36bc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) elected official among Democrats in America, by far, is Bernie Sanders (and he is not even a Democrat!). The second is AOC. Important when you try to make sense of primaries.
* Half of Pennsylvania Democrats have a positive view of the Democratic Socialists of America. Only 15% have an unfavorable view. (Your support helped me access some private research I can't link here. Thank you!)
* Even though the DSA draws its votes mostly from [highly educated](https://substack.com/redirect/b97891a7-6af0-4228-bd41-8be82b46d693?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) voters, I am choosing to believe most of these Pennsylvanians don't know that one of the chairs of the DSA just [told](https://substack.com/redirect/3d92fb09-c74e-47e8-a709-2fc45b9f8e98?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) The New Yorker that the mass slaughter, rape, and kidnapping of Jews in Israel on October 7 was "largely inevitable," and reaffirmed her support for those who rallied for Hamas in New York the day after the attack.
* I asked Claude to make this table comparing Trump's current popularity to Biden's in 2022, and you can see how similar they are, with Trump actually holding his party slightly better. Notable since '22 was decent for Biden:

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e44f31f5-93e6-4968-ab94-e01bbd10ef6c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* On the other hand, enthusiasm to vote among Republicans has [dropped dramatically](https://substack.com/redirect/5335f27f-4a95-4ea1-adae-7e84089c2f19?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and seems to be worse than Democrats' enthusiasm in 2022, and worse than Republicans' own enthusiasm in 2018.
* Can money buy back any of that enthusiasm? Outside of each side's candidate campaign accounts, Republicans have at least _**three times**_ as much money as the Democrats, which is different than previous cycles. This chart from [Politico](https://substack.com/redirect/00665ed1-dfb1-4da6-beeb-30bc7fd60fd5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) sums up it pretty well:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a6d44739-1a3a-4afb-8516-8dfae062b019?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* Some say a "wave" could overcome these dynamics, which is true, but people tend to forget that ticket-splitting still happens to a significant degree:
* In 2020, Susan Collins (who won) got almost 57,000 more votes than Donald Trump (who lost), which was about 7%. Decisive.
* Mid-term electorates are different, but note that in 2022 Democrat Josh Shapiro and Republican Brian Fitzpatrick each carried the same congressional district by [double](https://substack.com/redirect/c424c8dd-d8bd-485e-998c-8e603bf48130?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) digits.
* 2022 also reminds us how the mid-term pattern of the President's party losing power is a [less dependable](https://substack.com/redirect/ef4d38f6-a861-48db-b5cf-13ce795f008f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) pattern for Senate races than for House races.
* To take control of the Senate in 2026, Democrats need to hang on to _both_ Michigan and Georgia, _and_ win at least four of these six: Maine, North Carolina, Ohio, Iowa, Alaska, Texas. (Then, we'd need to hope Fetterman didn't flip to become a Republican and give back control of the chamber.). A tall order.
* While these states are hard to win, you should not think of them as one-off exceptions. They are the new map. The 2030 redistricting will [shift more representation](https://substack.com/redirect/74911a70-58ec-43e4-87b1-1f085c451727?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the Sun Belt and make it impossible for Democrats to win the White House purely with its old "blue wall" strategy.
* Education is emerging as [the critical divide](https://substack.com/redirect/b3fb5d07-52c2-4791-ae77-a940d1992680?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in American politics, with 2024 having the highest level of educational polarization seen yet.
* Of the six states I mentioned above, five are below the national average in percentage of voters with a bachelor's degree.
* Yet Nevada is even further below the national average than these five, and Democrats control both of its Senate seats.
* Two years ago, Democrats held a Senate seat in the state with the lowest percentage of bachelor's degree holders in the entire country. His name was Joe Manchin.
* A Democrat who succeeded with working-class voters more recently was definitely not a DSA member: In 2025, Gov. Abigail Spanberger won [half](https://substack.com/redirect/8dee117c-c7a2-45f8-813f-74fa4b9308e4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of these voters, a significant number considering Harris won 42% in 2024.
* Also in 2025, [Cuomo beat Mamdani](https://substack.com/redirect/bb8999a3-c53a-4784-bb8e-38a6c66bff2e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) among voters without a college degree.
* Last month, Susan Collins was beating Platner [among working-class voters](https://substack.com/redirect/124f7d9d-3f92-4f60-a3e4-af128e183dbf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by more than 20 (he was getting 37%), and Stevens was beating El-Sayed by a similar amount.

Hope this is helpful. How about a [quote](https://substack.com/redirect/903aef87-c555-4a32-9a19-d7037059e55b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from the late, great Senator Daniel Patrick Moynihan to close?
> There is a center in American politics. It can govern. The [National Commission on Social Security Reform] is just an example of what can be done. First, get your facts straight. Everyone is entitled to his own opinion, but not his own facts. Second, decide to live with the facts. Third, resolve to surmount them. Because, fourth, what is at stake is our capacity to govern.

Some of the 2028 Presidential hopefuls for the Democratic Party
The Democratic National Committee's Rules and Bylaws Committee voted to keep South Carolina at the front of the 2028 presidential primary calendar. The early primary window expanded from five states to six. The primary order now runs [South Carolina on January 22, Nevada on February 1, New Hampshire on February 8, New Mexico on February 15, Michigan on February 22, and Virginia on February 29](https://substack.com/redirect/86247ce0-1d31-4218-bd82-1749d3515c64?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), with Super Tuesday on March 7, 2028. [New Mexico and Virginia are in the early window for the first time](https://substack.com/redirect/e9722e34-1f83-4499-9071-f5c7a9d9b723?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
On the new order, [members of the panel invoked Black Americans' long struggle for voting rights and the need to build political power in the South](https://substack.com/redirect/86247ce0-1d31-4218-bd82-1749d3515c64?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and [several said South Carolina's position gained salience after the Supreme Court further gutted the Voting Rights Act earlier this year](https://substack.com/redirect/cc96279e-d941-481e-8816-540225ac0d71?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). That argument is real and valid, but there is another read on this most people are missing and no one is writing about.
The order of the primary is a tell on where the party is focused on picking up votes. Based on the lay of the land for the 2026 midterms cycle, as well as the shift we've seen to a male-dominated brand strategy for the party nationwide, we can apply five basic filters to narrow down the field of likely Presidential candidates. And there will be many and at last count, I am confident there will be at least 20 Democratic challengers.
These Democrats are: Kamala Harris, Gavin Newsom, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Pete Buttigieg, Cory Booker, Ruben Gallego, Chris Murphy, Wes Moore, Andy Beshear, Jon Ossoff, Raphael Warnock, JB Pritzker, Ro Khanna, Mark Kelly, Tim Walz, Amy Klobuchar, Gretchen Whitmer, Josh Shapiro, Roy Cooper, Rahm Emanuel.
Applying all five filters to these 20 candidates reduces the field from 20 to 2.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/65db4336-e696-4428-a7ec-ebf5779c42f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
#### Filter 1: The Black Church as a Foundation
[Black voters make up about 60 percent of South Carolina's Democratic primary electorate](https://substack.com/redirect/cccb4566-c1fe-42bc-a05a-9b49d42d4d86?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). That number is why the state is first, and it is where most analysis of this decision stops. I am going further.
[Pew finds 84 percent of Black Protestants identify with or lean Democratic](https://substack.com/redirect/9eda1bd3-78ce-4224-9c11-7b75262bc58e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and it finds something that matters more for a primary. [Among white adults, Republicans attend services more often than Democrats. Among Black Americans no such gap exists, and Black adults across every religious background are strongly Democratic. Black adults who attend services at least yearly are significantly more likely than attenders in the general population to say they have heard sermons about voting, protesting, and civic engagement](https://substack.com/redirect/30896a51-9726-496e-9a77-0c9af15ae64c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
The Black church in South Carolina is an organized, politically active distribution network, where candidates get introduced and where an endorsement travels with weight. When Joe Biden needed the state in 2024, [he campaigned at a barbershop and spoke at a luncheon at a Black church](https://substack.com/redirect/cccb4566-c1fe-42bc-a05a-9b49d42d4d86?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). He leaned heavily on Senator Jim Clyburn that most people acknowledge has the strongest influence on this network.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8b3a1732-7628-418a-8d4d-8520b7514a27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Representative Ro Khanna and Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear attend South Carolina Senator Jim Clyburn's Fish Fry in May.
Senator Jim Clyburn endorsed Biden days before the 2020 primary, and [that endorsement rescued a collapsing campaign and carried him to the presidency](https://substack.com/redirect/4615e4d0-9675-4ae4-83c1-464b15f16746?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). He has been picking sides far longer. [He backed Hillary Clinton over Bernie Sanders in 2016, stayed formally neutral in 2008 while being seen as tacitly supporting Barack Obama, and chose John Kerry over fellow Southerner John Edwards in 2004](https://substack.com/redirect/f01a244c-4252-4136-9e8c-e55de7ac1476?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Asked whether his fish fry was really world famous, Clyburn told NPR: "Well, it's my world."
Two months ago, [the 34th annual World Famous Fish Fry featured Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear and Representative Ro Khanna](https://substack.com/redirect/10d47c2e-9627-494d-9d09-ace26db81378?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Gavin Newsom [spent the day before his memoir's release doing meet-and-greets in Berkeley and Clarendon counties before a Rock Hill event moderated by former DNC chair Jaime Harrison](https://substack.com/redirect/4816e907-5fb1-4ba0-9cc2-46473d9b49bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Wes Moore keynoted the Blue Palmetto Dinner and [opened by calling Clyburn the voice that has driven more change than any other](https://substack.com/redirect/c2b3df80-1a88-4ca8-99e2-9ca90d4dd246?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
This church network should also tell you something else. A candidate who spends a year working South Carolina pulpits comes out the other side fluent in a language the party has not spoken in a generation. Faith vocabulary is a rare political asset that travels. The same cadence that lands in a sanctuary in Orangeburg lands in a Sunday school room in Paducah, and it reaches a bloc the party has written off entirely. [Pew puts white evangelical voters at 85 percent Republican against 14 percent Democratic](https://substack.com/redirect/9eda1bd3-78ce-4224-9c11-7b75262bc58e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
That's the theory the party is testing right now. [A striking number of clergy are running for office as Democrats, including three ministers running for Congress in Iowa alone](https://substack.com/redirect/216c29c7-4c83-4289-90c6-71cf7212c4f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Andy Beshear and his wife are both deacons at their Disciples of Christ church in Louisville. His forthcoming book is titled _Go and Do Likewise_ , after the Parable of the Good Samaritan. He blames his own party for the gap with churches, arguing Democrats stopped explaining their motivations in the terms religious voters use, and he told the AP that [his faith is his authentic why](https://substack.com/redirect/216c29c7-4c83-4289-90c6-71cf7212c4f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
_**Who doesn 't survive this filter? **_Josh Shapiro and Gretchen Whitmer
Sorry Josh Shapiro and Gretchen Whitmer. It won't be you.

#### Filter Two: A Moderate Democrat
The party has told you what it thinks wins. [The DCCC's 2026 recruitment strategy sought candidates resembling a small group of moderate Democrats who have shown they can win where Trump performed well](https://substack.com/redirect/90425039-f9af-42d0-8164-82af66e30a6a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), including seats Trump carried by 17 points.
An institution that spends two years telling itself moderates are the answer does not switch theories for the presidential cycle. It scales them up. That removes the Democratic Party putting up anyone in the progressive wing on ideological grounds alone, regardless of what those candidates are polling.
You can watch this theory operate on individual candidates in real time. James Talarico spent years in the Texas legislature calling to tear ICE down and describing the border as a welcome mat. [The month he launched his Senate campaign, he recast himself as a border security Democrat, telling a podcast host he had called out Biden for failing to secure the border, and softening his positions on guns and transgender issues in the same interview](https://substack.com/redirect/6761caf1-db3a-4d4d-910b-12127b7da2f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). [He now runs a Frontera Tour of the Rio Grande promising a mix of barriers and surveillance technology](https://substack.com/redirect/d3934024-5699-4382-a285-8025e1c3f19d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The same conversion, on the same issues, is running through red-state Democratic campaigns across the map this cycle. The recruitment push Democrats have branded a masculinity strategy has a policy half that gets less attention, and this is it: candidates entering Trump-won races and shedding the progressive positions that made them targets. That is the substance under what the party means when it says a candidate can win in Trump country.

#### Filter Three: From a State Trump Won
A moderate record is a claim anyone can make in a primary. Winning a state Trump carried is evidence nobody can argue with, and the party has decided that's the evidence it needs.
Beshear won the Kentucky governorship twice, in a state Trump carried in 2024 by roughly 30 points. Ossoff holds a Senate seat in Georgia, which Trump carried, and defends it this November. Neither man has to argue he can win Trump voters.
A blue-state Democrat cannot make that case no matter how disciplined a moderate he runs. So this filter clears the field substantially: Gavin Newsom governs California, which Harris won by roughly 20 points, and no matter how far he goes to sound moderate, a Californian asking Kentucky to trust his read in Trump country is making an argument, not pointing at a result. Pete Buttigieg now runs out of Michigan, a state Harris lost, but he has never carried it or anything like it on a ballot, and a competitive mayoralty in Indiana a decade ago is not the credential the party is looking for.
JB Pritzker governs Illinois and Tim Walz governs Minnesota, both comfortably blue, both men who would have to explain why their record is sellable to moderate voters. Amy Klobuchar has won Minnesota by margins of twenty and thirty points, while Harris carried it by four, proving she is popular at home in a blue state, not that she can drag Republican voters across the party line. Cory Booker represents New Jersey, which the party now watches with genuine worry after Harris carried it by six, but watching a state slip is not the same as a Democrat proving he can win where it already went red. Rahm Emanuel is Illinois. Chris Murphy is Connecticut. Both safe, both disqualified by the same logic.
Gavin Newsom, Rahm Emmanuel, Amy Klobuchar, Tim Walz, Cory Booker, Wes Moore, Pete Buttigieg, and Chris Murphy - all from blue states, and all eliminated based on this filter

### Filter four: What the Democratic Party Means by Electability
I want to be exact about whose reasoning I am describing. This is not my read of what American voters will accept, rather its the operating theory of the people who recruit and clear candidates for national races. That theory holds that the voters Democrats lost are men who went to Trump, and that winning them back requires a candidate who looks like them.

### Filter Five Will Test the Progressive/Moderate Divide on Israel
By now you may have noticed we have winnowed our list from 20 names to just three: Senator Jon Ossoff, Senator Mark Kelly, and Governor Andy Bashear. A combination of these three names is what the Democratic institution will want on the ticket for 2028. But they will have to content with a 5th filter, being pushed up by the base: Israel.
[Pew found in April that 80 percent of Democrats hold an unfavorable view of Israel, up from 69 percent a year earlier and 53 percent in 2022](https://substack.com/redirect/40ee5e8f-4e2e-43a2-bb55-22530736b23a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). [A New York Times-Siena poll in May found 24 percent of Democrats support additional aid to Israel while 68 percent oppose it](https://substack.com/redirect/ebb59f54-aef5-4213-8f17-06b06738b8f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). [Gallup has American favorability toward Israel falling from 75 percent in 2021 to 46 percent in 2026](https://substack.com/redirect/e49115aa-4963-4e6c-bf61-2b9b1dbcdea1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Additionally, and perhaps more importantly, [Three-fifths of American Jews view Netanyahu unfavorably, and white evangelicals are the only major religious group where a majority still views the Israeli government favorably](https://substack.com/redirect/e49115aa-4963-4e6c-bf61-2b9b1dbcdea1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
[A House floor vote in July month split Democrats and their own leadership over cutting military aid to Israel, with Nancy Pelosi saying afterward that US policy must change and the Netanyahu government cannot maintain its current course. In New Jersey, an organizer who ran openly against AIPAC won a February special election after AIPAC affiliates spent millions attacking her](https://substack.com/redirect/40ee5e8f-4e2e-43a2-bb55-22530736b23a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Abdul al-Sayed won the Michigan Senatorial primary on Tuesday, a huge upset for AIPAC-backed Haley Stevens.
### How the Calendar Fits the Narrative
South Carolina is the coronation. Whoever the brokers move behind on January 22 gets the coalescence that follows, the endorsements, the money, the donors who were waiting for a signal, and the press narrative that the race is effectively over. The field will thin fast, the way it did for Biden in 2020, and the moderate winner will spend February being sold as inevitable by the Democratic machine.
Michigan is seen, rightly, as a cross section of the American midwest, and where the moderate views on Israel will be tested. It comes third, close enough to the front to matter and late enough that the nominee is already presumed. It asks one question of whoever is left in the primary: who among them can hold the November electorate and bridge the divide between progressive and moderates on Gaza. A nominee who cannot bridge this divide is a nominee who cannot carry Michigan, and likely will not be able to carry the country in the general election. But the party is betting that inevitability and vibes will turn out Democrats in droves larger than who stayed home or voted for Trump in Michigan in 2024.

### The 2028 Presidential Ticket Prediction
[Pew found 61 percent of veteran registered voters backed Trump over Harris in 2024 against 37 percent for Harris, and 63 percent of veteran voters lean Republican](https://substack.com/redirect/ce9fb7f7-ee31-4b1e-82d9-370a545e31f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
On November 18, 2025, six Democratic lawmakers made a video reminding service members they can refuse illegal orders. [Trump called it seditious behavior punishable by death](https://substack.com/redirect/6f8a2f95-42cf-4297-a246-1e84054940fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Six days later [the Pentagon opened a review of Kelly and raised recall to active duty for court-martial as a possible outcome](https://substack.com/redirect/e10fc6d0-0b8b-4019-b036-b4c9329eba8f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Hegseth noting Kelly was the only one of the six still subject to military law. Then it collapsed. [Hegseth announced no recall and no military proceedings, only a retirement-grade determination to demote a sitting senator and cut his pension](https://substack.com/redirect/1bf766bc-3d53-4650-8a89-1c324e3ee326?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Kelly sued. [On February 12, 2026, Judge Richard Leon, a George W. Bush appointee, blocked the Pentagon, writing that it had trampled Kelly's First Amendment freedoms and threatened the liberties of millions of military retirees](https://substack.com/redirect/cafc0919-f930-4476-9494-65b054a116b8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Mark Kelly is who will balance the 2028 ticket. An elder, moderate statesman with built in credibility, astronaut, veteran, husband of Gabby Giffords is pathway the party will use to bring back veteran voters. He will be the VP candidate no matter who else is in the race. The party can also afford him, since [his term ends January 3, 2029](https://substack.com/redirect/c7a03df4-ca8e-4596-bcda-4059d9a461af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and he is on the ballot in 2028 regardless. No appointed replacement, no special election, no seat handed to a governor.
Based on the timeline, trends, and strategists own admissions, your 2028 presidential ticket will either be:
**Beshear-Kelly or Ossoff-Kelly.**
Nothing is set in stone, but Democrats are not known for changing their tactics. This is where they are looking right now.

clean_body: | | ---|---|--- | | | | | cross-posted a post from ---|---|--- | | | The Angry DemocratAug 11 The Angry Democrat ---|---|--- Check this out from the Whisper Campaign. Laura wrote a really interesting analysis laying out five filters the Democratic Party is using to determine who could be the next presidential nominee. One way the party could enact one of those filters is by making South Carolina the first primary state. Laura brilliantly explains why that matters and what it could mean for the field. The DNC gave Black voters the first primary slot. The same party is running a candidate theory that filters Black candidates out. South Carolina winnows down a field of 20 likely candidates to 2. | | | Aug 10 | | | | | | | | | | | | Some of the 2028 Presidential hopefuls for the Democratic Party The Democratic National Committee's Rules and Bylaws Committee voted to keep South Carolina at the front of the 2028 presidential primary calendar. The early primary window expanded from five states to six. The primary order now runs , with Super Tuesday on March 7, 2028. . On the new order, , and . That argument is real and valid, but there is another read on this most people are missing and no one is writing about. The order of the primary is a tell on where the party is focused on picking up votes. Based on the lay of the land for the 2026 midterms cycle, as well as the shift we've seen to a male-dominated brand strategy for the party nationwide, we can apply five basic filters to narrow down the field of likely Presidential candidates. And there will be many and at last count, I am confident there will be at least 20 Democratic challengers. These Democrats are: Kamala Harris, Gavin Newsom, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Pete Buttigieg, Cory Booker, Ruben Gallego, Chris Murphy, Wes Moore, Andy Beshear, Jon Ossoff, Raphael Warnock, JB Pritzker, Ro Khanna, Mark Kelly, Tim Walz, Amy Klobuchar, Gretchen Whitmer, Josh Shapiro, Roy Cooper, Rahm Emanuel. Applying all five filters to these 20 candidates reduces the field from 20 to 2. Filter 1: The Black Church as a Foundation . That number is why the state is first, and it is where most analysis of this decision stops. I am going further. , and it finds something that matters more for a primary. . The Black church in South Carolina is an organized, politically active distribution network, where candidates get introduced and where an endorsement travels with weight. When Joe Biden needed the state in 2024, . He leaned heavily on Senator Jim Clyburn that most people acknowledge has the strongest influence on this network. | | ---|---|--- Representative Ro Khanna and Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear attend South Carolina Senator Jim Clyburn's Fish Fry in May. Senator Jim Clyburn endorsed Biden days before the 2020 primary, and . He has been picking sides far longer. . Asked whether his fish fry was really world famous, Clyburn told NPR: "Well, it's my world." Two months ago, . Gavin Newsom . Wes Moore keynoted the Blue Palmetto Dinner and . This church network should also tell you something else. A candidate who spends a year working South Carolina pulpits comes out the other side fluent in a language the party has not spoken in a generation. Faith vocabulary is a rare political asset that travels. The same cadence that lands in a sanctuary in Orangeburg lands in a Sunday school room in Paducah, and it reaches a bloc the party has written off entirely. . That's the theory the party is testing right now. . Andy Beshear and his wife are both deacons at their Disciples of Christ church in Louisville. His forthcoming book is titled Go and Do Likewise , after the Parable of the Good Samaritan. He blames his own party for the gap with churches, arguing Democrats stopped explaining their motivations in the terms religious voters use, and he told the AP that . Who doesn 't survive this filter? Josh Shapiro and Gretchen Whitmer Sorry Josh Shapiro and Gretchen Whitmer. It won't be you. Filter Two: A Moderate Democrat The party has told you what it thinks wins. , including seats Trump carried by 17 points. An institution that spends two years telling itself moderates are the answer does not switch theories for the presidential cycle. It scales them up. That removes the Democratic Party putting up anyone in the progressive wing on ideological grounds alone, regardless of what those candidates are polling. You can watch this theory operate on individual candidates in real time. James Talarico spent years in the Texas legislature calling to tear ICE down and describing the border as a welcome mat. . . The same conversion, on the same issues, is running through red-state Democratic campaigns across the map this cycle. The recruitment push Democrats have branded a masculinity strategy has a policy half that gets less attention, and this is it: candidates entering Trump-won races and shedding the progressive positions that made them targets. That is the substance under what the party means when it says a candidate can win in Trump country. Who doesn 't survive this filter? Alexandria Ocasio Cortez, Ro Khanna, and JB Pritzker JB Pritzker, AOC, and Ro Khanna, too progressive for the party Filter Three: From a State Trump Won A moderate record is a claim anyone can make in a primary. Winning a state Trump carried is evidence nobody can argue with, and the party has decided that's the evidence it needs. Beshear won the Kentucky governorship twice, in a state Trump carried in 2024 by roughly 30 points. Ossoff holds a Senate seat in Georgia, which Trump carried, and defends it this November. Neither man has to argue he can win Trump voters. A blue-state Democrat cannot make that case no matter how disciplined a moderate he runs. So this filter clears the field substantially: Gavin Newsom governs California, which Harris won by roughly 20 points, and no matter how far he goes to sound moderate, a Californian asking Kentucky to trust his read in Trump country is making an argument, not pointing at a result. Pete Buttigieg now runs out of Michigan, a state Harris lost, but he has never carried it or anything like it on a ballot, and a competitive mayoralty in Indiana a decade ago is not the credential the party is looking for. JB Pritzker governs Illinois and Tim Walz governs Minnesota, both comfortably blue, both men who would have to explain why their record is sellable to moderate voters. Amy Klobuchar has won Minnesota by margins of twenty and thirty points, while Harris carried it by four, proving she is popular at home in a blue state, not that she can drag Republican voters across the party line. Cory Booker represents New Jersey, which the party now watches with genuine worry after Harris carried it by six, but watching a state slip is not the same as a Democrat proving he can win where it already went red. Rahm Emanuel is Illinois. Chris Murphy is Connecticut. Both safe, both disqualified by the same logic. Gavin Newsom, Rahm Emmanuel, Amy Klobuchar, Tim Walz, Cory Booker, Wes Moore, Pete Buttigieg, and Chris Murphy - all from blue states, and all eliminated based on this filter Filter four: What the Democratic Party Means by Electability I want to be exact about whose reasoning I am describing. This is not my read of what American voters will accept, rather its the operating theory of the people who recruit and clear candidates for national races. That theory holds that the voters Democrats lost are men who went to Trump, and that winning them back requires a candidate who looks like them. | | ---|---|--- Read in the Whisper Campaign archive. . The biggest get was Graham Platner in Maine, a combat veteran and oyster farmer whose campaign collapsed under a Nazi-symbol tattoo, deleted posts appearing to blame sexual assault survivors, and allegations about his conduct with women. A Democratic operative told The 19th that a candidate who was not a straight white man would never have been launched with that record. "Everyone knows it's true," he said, adding that nobody wants to admit it because it would indict the whole of our politics. The party is pitching this openly now. In The Atlantic's "The Return of the Democratic Manly Man," published July 12, . Raphael Warnock and Kamala Harris do not fit the current electability trend in the Democratic party Filter Five Will Test the Progressive/Moderate Divide on Israel By now you may have noticed we have winnowed our list from 20 names to just three: Senator Jon Ossoff, Senator Mark Kelly, and Governor Andy Bashear. A combination of these three names is what the Democratic institution will want on the ticket for 2028. But they will have to content with a 5th filter, being pushed up by the base: Israel. . . . Additionally, and perhaps more importantly, . . Abdul al-Sayed won the Michigan Senatorial primary on Tuesday, a huge upset for AIPAC-backed Haley Stevens. How the Calendar Fits the Narrative South Carolina is the coronation. Whoever the brokers move behind on January 22 gets the coalescence that follows, the endorsements, the money, the donors who were waiting for a signal, and the press narrative that the race is effectively over. The field will thin fast, the way it did for Biden in 2020, and the moderate winner will spend February being sold as inevitable by the Democratic machine. Michigan is seen, rightly, as a cross section of the American midwest, and where the moderate views on Israel will be tested. It comes third, close enough to the front to matter and late enough that the nominee is already presumed. It asks one question of whoever is left in the primary: who among them can hold the November electorate and bridge the divide between progressive and moderates on Gaza. A nominee who cannot bridge this divide is a nominee who cannot carry Michigan, and likely will not be able to carry the country in the general election. But the party is betting that inevitability and vibes will turn out Democrats in droves larger than who stayed home or voted for Trump in Michigan in 2024. The 2028 Presidential Ticket Prediction . On November 18, 2025, six Democratic lawmakers made a video reminding service members they can refuse illegal orders. . Six days later , Hegseth noting Kelly was the only one of the six still subject to military law. Then it collapsed. . Kelly sued. . Mark Kelly is who will balance the 2028 ticket. An elder, moderate statesman with built in credibility, astronaut, veteran, husband of Gabby Giffords is pathway the party will use to bring back veteran voters. He will be the VP candidate no matter who else is in the race. The party can also afford him, since and he is on the ballot in 2028 regardless. No appointed replacement, no special election, no seat handed to a governor. Based on the timeline, trends, and strategists own admissions, your 2028 presidential ticket will either be: Beshear-Kelly or Ossoff-Kelly. Nothing is set in stone, but Democrats are not known for changing their tactics. The stories that Sailors and Marines deployed in support of our needless war with Iran weren't being fed proper meals began circulating in April. It was clear the Department of Defense was having serious trouble supplying the fleet with food. Most of the stories seemed to come from 5,000 Sailors and Marines on the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln, but if it was happening on one ship, it was probably happening across the fleet.
We're now four months into reports of food shortages on the Lincoln, and things are reported to be getting worse. The Lincoln was supposed to be on a seven-month, 210-day deployment. They have been deployed for over 250 days, have just completed 40 days of sustained combat operations, and have recently learned their deployment has been extended again.
The members of our armed forces risk their lives in the defense of our nation. They do so trusting that this nation will take care of them while they stand in harm's way. This administration has broken that trust with our servicemen and women, and they seem incapable of fixing the problem.
The House and Senate Armed Services Committees have a moral and constitutional obligation to investigate matters such as this. But the GOP-led congressional committees are too afraid to speak up for the men and women serving our nation in a war they never needed.

# One Last Thought Until Next Week
---
| | |
---
This week we recorded the Alabama Politics This Week podcast with Josh Moon and David Person, one of the state's largest political podcasts. They asked thoughtful questions about what it means to serve, lead, and create change in Alabama.

I believe service is patriotism in action. Loving your country and your community means being willing to ask difficult questions, hold leaders accountable, and work toward a better future. Patriotism does not belong to one political movement or one set of beliefs. It belongs to anyone willing to show up, serve others, and help build a stronger community.

That work starts close to home.

Every conversation with a neighbor, every town hall, every yard sign placed, every question asked, and every volunteer who steps up helps build something bigger than any one candidate. These actions may seem small on their own, but together they give communities a voice and create the momentum needed for change
We are 84 days away from the general election.

We'll talk soon,

Lee

Most of the stories seemed to come from 5,000 Sailors and Marines on the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln, but if it was happening on one ship, it was probably happening across the fleet. We're now four months into reports of food shortages on the Lincoln, and things are reported to be getting worse. The Lincoln was supposed to be on a seven-month, 210-day deployment. They have been deployed for over 250 days, have just completed 40 days of sustained combat operations, and have recently learned their deployment has been extended again. The members of our armed forces risk their lives in the defense of our nation. They do so trusting that this nation will take care of them while they stand in harm's way. This administration has broken that trust with our servicemen and women, and they seem incapable of fixing the problem. The House and Senate Armed Services Committees have a moral and constitutional obligation to investigate matters such as this. But the GOP-led congressional committees are too afraid to speak up for the men and women serving our nation in a war they never needed. | == | A Few Things to Think About | | | ALABAMA IN THE NEWS | 📰 == The Senate Agriculture Committee failed to advance the farm bill after Democrats opposed the bill's one-year delay of new SNAP cost-sharing requirements for states. In Alabama, the changes could require the state to pay an estimated $174 million and could affect food assistance for roughly 648,000 residents, while the farm bill remains stalled ahead of the current extension's September expiration. | 📰 == Rural hospital closures and service reductions across Alabama are forcing residents to travel long distances or even relocate to access essential and specialized healthcare. Thomasville's hospital closure highlights how financial pressures, low reimbursements, staffing costs, and policy barriers are worsening healthcare access while also threatening rural communities' economic stability. | 📰 == A new ACLU of Alabama report calls Alabama the "most dangerous" state for pregnancy and childbirth, citing a maternal mortality rate nearly twice the national average and significant racial disparities. The report identifies rural healthcare shortages, transportation and financial barriers, limited mental health support, and negative experiences with medical providers as major challenges, and recommends expanding access to doulas and midwives, postpartum care, and maternal healthcare services. | A CALL TO ACTION | As we come down to the last three months, we need you to do four things: First, we need you to get the word out. This is a grassroots campaign which means we're going to rely heavily on you. Share our posts, talk to your friends, and show off those yard signs and bumper stickers. If you don't have a yard sign, email mailto:joinus@leemcinnis4alabama.comto let us know what county you're in, and we'll hook you up with the person in your county who has some. == == == | Second, we need to meet your friends. One asset we have in this campaign is a candidate who will meet with people and have a conversation. Sometimes those conversations can be tough, but they're always productive. Set up a group meeting either in person (which is great) or virtually (which is also great). Email mailto:joinus@leemcinnis4alabama.com to let us know where you are, and we'll work out the details with you. | | | Third, make a plan to vote. We don't know what is going to happen between now and November 3, but the best way to ensure a free and fair election is to show up in huge numbers. Once you have your plan, help your friends and neighbors plan to vote. | | | Fourth, donate to the campaign. You have all been incredibly generous financially, but we are entering the expense phase of this race. Barb and I haven't charged the campaign for gas, meals, or hotel rooms so that we could save money for these last 90 days. Without corporate or foreign-interest PAC money, we knew we would have to run a slim campaign, but now we have to start getting our name in front of a wider audience, and that will require capital. | | == | | One Last Thought Until Next Week | | | This week we recorded the Alabama Politics This Week podcast with Josh Moon and David Person, one of the state's largest political podcasts. They asked thoughtful questions about what it means to serve, lead, and create change in Alabama. I believe service is patriotism in action. Loving your country and your community means being willing to ask difficult questions, hold leaders accountable, and work toward a better future. Patriotism does not belong to one political movement or one set of beliefs. It belongs to anyone willing to show up, serve others, and help build a stronger community. That work starts close to home. Every conversation with a neighbor, every town hall, every yard sign placed, every question asked, and every volunteer who steps up helps build something bigger than any one candidate. These actions may seem small on their own, but together they give communities a voice and create the momentum needed for change We are 84 days away from the general election. We'll talk soon, Lee | | | | == | == ---|--- == | == ---|--- == | == ---|--- mailto:?subject=The%20Latest%20News%20from%20the%20Campaign&body= | mailto:?subject=The%20Latest%20News%20from%20the%20Campaign&body= ---|--- | == == == | | | | Lee McInnis 4 Alabama | PO Box 111 | Opelika, AL 36801 US | | | | | | |

## Meta Agrees to Abbott Data-Center Rules
Gov. Greg Abbott announced Monday that Meta will follow the [data center standards](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGupDAQRE9jMiO3YYAJHGxCNptuiNq4Ae8aG9m9MHP7L_4VflTBUz2V6s9reqEPPq6_cSfD7yVNka4SiJnytGMp_qS_GPCgmDLNGELANU1a6U6qQQJMOLM_aWqxcsYq94SKDPRD17Yd6KbaDHUWmh4G3S2DtUMDzcNR457dsijlbF95c-vUAACgtFK1Qmgfi5sfzUL93FvRKnKeU655I6Y3liV80km5ntNeBbMxH0U0v4QehR6v66r_WX7fUOjxdgs9qkHoEZTQ43o3Y8oSrU3MEmNM_-NMRe7EKOe0757LnUf4yMvzJjdfpMMbUmTKsjBGh9kVoccqG3dcPgRful60at3Rh-9h_NNDT6O_AgAA__-jvIxk) he set for Texas. The rules make data centers pay for their own power lines, reuse their water, avoid disrupting neighborhoods, and drop taxpayer-funded incentives. The Public Utility Commission and ERCOT [must audit each project first](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO5CAQRL8GZ4ygjQ0EDi5xtpdeaLWhPcMJDxbuNXt_f_L-wqb1pKeq-vOxfGDK6f38jTtN_LWV5U3tzMRMddnxPNNFfzHjQe9SKWDOGZ9lAQWjVE5qvWDgdNFisIvTqqLXHU3autGYUUPfvSbvvA3OKI_bCpqUdoPBAW1vneujs12abp1yWmutQKmHQm2GLYah38gGuwqjKCYu9cEvYvrCc8v_ykX1Ecre5enFfJyi_yVgFjC31h5tQ7yhgBkrp5BJwHwvEzDnEjALmHdilKHse-JTfltlxDuiN1OV9TPTKZ_lkriuhVkepVGVDW-InzHxLQNnZb8G2KIfJEUfpXHKyxVGJzftozYDxEC-q1M8Wso5naMVRj13TPm7Pv_09muC_wEAAP__WCSXHg), and companies that don't cooperate can be denied. Abbott said the standards ensure data centers "[pay their own way](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2SozAQhJ9GZKKkMX8OFFxC5ksvpAZpMLoVEiXNgv32W_gVNu7qr7u-f4_pgT74-PyLGxl-LWmKdJZAzJSnDUvxB_3HgDvFlMliCAGfaQIFnVSD1HpCy_6gqcHKmVm5u67I6H7omqbTcKtWg7pzanAIdO-7BVo9L5Y0NoCtItveK28unBq01lqBUrVC3bSLs-1tod72s2gUOc8p17wS0wvLEt7poFzbtFXBrMx7Ebc_AkYB43me9Vfg4woFjBdbwKgGAaNWAkac58QsMcb0HS0VuRGjPH0I0qZtD295el7lZ0c6ZJSWIlOWhTE6zK4IGKts3H51fOl60ajnhj587vBvNR4GfgIAAP__Z8CIuw)" without passing costs to Texas families. ## Drugmaker Picks Houston for $2.3B Campus
Bristol Myers Squibb will build a [$2.3 billion medicine manufacturing campus](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGS4yAURE-DMlzwhRAOCDZRNptuqPrAx2IGCS9ga3z7Le8VJu7qrn7vz8f6gSmn4_Ybd7L9O5b1oLNl6p3qumNr6UmfmPFOR6nkMeeMt7KCAM2F4VKu6Ht60qpwCNaJcJUDWTkbrZSWMA6bNc7g5CY_K6k16DjNHhFHEUGJ6PV1SPY9J4yUUgoQ4iJQqikGP42RZj87pgSF1Eu99I06fWOL-VWeVC--7EO2W-_3xsZfDBYGy3mel6-tPN4hgwVrTz4Tg-VNxmDJxWNmsLiaWi-Z7y-qjbe_j-Qc38qj9XLwGx1Usady8DvWL_5Z3LsLZuIxgIlX7_lMSnBlRuAugOQBlEAhtZJxHqoN9zPlnJqemRK3HVP-_7b_1PLTwr8AAAD__wOVkUc) at Generation Park in northeast Houston, the drugmaker announced Monday. Texas added a $4.89 million Enterprise Fund grant.
## Jalapeño Recall Hits Texas Grocery Shelves
H-E-B [pulled five ready-to-eat meals](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2OpDAUBODTmAzkf7sDB5uQ9aYboof9aLwyNsIe6L79qGc0J5i8VKWv_t2nO8QU8-MvbOjacylTxqsmbA2PaYNa44n_IcGOuRzoIaUEjzJxynVPbc_YBL7FEycJXXAzDTfWoWPGaik146JbnZw9MCaUNUIZBUIZSaW5KR0CeD3bLrp3HbWMMUY5pQMFJtUSvBILGm9mIimG2MoxtBUbPqEu6VVOPAZfti65tbW9EvGH8JHw8bquYXtVyJBbybG8Q4SP80eNGWslfISjRZ-Q8HHFuf_h9d--nnNhmeZ22Ne9O1zYr5hSrNoQSR8bxPS12n771un4ZwAAAP__bn1_tg) from its shelves after the jalapeños inside were linked to a national salmonella outbreak. The San Antonio grocer's Shake Rattle Bowl Southwest Chicken, two Higher Harvest dishes, and two Meal Simple bowls carry use-by dates between Aug. 3 and Aug. 15. Shoppers can return them for a full refund. Randalls, Tom Thumb, Albertsons, Kroger, and Walmart [pulled affected items in Texas](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLFu8yAURp8Gb1iAwXYGhn_xln_taF3DJaG9NhYQO3n7KpX6BN0_fUfnfFznK0SK2-0_rGjrM6R5w7MQ1op5XqGUeOAnEOy4pYwOiAhuaVZC9VyMXMoZXI0HzhoabxfhL7JBK4ex17qXqmvuVukwGq2UgXEwg7sIlA5MUL3sDIDGJtr3nRillFIoIVoBUpvgnekCDm5YmBboY025rXes-IQS6JUOzK1La0P2XuteWPePqYmp6TzPNqTn8ihxw1LeG6YmigFLfREyNf0K8QK0pg2JgKdHXTLCF98z7pDR85CSLxwIc22y9fsZiWLpB6bFbYVIP_D612iHVd8BAAD__09DhQk) as well. Taylor Farms' [recall of salsas, guacamole, and dips](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGu2zAMRb_G3hhIiiLbg4Yu2V7XjgafRCdKacmQWDv9-8Jt_-BNBEHw4tzz42P-wMQpP77jSl7eS5kzHY1JhOq8YmtppxcybpRLpYDMjI8yG2UcqBG0njFI2mm22Ef_qeKke_J6GJ21Tptr__STo0kTqjhOyjhLYQiDujqcbLyZEac--TNOjVprrYxSF4Xa3pYYbteFhjB8dlZRTFLqRZ4k9Ma28O-yU72EsvbsnyJb667fOnPvzP04jsvPN-bz2Jn72eccKKlkZPi_L7-YgVMTiGlr0JAbNmiFI6DAiq9SoZJgYqoNUgbjoAkKNfjngSKcCOfnWjIxI4SSA9V8xvfVx-1IzKm5obPqsWLiv7jyVc27N38CAAD__1eTlho) sold at Target, Trader Joe's, and Whole Foods spans 26 states, and Texas is listed on nearly every item. The peppers were grown in Sinaloa, Mexico, and imported by [Coast Citrus Distributors](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2OpDAQBeDTmAxUZcxf4GATst50Q1SYotu7BW7ZXui-_YgZzQkmK6mk9_S9P7fpRl78fv9NG9v8WsO085mEc-Y4bZSSP_gvCT15D5EdiQjdw6RBtyX0JeJELvuDJ0PFYmdYBizYYte3xrSo6-Jhl6GvwbCuB0OILfQ1ADMMPTaDazQW3l5x0CMiggaogNA06-KaeuXOdbMywIvPIVb5wZlflFZ5h4Nj5cJWiH3k_Eyq_qX0qPR4nmfl5nQ5rr_S43UqPWZ6S4jlSnFL5Teq_FKViWQLO4tQGf7nOTL9U3osol2epxfxqe2UgftGXj5b80_XOqz-CAAA__9tEICs). body:
If you’re like me, you give thanks to God every day that you live in a country that is free, peaceful, and where citizens have inalienable rights.

This sponsored message from Inside Scoop Politics is on behalf of Hillsdale College

| | Dear Fellow American, Are you proud to be an American citizen? If you’re like me, you give thanks to God every day that you live in a country that is free, peaceful, and where citizens have inalienable rights. Most people in history can’t say the same thing—in fact, most people in the world can’t say the same thing even today. You don’t have to be a historian to see that the long practice of citizenship in America is unprecedented. It’s one of our nation’s great achievements. But there’s a catch—citizenship requires vigilance and knowledge to maintain. Especially now, when it faces threats from the far-Left and progressive economic policies, illegal immigration, and more. Everyone who wishes to defend freedom in America requires an understanding of the nature and scope of these challenges. As a college, we know that a proper education is the best defense of liberty. And unlike the vast majority of colleges and universities, we must **reach** and **teach** millions of Americans about liberty. And we have to do it without taking ONE PENNY of government funding—not even indirectly in the form of student grants and loans. NOT. ONE. PENNY—to remain proudly independent. This means that your support is critical to our success. With your help, we’ll engage the far-Left on the battlefield of education. With your help, we will defend liberty against dangerous ideologies. And with your help, we will preserve freedom for future generations of American citizens. You can give safely and securely at this link: [https://secured.hillsdale.edu/hillsdale/dying-citizen](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckcFunDAQhp_G3ED22AHvgUMlwqmbtGmrHJHXM4GRDHax2ap9-irVbh8gx5lf-kbz_a_n6ew48DY_uZV6znnCiJPnwn9oywunnX4evFO-8szBTSChraWtlZqcL3ylybgK-wdQ9s1W1KvOtsa0oGS19Kq9EFrrwT44NK2VF02W5OkN_cl3aCvu33nSKqWU1GAb9OZkOyANEi8Xq4SRR0JXqOEtM1L2MaYUAxf2uYn7XIV-KSVloT8JGAWMmfyxEzYLh5DRBWoIDwHj_1nAiL95m-vbk0KP2Qs9SNnC6UmCgc_mPDwPj4_fBLRHWaccj92T0EPaY07kC2_zLVoJ-ViFHmh1HG5L79bkeN6EHv5duuu8x3ErtBWhhy8vzz-G6WtXv35_qe8mqr3H9ItD4Nx2wsj5ndz4uFblo_1ce_gbAAD__8Qqofo) **And for a gift of $100 or more, you’ll receive a special hardcover edition of Victor Davis Hanson’s book,** **_The Dying Citizen: How Progressive Elites, Tribalism, and Globalization Are Destroying the Idea of America_****. Victor Davis Hanson is a frequent commentator on Fox News and online. He’s also a historian and distinguished fellow here at Hillsdale.** Regarding the book, my boss and teacher, Hillsdale President Larry P. Arnn, has written, “In this book, Hanson demonstrates yet again his command across time and for our time. **This book and he are a treasure.** ” Thank you so much for your partnership in promoting the kind of intelligent patriotism—especially among younger Americans—that is essential to preserving citizenship and free government.

This sponsored message from Inside Scoop Politics is on behalf of Hillsdale College | | | | | Dear Fellow American, Are you proud to be an American citizen? If you’re like me, you give thanks to God every day that you live in a country that is free, peaceful, and where citizens have inalienable rights. Most people in history can’t say the same thing—in fact, most people in the world can’t say the same thing even today. You don’t have to be a historian to see that the long practice of citizenship in America is unprecedented. It’s one of our nation’s great achievements. But there’s a catch—citizenship requires vigilance and knowledge to maintain. Especially now, when it faces threats from the far-Left and progressive economic policies, illegal immigration, and more. Everyone who wishes to defend freedom in America requires an understanding of the nature and scope of these challenges. As a college, we know that a proper education is the best defense of liberty. And unlike the vast majority of colleges and universities, we must reach and teach millions of Americans about liberty. And we have to do it without taking ONE PENNY of government funding—not even indirectly in the form of student grants and loans. NOT. ONE. PENNY—to remain proudly independent. This means that your support is critical to our success. With your help, we’ll engage the far-Left on the battlefield of education. With your help, we will defend liberty against dangerous ideologies. And with your help, we will preserve freedom for future generations of American citizens. You can give safely and securely at this link: And for a gift of $100 or more, you’ll receive a special hardcover edition of Victor Davis Hanson’s book, The Dying Citizen: How Progressive Elites, Tribalism, and Globalization Are Destroying the Idea of America. Victor Davis Hanson is a frequent commentator on Fox News and online. He’s also a historian and distinguished fellow here at Hillsdale. Regarding the book, my boss and teacher, Hillsdale President Larry P. Arnn, has written, “In this book, Hanson demonstrates yet again his command across time and for our time. This book and he are a treasure. ” Thank you so much for your partnership in promoting the kind of intelligent patriotism—especially among younger Americans—that is essential to preserving citizenship and free government. | | Warm regards, Bill Gray, ’01 Vice President National Donor Outreach Hillsdale College Pop Acta Media | Inside Scoop Politics PO Box 2221 Fort Collins, CO 80522 | _

There is still real work ahead of us! I will be working hard to help my colleagues across the state who are facing re-elections, I will be helping amazing candidates from Memphis to Johnson City running to be elected as we strive to make sure Tennessee gains the best representation.

But something is brewing where MAGA and the media least expects it.
This November, Nebraska is home to two races that could decide control of the U.S. House AND Senate. Denise Powell's fight to flip Nebraska's 2nd Congressional District, which could tip the balance of the U.S. House, and Dan Osborn's challenge to Pete Ricketts, which could break MAGA's grip on the U.S. Senate.

A man named Dennis Kirk who helped author Project 2025 has been selected by Trump to be Inspector General for the Interior Department.
Normally this might be a minor post that would not make headlines, but Kirk has been charged by Trump with reversing the conclusion that the Reflecting Pool renovation disaster was caused by incompetence, instead of vandalism as Trump baselessly insists.
Kirk was an adviser to former Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard, who infamously oversaw the raid on the election office in Fulton County, Georgia where official paper ballots cast in the 2020 election were seized.
Kirk is also a staff member at the Heritage Foundation -- the far right think tank that delivered Project 2025, the authoritarian playbook that Trump has been working off of since he took office in January 2025.
As a co-author of Project 2025, Kirk helped draw up the very blueprint that Trump relies on to focus his attacks on courts and systematically weaken the power and independence of the judiciary.

body:
| Polling places in your community need YOU this election. _You’re getting this message from[ _Power the Polls_](https://act.powerthepolls.org/go/4508?t=1&akid=9120%2E934366%2EH3TRLA) because you signed up to learn about serving as a poll worker. If you no longer wish to hear from us, [_please unsubscribe here_](https://act.powerthepolls.org/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?akid=9120.934366.H3TRLA&t=2&akid=9120%2E934366%2EH3TRLA). Marking emails as spam can affect our ability to reach others with important information. _
# [](https://act.powerthepolls.org/go/42?t=3&akid=9120%2E934366%2EH3TRLA)
Hey Peter— Today is National Poll Worker Recruitment Day. **We set a goal of 10,000 applications this week** – we’ve made a dent, but we’re still short. There’s plenty of time to make it up and right now thousands of people across the country are signing up on the same day to make sure every polling place is staffed this November. [Get in on the action and sign up now](https://act.powerthepolls.org/go/4927?t=4&akid=9120%2E934366%2EH3TRLA) If you've been meaning to finish your application, there's no better time than right now. Know someone who'd make a great poll worker? [Make sure you forward this to them.](https://act.powerthepolls.org/go/4928?t=5&akid=9120%2E934366%2EH3TRLA)**After you sign up, spread the news!** [](https://act.powerthepolls.org/go/446?t=6&akid=9120%2E934366%2EH3TRLA) If you'd rather post it straight to your [Instagram](https://act.powerthepolls.org/go/4929?t=7&akid=9120%2E934366%2EH3TRLA) or [Facebook](https://act.powerthepolls.org/go/4930?t=8&akid=9120%2E934366%2EH3TRLA), go ahead! Don’t forget to tag us so we can share it too. Thank you for stepping up. Democracy needs people like you. —The Power the Polls Team One more thing: Since your application goes straight to your local elections office, we don't always know if you've finished, started training, or decided the timing isn't right. **[Take two minutes to update us on your application status so we can send you the more useful information.](https://act.powerthepolls.org/survey/2026_poll_worker_status_survey/?t=9&akid=9120%2E934366%2EH3TRLA)**
---

There’s plenty of time to make it up and right now thousands of people across the country are signing up on the same day to make sure every polling place is staffed this November. If you've been meaning to finish your application, there's no better time than right now. Know someone who'd make a great poll worker? you sign up, spread the news! If you'd rather post it straight to your or , go ahead! Don’t forget to tag us so we can share it too. Thank you for stepping up. Democracy needs people like you. —The Power the Polls Team One more thing: Since your application goes straight to your local elections office, we don't always know if you've finished, started training, or decided the timing isn't right. *
