# Kitchen Table Tuesday
---
| | **Educating and connecting** with voters on important issues.
---
| | |
---
| | Our communities are currently facing significant challenges, as illegal immigration is cited as **draining local resources and allowing criminals to infiltrate local communities.** We must address this pressing reality to safeguard our district and our local economy. By protecting the integrity of the national immigration system, we can ensure that legal immigration remains a beneficial economic tool.
.To effectively address the issue of Border Security & Illegal Immigration, we need decisive action in Congress. My goal is to **enforce laws on the southern border, continue wall construction, and support the work of our federal agencies.** Taking these necessary steps will help us restore order, prioritize the needs of our residents, and build a safer, more secure future for our state.
---
| |
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | |
## The Conforti Brief
---
| | **Informing voters** on current events and how Niki plans to help them once in office.
---
| | Protecting the Ballot Box from Democrat Failures.
Recently, news reports out of New Jersey highlighted a staggering breakdown in election integrity. Governor Mikie Sherrill disclosed that a software error at the state's Motor Vehicle Commission led to the **improper voter registration of approximately 6,600 noncitizens between June 2023 and June 2024.** Even more alarming, roughly 400 of these noncitizens went on to cast ballots in recent elections.
.This is exactly the type of failure that occurs when our leaders refuse to take election security seriously. Unfortunately, **Democrats like Sean Casten have completely failed to secure our elections** , prioritizing partisan games and personal standing over common-sense security measures. While Casten and his allies continue to block safeguards that protect the integrity of your ballot, Niki Conforti will use her position in the U.S. House of Representatives to protect the ballot box for Illinoisans.
.Niki believes that in our everyday lives, we need a photo ID to buy cough syrup and to get on an airplane—we should also need a photo ID to vote. Her goal is to push for federal legislation that **implements the need for three forms of ID to register to vote** , alongside a strict requirement for a photo ID at the polling booth.
.By implementing these basic, common-sense measures nationally, the impact will be clear and immediate: it **ensures that only eligible voters are participating in the democratic process.** We must secure our federal elections, so they remain fair and truly representative of our hardworking citizens. Niki will confidently fight for these essential federal reforms in Washington to restore faith in our system and guarantee that every legal vote in Illinois is protected.
.
Stay informed on this issue—[**read the full breakdown here.**](https://us.list-manage.com/VZ4Bqe83kRl?e=25f4fa3311&c2id=7b058fb5598c3e136d157ed790328086)

High energy costs are identified as a primary driver of the current high cost-of-living in our district. As an energy consultant, Niki understands exactly why this is happening and how to fix it.

**Today is the day.**
Today, Tuesday, August 11, is the Republican Primary, and I respectfully ask for your vote.
I am proud to be the **Republican Party Endorsed Candidate for Congress in Connecticut 's Fourth Congressional District.**
This campaign is about the issues affecting you and your family every day:
**AFFORDABILITY. ENERGY. HEALTHCARE. OPPORTUNITY.**
The cost of living is too high. Energy costs are too high. Healthcare is too expensive and too complicated. And too many families are wondering whether their children and grandchildren will have the same opportunities that previous generations had.
**This election is about you. Your future. And the next generation.**
It is also about advancing **federal solutions to the local problems** we see every day -- from healthcare and energy costs to infrastructure, economic development, workforce opportunities and protecting the quality of life in our communities.
I haven't waited to be elected to start working.
I have been advocating, taking action and going to Washington to make Connecticut's voice heard **before I even hold the office.**
**Imagine what I can do when you send me to Congress.**
And as those of you who know me already know:
## I'M A FIGHTER.
I fight for my patients. I fight for my family. And I will fight for the people of Connecticut.
But today, **I need you to fight with me.**
Get to the polls.
Cast your vote.
Then call a friend, a neighbor or a family member and tell them to vote too.
An August primary is decided by the people who show up. **Every vote matters -- including yours.**
We can complain about the cost of groceries, electricity, healthcare and the direction of our country.
Or we can do something about it.
**Today is our opportunity to do something.**
* _**Let 's fight for affordability.**_
* _**Let 's fight for affordable and reliable energy.**_
* _**Let 's fight for better healthcare.**_
* _**Let 's fight for opportunity.**_
* _**And let 's fight to make sure the next generation has an even better future.**_

## DON'T JUST COMPLAIN. VOTE.
## FIGHT WITH ME.
## PUT A DOCTOR IN THE HOUSE.
# VOTE GOLDSTEIN TODAY.
**Dr. Michael Goldstein**

MICHAEL GOLDSTEIN FOR CONGRESS | | | Aug 11 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Today is the day. Today, Tuesday, August 11, is the Republican Primary, and I respectfully ask for your vote. I am proud to be the Republican Party Endorsed Candidate for Congress in Connecticut 's Fourth Congressional District. Healthcare is too expensive and too complicated. And too many families are wondering whether their children and grandchildren will have the same opportunities that previous generations had. This election is about you. Your future. And the next generation. It is also about advancing federal solutions to the local problems we see every day -- from healthcare and energy costs to infrastructure, economic development, workforce opportunities and protecting the quality of life in our communities. I haven't waited to be elected to start working. I have been advocating, taking action and going to Washington to make Connecticut's voice heard before I even hold the office. Imagine what I can do when you send me to Congress. And as those of you who know me already know: I'M A FIGHTER. I fight for my patients. I fight for my family. And I will fight for the people of Connecticut. But today, I need you to fight with me. Get to the polls. Cast your vote. Then call a friend, a neighbor or a family member and tell them to vote too. An August primary is decided by the people who show up. Every vote matters -- including yours. We can complain about the cost of groceries, electricity, healthcare and the direction of our country. Or we can do something about it. Today is our opportunity to do something. Let 's fight for affordability. Let 's fight for affordable and reliable energy. Let 's fight for better healthcare. Let 's fight for opportunity. And let 's fight to make sure the next generation has an even better future. DON'T JUST COMPLAIN. VOTE. FIGHT WITH ME. PUT A DOCTOR IN THE HOUSE. VOTE GOLDSTEIN TODAY. Peter Willis,

AIPAC has a new target: Aisha Wahab. And this special election ONE WEEK
FROM TODAY isn’t on most people’s radar, so they’re hoping they can
quietly buy this race and keep another bold progressive out of Congress.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39460?source=email-20260811&t=1112&akid=11179%2E5885482%2EMIXQge ]Headline: Aisha Wahab: AIPAC’s latest target

For months, Aisha Wahab was the clear favorite to fill Eric Swalwell’s old
seat. But then Super PACs started dumping over $5 million into the
district, trying to buy the seat for their hand-picked establishment
candidate. AIPAC has spent $1.2 million alone, most of it attacking Aisha.

They’re trying to flood the race in the final days to stop our progressive
momentum. Fewer than 10% of voters have already cast ballots in this
special election, so Our Revolution is stepping up in a big way.

We’re on the ground knocking doors with Aisha (Pramila Jayapal joined us
this weekend!) and printing out mailers to let folks know voting is
happening for this special election! And we’re making 128,000 calls,

mailboxes, we need a powerful final push to reach key voters in these
final 7 days.

name: Elizabeth Warren via The Democratic National Committee
subject: A big announcement from me:
body:
---
| [](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-warren-split?amount=20&refcode=em_20260811_8529_fr&refcode2=8529_22930333_8PnLiu&akid=8529%2E22930333%2E8PnLiu)
---
Derek, did you know we don’t have to wait until 2028 to stop Trump?
That’s right. There are three big ways we can put a strong check on his administration. Here's my plan:
1. If Democrats win back our majorities in November, we will be able to stop these spineless Republicans from enabling the president to do whatever he wants.
2. Once we have that power, we can block any far-right, extremist judge that Trump nominates to the Supreme Court.
3. And we can use our power in Congress to make Trump and his cronies follow the law, protect the programs they’ve attacked, and pass plans to make our government actually work for working people.

This is our chance to actually put a stop to Trump as soon as possible — and I’m not taking this chance for granted.
**So I have an announcement to share: Our campaign has now contributed over $1 million to support state parties in 2026. Because this is how we ensure Democrats win.**

| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | VOTE TOMORROW
---
| |
Tomorrow is the special primary election, and everything we are hearing points to an extremely low voter turnout. That means every single vote cast tomorrow will carry even more weight than usual, and your voice could have an amplified impact on the outcome of this race. This is the moment to show up, make your voice heard, and help choose a representative who will truly fight for “We the People.”

Make a plan to vote tomorrow, remind your family and friends that there is an election happening, and encourage everyone you know in the district to get to the polls. In an election like this, every vote truly matters.

Save the sample ballot to your phone, then take a few minutes to go through your contacts and text it to every friend and family member you know in Alabama’s 1st Congressional District.

Remind them that the special primary election is tomorrow and encourage them to make a plan to vote. In a low-turnout election, one simple text could be the reminder that gets someone to the polls.
---

| |
---

# About Austin Sidwell
---
| |
Austin Sidwell is a husband, father, Air Force veteran, small business leader, and conservative Republican from Alabama’s Gulf Coast. A former rescue helicopter pilot and instructor, Austin now serves as Vice President of Sidwell Protection Services and is running for Congress to bring practical leadership, fiscal discipline, and a new generation of conservative service to Washington.

| | | | | | | | | | | | **Sidwell for Congress**

**Join the Movement.****Stand Up for Alabama.** Alabama’s First Congressional District is rooted in faith, family, and country, a legacy of conservative leadership that has stood firm when it mattered most. With new lines stretching from Mobile Bay to Dothan and the Wiregrass, that calling is more important than ever. Washington is full of talkers and career politicians who’ve forgotten which side they’re on. The people of South Alabama deserve someone who will fight every single day to protect our values and put America First.

They’re absolutely right, team. If it wasn't for the Electoral College, Trump NEVER would have been president in the first place!

## Colombia Quake Kills More Than 100
A magnitude 7.4 earthquake [struck western Colombia](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDFupjAUhE8DnRE2xuDCxTZ0_7Zbood5wNsYm9gGlNtHRIpygLQzmtF88-81voAc-fUv7GjyEkaPd3KYM8bRBhf2iQAh5u39hDe0GyTy6yhqoVjdM85HsJkuHCWUs1kQBTYlGt71SraN0n25mUn2i2qtmpq2EXbWduq46CS0Wli0WpRknr6655w3dc9VpTRXEifFpUIFWhSyxplyiNX_QD5vuLiPcGGsbNhLZ7acj1Q0fwoxFGK477vyk304Hv9RQnRzIQYHmTyDHSNZKMSQcgx-ZT947JuYoT1hDpEdGA6HDC-w55Ne2RZ2TGw6yc3k18Si9dBq3tW6jGY-bnKOkuoKWa87kPuamH_57GXEZwAAAP__SvCQzQ) on Monday, killing at least 111 people, injuring nearly 90, and collapsing 61 buildings across cities in the country's coffee-growing heartland. Cameras caught buildings swaying and crumbling as the quake rolled through early in the morning. [See the moment it struck here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOnzAMxp8mbKDEyYUwZOiS7bp2RAYM-BrIvySA7u0rTqr6ALdZluXv-_1-vffvyJH35Sdu5Muc-p3uHKkUOvoxxbQNjIRHWf-c-JvGFTPvSw8SbC1drVSPY-GLeoPV5GciIF2RV62z5k3bzlWrV0MHup2NcwQWpX3THc5mnrRG4wy1Ffvnn3RKKS2dso3tlDU0WGUsWexAGEkTl3Q0H4n3stIcP9NFRzOmrYp-LeWVhf4hIAgI9303Z8aSJvx8DgSEiydKWUB44ASEJ05AkE5AUFJA-E9YjylGfGXK9XBynHhfcj3i-Sx4_zgP_hrqf24EhE6BUa1UUrYCQnX46XVzjJxtK4xcNuT4VbR80-_l4W8AAAD__4Jmjc8). In Cali, Colombia's third-largest city, rescue crews searched for about 15 people trapped under one of the 20 collapsed buildings, and at least six airports suspended flights due to structural damage. President Abelardo de la Espriella [declared a national disaster](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0M_K2zAQBPCnkW8O-uPI8kGHQjH08PXao1nJK3tbWUqtTULevqRQ-gDfeWCY3_z4WD6AMpXtOxzoOdWl4LNlZMZziTXXIxAgnLz_vsMvjDs0Ktuipba9dL1SC0SmBy4DdKtPiBpNh16Nzg5XYyfX7R6CniYZXBpBB2msCWtMMdkgR-MwYUf-3SedUspIp-zFTsoOGKwaLFqYtBgkrsT1vPysVHjHlF_1gecl1qPLfme-NWG-CD0LPUOIb8M7E3r-VhjPAky1QBZ6_mfq_6P6BAyZmLD14U55pbK1Ptac4dZwFXpuXM-XMDOtwnxV5npVzk1jd_r19qScqdlRDHI7gPLfSfzJJx9e_wkAAP__mmCKJA) and rushed to the hardest-hit region, while the Trump administration said it stands ready to help with recovery.
## White House Closing Food Additive Loophole
The Trump administration [moved Monday](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2u4yAUxfHV4A4LrjEhBcU07jLtlNYNvjZM-MgAiTW7f8rbwquP9NPR_89tvWGIIR-_MZHte1kznS1S71RXV2JJ94CEtft_L3yQ89hCPlYQoLkwXMoVXQ9vWhUOm92JgKaBrLwYreZJX83g7aTxMusNFc3azMIZAOUETqRAKTeLIdiPJ4yUchJG6lFfpVZ011Jp0ngFpgRtoZc6_i0hd097_F_eVEdX0hCt7_3Z2PSLwcJgOc9zdPnuPiOD5UMzWIRhsEjBYPG-8YQPahxzLq_sKFHujZfMj4qNv2Kv-KzFUWu08b2UbfQ9xaHa7XmGGEPTF6bEkTDE7wf9h-HeFr4CAAD__wAtgeM) to close a 68-year-old loophole that lets food companies add new ingredients without telling the FDA, while rolling out the government's first-ever definition of "ultra-processed food." Since 1958, manufacturers have been free to decide for themselves that an additive is "[generally recognized as safe](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFyhSAQgOHTaIcjaEALijR2L21KZ4VVSNA1LE8nt88kV8gF_n_me3_MD4gpHtsb7GjLSvOBNycsBfPsKNG-REDIJXw94RNdAI7HNqtWadEOQsoZXIkXzj3U3q6ICrsarTSD7l86PQ51sBrGsTPKDCOi84vXvh-lMetinDFdi3W0v712kFJ27SB1o0epe1y07DVqGFXVt-hjodx8UDxKwDV904W5cbTXyYZSTq6610pNlZru-25C4Gajq1LTmZFZZKK9UlMILOA46Hk4ZPFMJYM4MzlkRi9WIs9iy8Ai40p55yaUPdXZ-vOOKUXWpurbbYeY_s7ln2CXVT8BAAD__2VQgnE)" and ship it. The proposal would make FDA notification mandatory, with a public inventory of every submission. _"Nearly 60% of the American diet is made up of ultra-processed foods, and childhood obesity now affects more than one in five American children,"_ said Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. Under the proposal, the FDA would get [180 days](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFuhTAQBNDTmM4IL_7GFC7S0P20KdGCF9jEYGIc0L99RK6Q_mlGMx_P_okceJvfcSWXp9hvdB2BcqbUjzHEdWAkTHn5_sEvGhc8eJt7qMDIykqlehwzn9RrLLybiIDqgpxqrNGP2rS2WJy2djBgW8KK0GpoB-UbbR9ta0yDairY3XmVVUrVlVWmNK0ymgajtCGDLQhdkeccU_kZecsLTeEVT0rlGNciuCXn_RD1m4BOQHddVznF6D2fdAMB3b1JQDd5lHPCQ4YY9yUGkreTeww8viRvcyLPtOVDrriggM5Co7US0BXJ-f3iEPgwjdDVvCKHv_b8z9NOB78BAAD__-bbgPY) to rule on new submissions, and companies already selling self-approved additives would have to turn over their data.
## Fastest Man on Wheels Chases New Record
Andy Green, the retired British fighter pilot who became the only driver ever to break the sound barrier, returns to Utah's Bonneville Salt Flats this morning chasing a [new land speed record](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAQRL8GMo9sA8YEDi4hm0vupA1RYzfgHYPZpofR_P2K_YXNSiqpVO993Ic7xBS3-S-s6HjKw4avIyEz0uBzyusYAYF4-XrCA_0CR9zmQUtthLRCqQE8xxOHGsrgJkSNVYlOtdbUTWU6Wy6utZMdva_AmNAq71FVrW0bOU2T9SbUZXTXnrRKqUpaZW6mU6bG0ajaoIFOF7XEEDnT7TPHjRec0jufSDef1zK5hXk_iupPoftC9zD6i-HqCt3_R79sOeX5Xej-FQn_caYrB4onkhgpP1Ac-bkFMQJRRBLAjOvOh0iwBXHsiEEQ-kxBqKppZGdNW5IL-yumFA_TFrWcV4jp5w__UuPp9HcAAAD__7aqiR8) in a hydrogen-powered car. The 32-foot, bright yellow [JCB Hydromax](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDuyozAURFcDmSj9RohAwSRknnRC6iJdI9n6MEI2492_4m3hpd1VXX3O39tygxBD3v5AQtPuZcl4HhFbw7rYEktaAyDU5v-94InWwxHytnDKFaGaMLaAbeGNi4TemTsiR9GjYaNW8pdQk-69WQFRwjrhxJymkmlGRwVghdZq5JL3wVx7VDPGBNVMDWpiSuKqmFSoYOKdpOhCK3V4lJCbx3v8lDfWwZbUR-Nb249O_O743PH5PM8hZIc7Zoe5DbYMr2fH5wvsqkuNruMzJKzBwhVBdh-yVcRMjh3RkYq2VEdeDTx52JX4j6slwX-yCiqoHKfBtxT7atx-hhjDocZO0i1BiN-X2g9Nvg3_CgAA__9RyIkb) packs two hydrogen combustion engines with 1,600 horsepower. Green, 64, hit 368 mph in practice last week, already faster than his own 20-year-old diesel record. British equipment giant JCB has poured more than $134 million into hydrogen engines that it hopes to showcase during the run. Any records must be certified by racing's world governing body.

Since 1958, manufacturers have been free to decide for themselves that an additive is "" and ship it. The proposal would make FDA notification mandatory, with a public inventory of every submission. "Nearly 60% of the American diet is made up of ultra-processed foods, and childhood obesity now affects more than one in five American children," said Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. Under the proposal, the FDA would get to rule on new submissions, and companies already selling self-approved additives would have to turn over their data. You’re getting $0. | | | | | == Peter, Working people like me and my neighbors paid the price for Trump's tariffs. Now corporations are getting billions in tariff refunds. Not one dollar is being returned to us. Walmart's refund: $2.4B Apple's refund: $2.2B Ford's refund: $1.3B Amazon's refund: $600M refund Your refund: $0 | == | Trump's tariffs ended up being another wealth transfer from working Americans to billion-dollar corporations. And my opponent, Mike Johnson, defended them, claiming they benefited the economy. Wrong. Johnson and Trump took your hard-earned money and gave it to mega-corporations. Mike Johnson stood by as Trump's tariffs stole from us and now he's standing by as billion-dollar corporations steal from us too. Every single day since the tariffs began, Mike Johnson has defended them, blocked opposition, and refused to interfere on behalf of the Americans trying to get by while prices rose on basic necessities. While we struggled with skyrocketing prices on everything from our groceries to even getting a new iPhone, Mike Johnson just stood by and shrugged. Mike Johnson and Trump are saying the quiet part out loud: These illegal tariffs were always about making them and their friends money. We paid and then we were played. I'm Conrad Cable, the Democrat running to stop this. Mike Johnson will never stop defending Trump and his billionaire friends, while we pay the price. It's time for us to kick him out of Congress for good this November. Mike Johnson has let billion-dollar corporations take our hard-earned money one too many times. | | **Brent Surged to $88, Its Highest Since July 31, One Day Before the CPI. Trump Says the US Is ‘Only Semi-Negotiating.’ Here Is What the Rebound Means for Your Portfolio.**
---
| | The oil market delivered its sharpest move in weeks as the US-Iran deadlock hardened. Brent crude climbed to $88 a barrel on Tuesday, its highest since July 31, while WTI reached $82.45 — both extending a four-session rebound. **Brent settled at $87.72 Monday after a 5% jump; Tuesday’s move extended the surge just one day before Wednesday’s July CPI.** The rebound has retraced nearly the entire 7% weekly decline of the prior week, driven by fading hopes for a quick Hormuz reopening and Trump’s signal that Washington is “only semi-negotiating” with Tehran.
---
| | For your portfolio, the catalyst was a strategic pivot. Trump told Axios the US is “only semi-negotiating” and would rely on the naval blockade to pressure Tehran rather than airstrikes — “watching Iran with its huge inflation.” **A blockade-based pressure campaign implies a longer timeline to reopening, not a shorter one, which is why oil rallied.** For the American investor at or near retirement, the timing is what matters: Brent at $88 lands the day before the July CPI, Wednesday at 8:30 a.m. ET. While the CPI measures July’s average prices — mostly locked in before this spike — the $88 print resets the forward inflation narrative just as the data arrives. A print at or above expectations, alongside two-week-high oil, would revive rate-hike odds even after the weak jobs data. Stay balanced-to-defensive on rate-sensitive holdings into the number.

Friend, when President Trump endorsed me, he didn't just give me his stamp of approval; I looked him in the eye and made a promise: I will be his biggest, fiercest ally in the Senate. But in order to keep that promise and finish the America First Agenda, we have to win this Senate seat in November. ****************************************************************************************************** **************************************************************************************************** President Trump cannot do this alone. He needs a Senate full of unapologetic patriots who are ready to continue the fight for the America First agenda; That's why I'm turning to you today, Friend. If you want to defeat Chuck Schumer, save our Senate Majority, and back President Trump, **************************************************************************************************** **************************************************************************************************** **************************************************************************************************** ****************************************************************************************************** Thank you for standing with me, President Trump, and our shared values. name: Mark Ronchetti
subject: Bernie denies it. Brazile excuses it. Michigan elected it.
body:
Plus: New Mexico just made the bar exam optional | New episode for dpwillis67@gmail.com

| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/lvKyAlnJ33R?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | | | | |
Bernie Sanders just said he doesn't know a single serious candidate who wants to defund the police, abolish prisons, or open the borders.
EXCEPT....the woman who could be Wisconsin's Democratic nominee for governor by Tuesday night has publicly called for all three. [This is the civil war inside the Democratic Party](https://us.list-manage.com/GrikoygCBwZ?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e). Bernie denies it's happening, Donna Brazile says it's no big deal, and Michigan just nominated the guy who proves them both wrong.
Meanwhile, New Mexico just decided that passing the bar exam is optional if you want to practice law here. What could possibly go wrong?!
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/P_CgjKG7eDd?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| |
🔥 **BERNIE SAYS THESE PEOPLE DON'T EXIST. WE PULLED UP HER POSTS.
** He said it on Pod Save America, and then blamed Fox News for making it sound worse than it is. Francesca Hong's first post is about white supremacy. The second one calls defunding a first step toward abolishing. The third has nothing to do with police, and it's the one you'll be forwarding to people.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/U_sIcpXySae?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| |
🚨 **DONNA BRAZILE SAID THIS IS JUST LIKE THE TEA PARTY**
She said it Sunday morning on ABC. Same growing pains Republicans had in 2010, nothing to see here. Scott Jennings was sitting right there and read her the actual list of what these people want to abolish. Police. ICE. Borders. The Senate. The Constitution.
Then he brought up the Democratic attorney general in Michigan who says she can't safely attend her own party's convention. Mark ran in a Tea Party cycle. He has some thoughts about that comparison.

📉 **MEDIA RAN THE 23,000 JOBS NUMBER ALL WEEKEND**
Every broadcast led with it. The economy lost 23,000 jobs in July. Here's what nobody mentioned. Private payrolls went up last month. Government payrolls went down by more than that.
Krysty pulls the whole thing apart, then makes a point that has nothing to do with July. It's about the four years before it. Kevin Hassett went on CNN and explained that part of it was snow. In July.

⚖️ **675 HOURS AND YOU'RE A LAWYER IN NEW MEXICO**
That's it. Twelve months following an attorney around, and you never take the bar. You will also never know which one your lawyer did. Krysty asked whether we're doing this with doctors next.

PLUS: Democratic registration in this state hit a number Vince Torres hasn't seen in his lifetime, Gabe Vasquez put the police union's logo on a mailer you paid for, and the tax secretary who called your paycheck a wealth transfer.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. | | Whether your family is soaking up the final weeks of summer break or already settling into a new school routine, history is always better when it comes to life. Before the backpacks are fully packed and the school year gets busy, take time to create meaningful memories with your kids by exploring places that celebrate America's story. From rockets and space exploration to presidential homes, historic landmarks, and hidden treasures across the country, these patriotic destinations offer unforgettable opportunities to learn together. In our latest blog, discover 8 family-friendly destinations where history, adventure, and inspiration come together, including:
* Space exploration landmarks
* Mount Rushmore
* Abraham Lincoln's home
* George Washington Carver's legacy
* Harriet Beecher Stowe's story
* Underground Railroad history and more

You don’t have to travel across the country to discover America’s story. Read the [full blog](https://momsforamerica.us/so/b0P-muyOz/c?w=2etn69GH3OXi1USSMYW8iPh4Ecz6ldGckkCDl5ZQX9Y.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubW9tc2ZvcmFtZXJpY2EudXMvYmxvZyIsInIiOiIwZDY3YmJhZS0wZDI3LTQ2ZDMtOTYyMy01NjU3OTczYzljYjgiLCJtIjoibWFpbCIsImMiOiJiMzgzOGJmOC1mYWIwLTQxYjktOTY3My1lOGM2YmVmYjY1NzcifQ) to discover even more amazing places in every state, many of them just a short drive away. Give your children the gift of hands-on history and make memories that last long after summer ends.

| | John Strand: Prison Couldn't Silence Him
---
| | [](https://momsforamerica.us/so/b0P-muyOz/c?w=8vD376IEjGjTf3oHTquGIwNCAJ16APka0Aangr17Xhg.)

| | Thomas Jefferson is often credited with saying, "All tyranny needs to gain a foothold is for people of good conscience to remain silent." Whether that quote captures today's moment is a matter of perspective, but for John Strand, remaining silent was never an option. Two years after Strand was literally swept into the U.S. Capitol by the crush of people on January 6, he left his life of liberty for the darkness of captivity in a federal prison. In this episode, he recounts his arrest, conviction, imprisonment, eventual exoneration, and the experiences that inspired his latest book, Patriot Plea: The J6 Journey of a Political Prisoner in the Divided States of America. Strand also discusses how those events shaped his views on the American justice system, why he believes his conviction was unjust, and what motivated him to seek public office as he now runs for Congress. Whether you're familiar with the January 6 cases or simply interested in hearing one individual's account of this highly debated chapter in American history, this conversation explores themes of conviction, resilience, faith, civil liberties, and civic engagement through the lens of Strand's personal journey. body:
I need to be transparent with you about what we’re up against.
Peter, it’s Chris.
I wish I didn’t have to write this email, but I need to be transparent with you about what we’re up against:
_Right now we’re being outspent 2:1._
**For every dollar our campaign is putting into reaching voters, Republicans and their outside groups are spending _twice as much_ to flood New Hampshire’s airwaves with attack ads.**
National GOP groups are pouring millions into the Granite State because they know what happens here could decide control of the Senate.
Their strategy is simple: spend as much as they can, as fast as they can, and try to drown out our message to voters.
But Granite Staters don’t let outside groups decide their elections. They want to hear directly from candidates. They want to know who will fight to lower costs, protect reproductive freedom, and deliver results for their families.
**That’s why we need to make sure our campaign message can break through, Peter.**
Our campaign is powered by grassroots supporters – people who believe New Hampshire deserves a senator who answers to them, not Washington insiders or special interests.
But when the other side has a 2-to-1 spending advantage, we need your help to keep pace.

| | Dear Fellow American, Are you proud to be an American citizen? If you're like me, you give thanks to God every day that you live in a country that is free, peaceful, and where citizens have inalienable rights. Most people in history can't say the same thing--in fact, most people in the world can't say the same thing even today. You don't have to be a historian to see that the long practice of citizenship in America is unprecedented. It's one of our nation's great achievements. But there's a catch--citizenship requires vigilance and knowledge to maintain. Especially now, when it faces threats from the far-Left and progressive economic policies, illegal immigration, and more. Everyone who wishes to defend freedom in America requires an understanding of the nature and scope of these challenges. As a college, we know that a proper education is the best defense of liberty. And unlike the vast majority of colleges and universities, we must **reach** and **teach** millions of Americans about liberty. And we have to do it without taking ONE PENNY of government funding--not even indirectly in the form of student grants and loans. NOT. ONE. PENNY--to remain proudly independent. This means that your support is critical to our success. With your help, we'll engage the far-Left on the battlefield of education. With your help, we will defend liberty against dangerous ideologies. And with your help, we will preserve freedom for future generations of American citizens. You can give safely and securely at this link: [https://secured.hillsdale.edu/hillsdale/dying-citizen](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/s/c/8pPArde3aDXx2-szsltrtqxSrC90v8CdTVsthNw6nvTccfGfeT8kj9BVEIA1OwKzq3Sr5Llva2MIXlqzurSfrAG_pQoEl7VWcr2E1Nll_LN17-JVVE5-g4qpSqw6GclEH5N5-isj1FoMRCADeGynl6GMnAhxvjjmDAGrvWbhtGj5K_uZ1sxK9FEV_a5N0eHCsZpo4QkV_x-Tm_Oq1KMM7x75HJx0u-iqgnY504ygAjyaVLYUiyv5gPgEtWvL7QMV9KQN-g75owGqt-jYzOrwwvuEBFC4xLOYo7WaUjPwOjLiRbdV2vkhygvQvZvKm6y2UrGAsPjifC7w92M68QLUQ1-j3rVKtwuCh9t6baoox09WGgqc8rV-jVsQ0HUxeV4TtpTF8IFcdIGAGsKaP702FdsSutAFcb2036AQ27lnXShg1x68IUWxhACQ2ut5q9OZIjUmxSDDzwkTSctzrXDKimniLwCnnS5VLCJb85VyZ8y79YBryYbhBfFXN7EI4jhrReqsKFpJYkKGQnVRasx2d9q6wrQNEythf1oQ6H94Uwy8iCI7155Guo3cBv5s-SuJLmJ4gK5_2VnJReMjkDzADVXzS6rLPmpl3KX1U6i06nQ0mY1Vbiwm-fOg0_ZwbwKpHo-5rWJCD3ZmpJT8iSPk8mostI-XwVFxmUwSYPVUnrIL0yAPy63-E72GMec0UFIGfe7YssH2zRSP487MObfD752UUTGGm6FOzOnw/HiAbLEZdrWpyG5KCwqlLXkLzfyw49yVV/23) **And for a gift of $100 or more, you 'll receive a special hardcover edition of Victor Davis Hanson's book,** **_The Dying Citizen: How Progressive Elites, Tribalism, and Globalization Are Destroying the Idea of America_****. Victor Davis Hanson is a frequent commentator on Fox News and online. He 's also a historian and distinguished fellow here at Hillsdale.** Regarding the book, my boss and teacher, Hillsdale President Larry P. Arnn, has written, "In this book, Hanson demonstrates yet again his command across time and for our time. **This book and he are a treasure.** " Thank you so much for your partnership in promoting the kind of intelligent patriotism--especially among younger Americans--that is essential to preserving citizenship and free government.

| | Warm regards, Bill Gray, '01
Vice President
National Donor Outreach
Hillsdale College

# Harris County Elections are a theatrical production with negotiated outcomes and DOES NOT represent the TRUE and verifiable authentic vote.
## Examine the vote "heat map" from the 2024 election above...
**and let it soak in for a few minutes.** _So, what you are telling me is that the concentration of citizens in the epicenter of business and commerce_ _Fortune 500 publicly traded, indexed and audited company employees_ _Some of the best decision makers and money makers_ Located in the center of the 4th largest city in the USA are blissfully ignorant and consistently voting for Democrat Socialism? Because, that is exactly what they want you to believe is happening over and Over and OVER again. That's like hitting your thumb with a hammer, then raring back and striking it again...then, raring back and really letting it have it with a another smashing blow. When the Harris County District Attorneys NEVER invite the Statewide Elected Texas Attorney General Office in to investigate County Election Crimes for a decade, you might want to consider you've been played for a fool. **THREE:**

# Highest Priority: Sweeping Election Integrity Reform
---
My Fellow Texans,
I encourage you to consider that "Sweeping Election Integrity Reform" is our highest and most important priority. Consider Florida and the results once sweeping Election Integrity Reform was passed by their state legislators: ALL COUNTIES, less 2, flipped RED Here we sit in a Texas with 254 Counties whereby population concentrations in the big urban counties are extraordinarily swollen, many times with non-native Texas not reflecting our historical conservative values. Florida was facing the same level of infiltration corruption with miserable results. There are several key elements the business owners, top business executives and credentialed professionals of Texas ask for you to consider: 1) The Secretary of State that certifies the vote of each county MUST be elected by the people of Texas reporting only to the tax paying citizen voters like any other statewide elected official. 2) Election Fraud MUST be vigorously and zealously prosecuted by the State Attorney General's Office with Citizen Oversight in each County and the penalty must result in the banning of any convicted voting fraud from every possible benefit of being a citizen of Texas for life. Theft of vote is muzzling the voice and will of the people and a sentence of life in prison, hard labor and public notice of election fraudsters is our only reasonable choice in a civil society. All else is chaos. 3) The Secretary of State MUST keep a separate "check point" electronic and tokenized secure copy of each ballot cast whereby each voter sets the PIN code to verify his/her legal ballot is cast correctly in the SOS system. Each county may NOT certify an election that does not perfectly match that system. In this way, our individual votes will be kept private and our vote will be 3rd party validated instantly. 4) Mail in Ballot fraud at present has no audit trail and ballots are NOT tracked and traced when they are "re-voted" at the County Election Centers allowing for wholesale ballot manufacturing. This is the source of the Election Fraud Investigation opened by Texas State Attorney General Ken Paxton's office in March of 2026. No chain of custody from the US Postal Service exists for Texas Mail in Ballots. This mail in ballot situation must be standardized, auditable and a clear transparent system that submits entirely to item 3 above. 5) Voter rolls must be purged of voters MONTHLY that no longer meet the test of valid voters residing in the county at the address on file validated by the US Postal Registration Database. Harris County Texas alone has not cleansed its database of voters in years with over 600,000 illegal voters still on its rolls from which ballots are manufactured to throw elections as alleged by the people's lawsuit before Texas Supreme Court as we speak. County Officials that do NOT purge the voter database are NOT prosecuted and this much change at once. They must serve prison time for NOT securing our voter registration database. This must NOT be outsourced to foreign owned entities and must be done locally by the citizens of each county. 6) Open Primaries are a source of weakening our Republican Party Values as candidates are inserted into our elections not reflecting our RPT chosen agenda and crossover primary voting tragically disfigures our Primary Elections. At the same time, our primary elections in big blue counties are often entirely run by Democrat Election Centers. **This is insane.** We must control our brand and hold it entirely accountable to our RPT values elected by our members at Convention. NO election fraud can withstand such vigorous and strategic integrity measures. We encourage you to make election integrity job 1 so the people can believe in our elections.

Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

## It’s the best day of the week! Ten Dollar Tuesday!
---
| | | | |

We are back after a full week of campaigning. Last Thursday, over 600 concerned residents filled the auditorium in Mandan for a community gathering on Mandan’s proposed data center. Folks are fired up and agreeing with a lot of what Vern’s been saying.
Also, it’s another Ten Dollar Tuesday! Naturally, Vern is on the road. He’s got a press conference in Bismarck this morning (Tuesday, 10am at the Bismarck Veterans Memorial Public Library, Meeting Room B- public are invited!), several days in Fargo, and then the Sheyenne Stampede on Saturday.
With summer winding down and November drawing nearer, your donations make that much more of an impact.

[**Will you get Vern’s back by chipping in $10, $50, or whatever you can give for this week’s Ten Dollar Tuesday?**](https://us.list-manage.com/MCHgRaoJPEu?e=37dda778f5&c2id=cdbf6368064ed4acbe3dc3fec7c073dc)

Peter, When's the last time anyone looked at your previous tax returns and asked _whether you overpaid?_ Most **never **get that conversation. They get a tax preparer who files what happened last year and moves on to the next client. Nobody's looking ahead. Nobody's checking whether last year, or the year before, left money on the table. That's the gap **Rob Gill built Tru-Fit Tax & Planning** to close, and it's why Bill Spadea is joining him in person next Thursday, August 20th at the Molly Pitcher Inn for **Stop Overpaying the IRS** , a dinner reserved for business owners and high earners. **[Reserve Your Seat at NJTaxDinner.com](https://xtz223.keap-link020.com/v2/click/60de63122a7c5af7b9cf95f3d3796417/eJyNj0ELgkAQhf_LnCVJLcxbiIhoHqLOsbgDbem4bGNY4n9vrehU0HXe977hDcBIgjiTEEHPd8_zwQGDldIKieOWWFTP1FsEc3_uQK3onJq20xANX8sfYDqvll7gAN80WmS3Xcd5VqaHIitzS2ph7I-_PGEYhB9PsllnBYzjTzE2ipOrdV8gYtPhtEgqu4r3prb8kVlHrksnFr1URGhmVdvYotAaSb5X53h71ccHEfRfyQ==)**

body:
A bold vision, a debate, and 7 days until the primary.

| | | | |
---
| | Alaska Isn't the End of the Road. It's the Door to the Globe.
---
**Greetings, Fellow Alaskans and Friends: **
**Most maps show Alaska tucked in a corner. Rotate the globe and look from the top, and the picture changes completely. Alaska sits at the center of Arctic commerce, closer to Europe than the East Coast and home to the nearest North American port to Asia. This week, Hughes/Gettys unveiled a phased plan to make that geography work for Alaska: connecting the Alaska Railroad to Canada's network, extending rail to Nome, and building on the Port of Nome project already underway to position Alaska as the intercontinental transportation hub of the 21st century. This isn't a campaign vision statement; it's built on years of legislative groundwork, including the presidential border permit for the A2A rail project and the $175 million state appropriation that brought federal dollars to Nome.**** ****That same record-backed approach shows up across every issue. An A+ NRA rating. A Stand for Health Freedom endorsement rooted in a conviction that Alaskans should make their own health decisions, not government. And a KTUU interview that gets at why this campaign exists: because the work isn't finished and the people's choice is ready to finish it.**** ****August 18th is seven days away. If you haven't voted yet, early voting is open now. Scroll down for the full transportation hub plan, debate highlights from Soldotna, and everything else from a big week on the trail.** ** ****Ready to serve you,**
---
---
**Republican Candidate for Governor****of the Great State of Alaska**
---
**p.s. In the homestretch now - one week to go until the Primary Election on August 18, and we truly need every Alaskan for the Hughes/Gettys ticket to rally behind us big time! Vote early, vote on election day or send that absentee ballot in ASAP! Can we count on your vote?**
**Sign waving opportunities this week! Want to help with sign waving? We'd love to hear from you in whatever way you are able to support - reach out to us at **[**info@alaskansforhughes.com**](mailto:info@alaskansforhughes.com)** and let us know how you would like to join us or simply donate using the button below!**

**Alaska: Gateway to the Globe**
---
**Built on Prior Work, Hughes Governor Campaign Unveils Vision to Make Alaska the Intercontinental Transportation Hub: The Panama Canal of the 21st Century**
**The Hughes/Gettys plan lays out incremental steps to connect Alaska to the Lower 48, support US Arctic shipping traffic now dominated by Russia, lower costs for Alaskan families, open new markets for Alaskan products, unlock critical minerals and energy development, and strengthen national security in the Arctic.****Gubernatorial candidate Shelley Hughes and running mate Blake Gettys laid out a long-term vision to position Alaska as the central transportation and commerce hub connecting the United States to Europe and Asia through the Arctic, while outlining the concrete, near-term steps needed to get there.**
**“Far too long we have looked at the globe from the vantage point of North America with Alaska tucked up to the left. It’s time we rotate the globe and look from the top. Alaska isn’t an afterthought. We are the center of the top of the world and need to act like it,” Senator Shelley Hughes pointed out. “We must take our rightful place over the next few decades to become the global crossroads we’re positioned to be.”**
**To view the replay of the Facebook live of the Tuesday, August 4 event with the full presentation, **[**click here**](https://eot.alaskansforhughes.com/f/a/W7cA1aAsh4eYz4X7srbqzw~~/AAAHURA~/lcQxhjauvxw-18qegQYAjxUOaIzwdGKKJLN441vMKZHdyE5JmPTdkwjTXsNky9X5xPcpRDNjjjnBOGDD4Z01iP6FpYAIadjkK5miHem_E_Uju8gkca_5PiAVHaXjP3cfWOGlWZgSpcWSoSSqM5OlNVqbyndKiZjN7DN7lQCWHXvQsfw2Dr70Ga-gSqBgiCafvMZ_yJTKRfxxmnytbrzVkw~~)**.**
**To view the replay of the YouTube live of the Tuesday, August 4 event, watch the video below:**
---
[ ](https://eot.alaskansforhughes.com/f/a/iSPQ7Q1kgTNU_wm7S6f5Lg~~/AAAHURA~/32KlvQa0VILeSbqEvnTzy-TRrx-yAtOf4z8gTYWt8oWHnnWIjlDN-U6M4IDmINjNYr2UxhxWf5afiHLKu_apMgazqb8ah-b6hB3JPoNantjk6_ij8G5DzJkONTLgMA9wSYl8H92FD_JwcYjs8IV0e2Cdd-0g3YAt2qsDphZe0NY9MCzEZA3SPvChmDjIFn7l)
---
**Hughes emphasized that, with Arctic traffic increasing and Russia dominating 90% of it, Alaska must step up on behalf of the United States. “We are ready. The preliminary work is underway on our eastern and western borders, and it’s time to build on that.” The proposal is not a single massive undertaking, but a sequence of achievable projects, each building the case and the infrastructure for the next.**
**The plan presented was based on Hughes’s prior work in the House and Senate, including her hearings as House Transportation Chair on the opening of Arctic shipping lanes and the potential of the Port of Nome; her successful Senate resolution supporting the presidential border permit for the A2A (Alaska to Alberta) rail project; and, most recently, her work to broker the deal appropriating $175 million in state funds to draw down federal funding for the Port of Name.**
**Instead of Alaska being at the end of the road, Alaska will be the door to the globe. Alaska is as close to Europe as the East Coast is. Nome is the closest port to Asia in all of North America. **
**The first phase is under construction now: the Port of Nome. **
**The second phase connects the existing Alaska Railroad to Canada’s network, tying into a border crossing already backed by the presidential permit signed in 2021 and a right of way already approved on the Canadian side. **
**The third phase extends the existing Alaska Railroad from Nenana to Nome. **
**Alaska will become the far more convenient Panama Canal of the 21st century. **

clean_body: A bold vision, a debate, and 7 days until the primary. | | | | | | | Alaska Isn't the End of the Road. It's the Door to the Globe. Greetings, Fellow Alaskans and Friends: Most maps show Alaska tucked in a corner. Rotate the globe and look from the top, and the picture changes completely. Alaska sits at the center of Arctic commerce, closer to Europe than the East Coast and home to the nearest North American port to Asia. This week, Hughes/Gettys unveiled a phased plan to make that geography work for Alaska: connecting the Alaska Railroad to Canada's network, extending rail to Nome, and building on the Port of Nome project already underway to position Alaska as the intercontinental transportation hub of the 21st century. This isn't a campaign vision statement; it's built on years of legislative groundwork, including the presidential border permit for the A2A rail project and the $175 million state appropriation that brought federal dollars to Nome. That same record-backed approach shows up across every issue. An A+ NRA rating. A Stand for Health Freedom endorsement rooted in a conviction that Alaskans should make their own health decisions, not government. And a KTUU interview that gets at why this campaign exists: because the work isn't finished and the people's choice is ready to finish it. August 18th is seven days away. If you haven't voted yet, early voting is open now. Scroll down for the full transportation hub plan, debate highlights from Soldotna, and everything else from a big week on the trail. Ready to serve you, Republican Candidate for Governorof the Great State of Alaska p.s. In the homestretch now - one week to go until the Primary Election on August 18, and we truly need every Alaskan for the Hughes/Gettys ticket to rally behind us big time! body:
I spent the last few days in Michigan and I wanted to let you know how it went.

I spent the last few days in Michigan and I wanted to let you know how it went. And before you click away, I have an ask at the bottom (non-fundraising). So don't leave before you look at that.
First, I arrived with the news that we helped raise almost $175,000 for the Michigan Democratic Party in the last week from almost 6,000 individual donations (average of less than $30). Needless to say, they were very thankful -- so thank you for that. That's money that will go right toward electing Democrats up and down the ballot in Michigan this November.
While there, I met with the next Governor of Michigan, Jocelyn Benson, and the next United States Senator, Abdul El-Sayed. I kicked off a canvass for Alex Hawkins and Sarah Pounds, both running for state representative in Michigan. Well over 100 people turned out, which is an extraordinary number for a canvass kick-off, let alone one in mid-August.
I attended services at Fellowship Chapel -- a pillar of Detroit and a place where faith has matched action. Under Reverend Dr. Wendell Anthony’s leadership, this congregation has carried forward the tradition of civil rights advocacy and community empowerment.
[](https://act.gavinnewsom.com/go/11068?t=1&akid=2994%2E4767699%2ELuN-fV)
And while there has been a lot of talk about our interesting differences in the Democratic Party, I spoke about the fight that unites us -- the fight against concentrated wealth and power in this country.
Not left vs. right.
Top vs. Bottom.
[**Please watch and share.](https://act.gavinnewsom.com/go/11069?t=2&akid=2994%2E4767699%2ELuN-fV)**
[](https://act.gavinnewsom.com/go/11069?t=3&akid=2994%2E4767699%2ELuN-fV)
Before you go - if you are someone who is sick and tired of what is happening in this country with Donald Trump in the White House and Republicans in control of Congress, then I offer you a chance to something about it.
Thank you,
Gavin Newsom
* * *

⛅️ To my fellow Democrats — Please do not click away just yet... 🇺🇸
This is a moment that reminds me of Bobby Kennedy’s speech at the 1964 Democratic Convention. He said that JFK would have never been able to accomplish any of what he did without the support of all of you — the Democratic Party. That when we’re in it together, we can accomplish a great deal. That remains true today, and it's the only way forward.
The outcome of this election is not something we can just sit back and witness. We all have a role in shaping its outcome. For some, it's donating. For others, it's knocking on doors or making phone calls. For others, maybe it's sharing information online. That last one is my ask of you today. And it's a big one.
[**Please signup to attend a very brief training to learn how you can help online to elect Democrats up-and-down the ballot this November. Trainings are every Tuesday between now and the election (including one later today). Please join.**](https://act.gavinnewsom.com/go/11070?t=4&akid=2994%2E4767699%2ELuN-fV)
| [JOIN A TRAINING](https://act.gavinnewsom.com/go/11070?t=5&akid=2994%2E4767699%2ELuN-fV)

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com . Email is a very important way we communicate with supporters like you, but if you want to, you can [ unsubscribe here](https://act.gavinnewsom.com/unsubscribe/unsubscribe?t=6&akid=2994%2E4767699%2ELuN-fV).

Sacramento, CA 95815

### What Eisenhower, Gavin, and Powell can still teach us about leadership.

America was born because a revolutionary army learned how to adapt and eventually become a conventional army.
George Washington understood something that has remained true through 250 years of American history: military strength depends on far more than weapons or battlefield skill. Armies are institutions made of people. They require judgment, trust, discipline, and leaders capable of holding those things together under extraordinary pressure.
I have spent much of my adult life around that institution--as an Army officer, teaching at West Point, a paratrooper deployed to Iraq with the 82nd Airborne Division, a member of Congress serving on the House Armed Services Committee, and eventually Under Secretary and Acting Secretary of the Army at the Pentagon. Along the way, I studied great commanders and served alongside leaders who shaped my own understanding of what leadership demands.
Three generals, in particular, have stayed with me: Dwight Eisenhower, James Gavin, and Colin Powell.
They came from different generations and faced very different wars. What connects them is something more useful than a list of victories. Each understood a different dimension of leadership that remains relevant far beyond the military.
## **Dwight Eisenhower: The General Nobody Expected**
By late 1943, the Allies were preparing one of the most complicated military operations in history: crossing the English Channel, landing an enormous army in Nazi-occupied France, and beginning the liberation of Western Europe.
There were more obvious choices than Dwight Eisenhower. George Marshall, the Army Chief of Staff and one of the architects of America's war effort, was widely considered a leading candidate.
Eisenhower was an unusual choice in one obvious respect. He had never commanded troops in combat before World War II. Only a few years earlier, he had been a relatively obscure Army staff officer whose strengths were planning, organization, judgment, and an unusual ability to work with powerful people.
By 1943, he had successfully commanded Allied operations in [North Africa](https://substack.com/redirect/922acfb2-17e3-4bc0-ac62-ac605dcbe1b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and the Mediterranean. Still, his resume looked unconventional beside some of the celebrated battlefield commanders around him.
Yet FDR chose Eisenhower to lead [Operation Overlord](https://substack.com/redirect/dd433d54-0ada-4f5b-b770-38280a4bf198?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the Allied invasion of Normandy better known as D-Day.
The reason becomes clearer when you look at the people he had to manage. George Patton was brilliant but occasionally uncontrollable. British officer [Bernard Montgomery](https://substack.com/redirect/8c3f0731-8231-467e-afcd-c14ad5151ef6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) was talented, but unbearable. [Charles de Gaulle](https://substack.com/redirect/b801a2dc-6f27-402e-8893-667625f3db15?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) had his own conception of France's interests. [Winston Churchill](https://substack.com/redirect/b5132786-d36c-4f23-a0a1-a80c061afa55?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) had his own conception of practically everything. Somebody had to keep all of them moving in roughly the same direction. Eisenhower did.
He listened, negotiated, absorbed disagreement, and understood when an ego could be indulged, when it had to be contained, and when the mission required him simply to make the call.
That mattered on D-Day. When bad weather threatened the invasion in June 1944, the final decision to launch belonged to Eisenhower. He gave the order. Before knowing whether the invasion would succeed, he also wrote a statement accepting responsibility if it failed. The blame, he decided, would be his.
Then came another test of leadership. On April 12, 1945, Eisenhower toured [Ohrdruf](https://substack.com/redirect/b452682d-24ed-479c-a817-e9f04b955ad6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), a Nazi concentration camp and subcamp of Buchenwald liberated by American forces. What he saw left him physically sick: corpses, starvation, and evidence of systematic murder.
But Eisenhower was already thinking about what would happen after the war. He worried that one day people might dismiss the evidence of Nazi atrocities as propaganda. So he pushed for journalists (Hitler shut down the press when he came into power), members of Congress, and other witnesses to visit the camps themselves and document what they saw. He wanted photographs, film, testimony, and firsthand accounts that would make the truth impossible to erase. He was thinking beyond the battle, beyond the war, and beyond his own lifetime.

## **James "Jumping Jim" Gavin: The Visionary**
James Gavin has always felt a little closer to home.
Decades before I deployed to Iraq with the 82nd Airborne Division, Mount Carmel, Pennsylvania native 'Jumpin Jim' Gavin helped turn that division into [one of the most formidable fighting forces in the U.S. Army](https://substack.com/redirect/e1205939-a23f-4c76-a5ea-6b3ec587227b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). What makes him remarkable is how early he understood that warfare was changing. Airborne warfare was still a radical idea when Gavin volunteered for the Army's fledgling parachute forces in 1941. Armies had spent centuries moving soldiers across land and sea. Aircraft suddenly created another possibility: troops could maneuver through the sky, appear behind enemy lines, seize key terrain and transform the geometry of a battlefield. West Point graduate Gavin threw himself into figuring out how. He became one of the officers shaping America's emerging airborne doctrine as the Army developed its first field manuals for parachute and air-landing troops.
Gavin fought in [Sicily](https://substack.com/redirect/6defec89-1190-436b-88de-da4e21f83a72?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [Normandy](https://substack.com/redirect/23c8704a-f8d5-4e2a-be13-cf56e8ab1884?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), jumped into the [Netherlands](https://substack.com/redirect/dc895378-c253-4a8d-aff1-4b50c5c11b4c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) during Operation Market Garden, and later commanded the 82nd Airborne Division during the [Battle of the Bulge](https://substack.com/redirect/fe431a92-ef92-417c-bb36-f8099a56e820?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). He became known as the "Jumping General" because he did something unusual for a senior commander: he jumped into combat with his paratroopers, always the first one out of the aircraft (and the last one in the chow line making sure his paratroopers ate first), ultimately making four combat jumps during the war.
As a young officer, he also helped develop the doctrine that made airborne forces usable, helping turn an experimental concept into battlefield capability. His rise was extraordinary: in just four years, he went from captain to a two-star major general - the youngest WWII division commander at age 37. That combination is what makes Gavin so compelling. He imagined a new way of fighting, helped write the book for it, and then put his own life behind the idea.
And he kept looking ahead. After World War II, as the Army's first chief of research and development, Gavin became an early advocate for using helicopters to move troops rapidly around the battlefield--years before air mobility became central to the Vietnam War.
Gavin understood a danger that confronts every successful military: victory can make an institution overly attached to the methods that just worked. History keeps moving.
That lesson feels especially important now. Drones, artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, directed energy, cyberwarfare, and increasingly sophisticated electronic warfare are changing the battlefield again. The Army that wins the next major conflict will almost certainly need capabilities, organizations, and doctrines that look different from those that won the last one.
Gavin's example is a reminder that adaptation cannot begin after the shooting starts. You have to build the future while everyone else is still comfortable with the present. He was instrumental in the desegregation of the US Army and went on to become the US Ambassador to France during the Kennedy Administration. He was the author of five books and will always be beloved by American paratroopers - especially every August 16th - National Airborne Day.
## **Colin Powell: Defining the Mission**
Colin Powell's rise was extraordinary. The son of Jamaican immigrants, he entered an Army still living with the legacy of segregation, at a time when Black officers faced major barriers to advancement. He served [two tours in Vietnam](https://substack.com/redirect/4932add4-f27b-46e5-a5c4-84b595e12dc5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), including with the 101st Airborne Division, rose through the senior ranks, became a White House Fellow, the President's national security adviser, and ultimately became the first Black Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff.
By then, Powell had become something unusual in American public life: a general whose credibility extended well beyond the military. Presidents trusted him and the public knew his name.
When I arrived at the Pentagon as Under Secretary of the Army in 2016, Powell had been retired from uniform for more than two decades. His influence was still everywhere, particularly in the way a generation of military leaders thought about the use of American power. He took me under his wing and I spent time with him at his home at McLean, Virginia. We talked often about our beloved Army, the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan, and national public service opportunities.
His experience in Vietnam helped shape what became known as the[ Powell Doctrine](https://substack.com/redirect/695f39bb-2c78-4caa-8373-fbfbdbb8facd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Powell came away convinced that American troops should never be sent into war unless the country clearly knew what it wanted them to accomplish and was prepared to give them what they needed to do it. The doctrine reduced that conviction to a series of deliberately simple questions: What American interest is at stake? What are we trying to accomplish? Do we have enough force to do it? Does the public support the mission? And how will we know when it is over?
The 1991 [Gulf War](https://substack.com/redirect/33ec12f5-8159-4ae7-9bdc-5fd4dbbab3a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) showed the approach in practice. Saddam Hussein had invaded Kuwait, and the mission was clear: force his army out. Powell helped ensure that the United States went in with enough troops and international support to do exactly that. Once Kuwait was liberated, the mission was over. That clarity was central to Powell's view of leadership.
He also believed bad news had to travel upward. Leaders cannot fix problems their subordinates are afraid to bring them.
Powell's own career eventually demonstrated how consequential that principle could be. As Secretary of State, he presented the case for Iraqi weapons of mass destruction to the United Nations in 2003. Much of the intelligence behind that presentation proved wrong, and Powell later called the episode a ["blot"](https://substack.com/redirect/fcd962b4-2e51-49b3-9676-4bffce74fec5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on his record.
It complicates his legacy, but it also makes the lesson more important. Powell spent his career insisting that America should never send troops into harm's way without a clear purpose, a realistic plan, and a shared understanding of what success would mean.
**Wisdom is Learning from Others ' Mistakes**
When you learn from great military or civilian leaders, you truly learn from their mistakes along the way. There's a reason why great leaders like Warren Buffett deliberately reads five to six hours every day - in his case, five newspapers, biographies and financial reports - he calls it compound learning. Knowledge is power and by reading and sharing the stories of these three great American generals - especially during America's 250th birthday - I hope you two can learn from them too.
