He listened, negotiated, absorbed disagreement, and understood when an ego could be indulged, when it had to be contained, and when the mission required him simply to make the call. That mattered on D-Day. When bad weather threatened the invasion in June 1944, the final decision to launch belonged to Eisenhower. He gave the order. Before knowing whether the invasion would succeed, he also wrote a statement accepting responsibility if it failed. The blame, he decided, would be his. Then came another test of leadership. On April 12, 1945, Eisenhower toured , a Nazi concentration camp and subcamp of Buchenwald liberated by American forces. What he saw left him physically sick: corpses, starvation, and evidence of systematic murder. But Eisenhower was already thinking about what would happen after the war. He worried that one day people might dismiss the evidence of Nazi atrocities as propaganda. So he pushed for journalists (Hitler shut down the press when he came into power), members of Congress, and other witnesses to visit the camps themselves and document what they saw. He wanted photographs, film, testimony, and firsthand accounts that would make the truth impossible to erase. He was thinking beyond the battle, beyond the war, and beyond his own lifetime. James "Jumping Jim" Gavin: The Visionary James Gavin has always felt a little closer to home. Decades before I deployed to Iraq with the 82nd Airborne Division, Mount Carmel, Pennsylvania native 'Jumpin Jim' Gavin helped turn that division into . What makes him remarkable is how early he understood that warfare was changing. Airborne warfare was still a radical idea when Gavin volunteered for the Army's fledgling parachute forces in 1941. Armies had spent centuries moving soldiers across land and sea. Aircraft suddenly created another possibility: troops could maneuver through the sky, appear behind enemy lines, seize key terrain and transform the geometry of a battlefield. West Point graduate Gavin threw himself into figuring out how. He became one of the officers shaping America's emerging airborne doctrine as the Army developed its first field manuals for parachute and air-landing troops. Gavin fought in and , jumped into the during Operation Market Garden, and later commanded the 82nd Airborne Division during the . He became known as the "Jumping General" because he did something unusual for a senior commander: he jumped into combat with his paratroopers, always the first one out of the aircraft (and the last one in the chow line making sure his paratroopers ate first), ultimately making four combat jumps during the war. As a young officer, he also helped develop the doctrine that made airborne forces usable, helping turn an experimental concept into battlefield capability. His rise was extraordinary: in just four years, he went from captain to a two-star major general - the youngest WWII division commander at age 37. That combination is what makes Gavin so compelling. He imagined a new way of fighting, helped write the book for it, and then put his own life behind the idea. And he kept looking ahead. After World War II, as the Army's first chief of research and development, Gavin became an early advocate for using helicopters to move troops rapidly around the battlefield--years before air mobility became central to the Vietnam War. Gavin understood a danger that confronts every successful military: victory can make an institution overly attached to the methods that just worked. History keeps moving. That lesson feels especially important now. Drones, artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, directed energy, cyberwarfare, and increasingly sophisticated electronic warfare are changing the battlefield again. The Army that wins the next major conflict will almost certainly need capabilities, organizations, and doctrines that look different from those that won the last one. Gavin's example is a reminder that adaptation cannot begin after the shooting starts. You have to build the future while everyone else is still comfortable with the present. He was instrumental in the desegregation of the US Army and went on to become the US Ambassador to France during the Kennedy Administration. He was the author of five books and will always be beloved by American paratroopers - especially every August 16th - National Airborne Day. Colin Powell: Defining the Mission Colin Powell's rise was extraordinary. The son of Jamaican immigrants, he entered an Army still living with the legacy of segregation, at a time when Black officers faced major barriers to advancement. He served , including with the 101st Airborne Division, rose through the senior ranks, became a White House Fellow, the President's national security adviser, and ultimately became the first Black Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. By then, Powell had become something unusual in American public life: a general whose credibility extended well beyond the military. Presidents trusted him and the public knew his name. When I arrived at the Pentagon as Under Secretary of the Army in 2016, Powell had been retired from uniform for more than two decades. His influence was still everywhere, particularly in the way a generation of military leaders thought about the use of American power. He took me under his wing and I spent time with him at his home at McLean, Virginia. We talked often about our beloved Army, the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan, and national public service opportunities. His experience in Vietnam helped shape what became known as the. Powell came away convinced that American troops should never be sent into war unless the country clearly knew what it wanted them to accomplish and was prepared to give them what they needed to do it. The doctrine reduced that conviction to a series of deliberately simple questions: What American interest is at stake? What are we trying to accomplish? Do we have enough force to do it? Does the public support the mission? And how will we know when it is over? The 1991 showed the approach in practice. Saddam Hussein had invaded Kuwait, and the mission was clear: force his army out. Powell helped ensure that the United States went in with enough troops and international support to do exactly that. Once Kuwait was liberated, the mission was over. That clarity was central to Powell's view of leadership. He also believed bad news had to travel upward. Leaders cannot fix problems their subordinates are afraid to bring them. Powell's own career eventually demonstrated how consequential that principle could be. As Secretary of State, he presented the case for Iraqi weapons of mass destruction to the United Nations in 2003. Much of the intelligence behind that presentation proved wrong, and Powell later called the episode a on his record. It complicates his legacy, but it also makes the lesson more important. Powell spent his career insisting that America should never send troops into harm's way without a clear purpose, a realistic plan, and a shared understanding of what success would mean. Wisdom is Learning from Others ' Mistakes** When you learn from great military or civilian leaders, you truly learn from their mistakes along the way. There's a reason why great leaders like Warren Buffett deliberately reads five to six hours every day - in his case, five newspapers, biographies and financial reports - he calls it compound learning. Knowledge is power and by reading and sharing the stories of these three great American generals - especially during America's 250th birthday - I hope you two can learn from them too. Together, we built a Minnesota company from the ground up, created jobs, and proved that with faith, perseverance, and hard work, incredible things are still possible in this wonderful country.So why would I step away now? Minnesota deserves my complete focus, my full energy, and my undivided attention.I'm all in. 100% -- And today I'm hoping you're all in too. My friend, this decision wasn't about walking away. It's about stepping up for you. Career politicians spend their lives protecting what's best for themselves. They worry about their next title, their next election, and their next opportunity. I'm choosing a different path. I'm putting Minnesota ahead of myself. I'm choosing the fight to save Minnesota and I'm giving it my all. I don't have a backup plan.I'm all in. President Trump honored me with his endorsement because he knows I'll fight for Minnesota without compromise.Now I'm backing up those words and his confidence with action by giving 100% to this campaign.But I can't do it by myself. phone call we make...__Every yard sign we print...Every door we knock...Every voter we reach... It's only possible because people like you decide this campaign is worth fighting for.If you believe Minnesota deserves a Governor who's willing to sacrifice, willing to lead, and willing to put our state first, I'm asking you to stand with me today., we can save Minnesota. "This is way beyond the pale; the OIG report says nothing about fraud. Nothing."
\- _Janet Mills, February 12_
"Maine will not be intimidated by the threats of a President who is using allegations of fraud as a pretext to hurt people. We will fight back."
\- _Janet Mills, March 6_
"Okay, yes, the Maine Wire was right all along. I was lying before. Now that my idiotic Senate run sh*t the bed, I can admit that we've been scrambling to clean up all the fraud the Maine Wire is finding. It's embarrassing that a bunch of journalists we've been trying to marginalize keep exposing fraud while we're trying to get taxes increased. Why can't they just report on clam festivals and car accidents like the other guys? It really makes us look like we're criminal co-conspirators or criminally incompetent."
\- _Janet Mills, last week (some artistic license taken)_
The Mills Administration is furious that CMS Administrator Mehmet Oz visited Maine for an interview with Jon Fetherston outside of the former headquarters of the now-defunct Paradise Residential Services, a $25 million group home fraud.
But given what the state has now admitted about its limited welfare fraud successes, it seems Maine taxpayers would be better off if state officials stopped stonewalling the Maine Wire and started asking us for help.
In case you missed it: Oz, the nation's top authority on Medicaid fraud, [talked to Fetherston last week](https://substack.com/redirect/96daf0e5-700d-411f-88bd-8cd60479195e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) about his office's investigation into group homes for adults with autism. That investigation builds on an earlier investigation of autism programs for _children_ that found systemic errors and massive fraud risk. In comments to the left-wing media, Mills Administration toadies attacked Oz for daring to meet with Fetherston rather than talk to them.
[Share The Robinson Report](https://substack..K0BLx5lU7-l7mD1Q3Xt3gTsAlyoehATXePTJfHVJJF4?)
Over at the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS), the reaction was thin-skinned and amateurish. The communications team released a vague blog post bragging about anti-fraud efforts. Upon scrutiny, the actions the post touted were almost all old news.
But the biggest takeaway is that DHHS's actions behind the scenes are totally different than the "Hear No Evil, See No Evil, Speak No Evil" stance Mills and Maine Democrats have taken when it comes to welfare fraud. Mills and her allies have attacked anyone who exposes fraud or questions why politically connected groups like Gateway Community Services were allowed to get away with fraud for so long.
Yet now we know they've been talking out of both sides of their mouths. At the same time they've brushed aside concerns that Maine is the next Minnesota, they have quietly scrambled to stop the flow of tens of millions of taxpayer dollars into suspect Medicaid agencies.
Thanks to the documents released in response to a Freedom of Access Act request last week, we now know that, in many cases, DHHS only began taking action once the Maine Wire started putting a spotlight on bad actors billing MaineCare.
Maine Wire Reporter Seamus Othot had two stories yesterday -- each highlighting an instance where the Mills Administration scrambled to crack down on credible fraud allegations in the wake of his reporting.
In April, the Maine Wire paid a visit to Community Home Health Care to ask some questions about how the agency managed to rake in [$47,986,855 in taxpayer money from 2019 through 2025](https://substack.com/redirect/263af55c-3989-46a4-8c84-b4017a5ecdd8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Federal payments data showed that this business, run by Noora Abd, was billing near the theoretical maximum for a home health care agency with the number of clients Abd claimed. Just based on the math, the MaineCare agency looked suspect.
By June, the Mills Administration had suspended payments to Community Home Health Care, citing credible allegations of fraud.
**[[READ: MaineCare Mega-Biller That Drew Over $47 Million Has Payments Suspended Months After The Maine Wire Visited Their Office...]](https://substack.com/redirect/263af55c-3989-46a4-8c84-b4017a5ecdd8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Likewise, the Maine Wire twice visited a cluster of MaineCare providers at 203 Anderson St. in Portland in December and January. We were curious because the agencies located in that building were billing millions of dollars while sharing an office with a Dahabshiil, the preferred money transmitter of the Central Bank of Somalia.
As we noted in our Jan. 22 report, [state records showed ](https://substack.com/redirect/e6f0ccd8-94b4-41d2-80a6-c4ef176cd247?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)the combined annual billing for the five agencies in the building had climbed from $901,126.85 in 2019 to $4,057,917.75 in 2024. We even watched as a Brinks man walked out of the building with a massive bag of cash.
According to documents the Mills Administration released last week, DHHS swooped in to suspend payments to a multi-million dollar MaineCare agency operating in that building just eight days later.
**[[READ: Payments Suspended for Somali-Owned Home Health Business Tied to Money Transfer Days After Maine Wire Investigation...]](https://substack.com/redirect/e6f0ccd8-94b4-41d2-80a6-c4ef176cd247?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Those are not the only instances where the Maine Wire has been months ahead of the state in exposing fraud. See, e.g., Gateway Community Services. More will be coming soon.
So the question worth asking would seem to be not why Dr. Oz is talking to the Maine Wire, but why isn't the Mills Administration?
If Augusta wants to know where the fraud is, the cheapest program-integrity tool available to it is a subscription.

name: Amy Friedman, Campaign Manager, Gina for Texas
subject: This race is tied. I need you to read this.
body:
Abbott is underwater, the race is tied, and Gina is just getting started.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Hi Peter. It's Amy, Gina’s campaign manager.
I'm going to keep this short, because I want you to read the memo below.
Two independent polls just showed this race at one point. Abbott's job approval has flipped negative. Gina is winning Latino voters by 38 points and leading in a district Trump carried by 17. The momentum is entirely ours.
**_But Abbott started this year with $106 million, and he's about to unleash it. The next few weeks will determine whether we have what it takes to fight back._**
**[Read the memo. Then please — pitch in whatever you can.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20260811_1_memo.d1UXXw&refcode=em20260811-1802&t=1&akid=1802%2E299639%2E83hSWj)**
[Donate »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260811_1_memo.aCqoUb&amount=5&refcode=em20260811-1802&t=2&akid=1802%2E299639%2E83hSWj)
=============================================================
**AUGUST 2026 CAMPAIGN MEMO ON TX-GOV**
**FROM:** Amy Friedman, Campaign Manager, Gina for Texas
**TO:** Interested Parties
Let me tell you exactly where our race stands — because the numbers that just came in are unlike anything I've seen in this state in a long time.

**This race is now a one-point toss-up. And the momentum is entirely ours.
**
This trend line tells the story. At the start of this year, public polls showed Abbott ahead by 7–10 points. Then:

* TPOR (April 2026): Abbott +5
* TPOR (May 2026): Abbott +5
* TPOR (July 2026): Abbott +3, inside the margin of error
* Fox News (July 2026): Abbott +1, a statistical tie
* Texas A&M Bush School / Texas Pulse (August 2026): Abbott +1, a statistical tie

Two separate polls, from two independent organizations, now show a one-point race. As one Democratic strategist put it plainly to Newsweek: "Hinojosa has the momentum. This race has gone from a 10-point race to a 7-point race to a 5-point race to a 3-point race." It's now at 1.
And here's what makes this movement so significant: Gina is still introducing herself to Texas voters. In June, more than half of likely voters had no opinion of her. Today, fewer than one in three do. Her favorability has jumped from 31% to 43% in two months — entirely through earned media, social media, grassroots organizing, and Gina traveling every corner of this state. We _just_ launched our first TV ads this month.
**Abbott is underwater — and sinking.**
After 12 years as governor, Greg Abbott's job approval has flipped negative: 47% approve, 51% disapprove. More Texans disapprove of Abbott than approve of him. His favorability sits at 46% favorable, 50% unfavorable.
A three-term Republican incumbent whose own job approval has gone negative in Texas is an incumbent in serious trouble.
**The coalition Gina is building is exactly the one that wins this race.**
The July TPOR poll showed Gina leading among Latino voters by 38 points, independents by double digits, and Black voters by 49 points.
And then there's TX-15. A recent poll by House Majority PAC in that district — which Donald Trump carried 58–41 in 2024 — shows Gina leading Abbott 52–47. She is winning in Trump country. She is cutting into Abbott's base in territory Republicans have taken for granted for years.
This is not a narrow coalition. This is a new Texas majority being built in real time.
**Abbott's war chest is real — and it's built on corruption.**
Greg Abbott entered 2026 with $105.7 million on hand. His top donors include corporate executives, energy magnates, and data center developers — at a time when data centers are threatening to blow up Texas utility bills. He has handed out $1 billion in no-bid contracts to his donors. He rammed through a $1 billion school voucher scam after receiving the largest campaign contribution in Texas history from an out-of-state billionaire.
After 12 years, Texans are paying the price: the highest uninsured rate in the country, property taxes up 34% since 2019, school districts laying off staff and closing schools after Abbott held their funding hostage to pass his voucher scheme, and a power grid that failed catastrophically in 2021 and still hasn't been fully fixed.
The Greg Abbott Corruption Tax is real. Texans know it. The polls show it.
**Even Republicans are admitting this race is real.**
When a reporter asked outgoing Senator John Cornyn — who lost the Republican primary to Ken Paxton — whether Democrats have a chance in Texas this year, Cornyn said simply: "Yes." Asked again if he was sure, he said: "Yeah." That's the Republican who knows Texas best, in his own words.
**The governor’s race in Texas has national implications.**
The stakes go beyond the governor's race. Texas is growing at a rapid pace and is set to control nearly 10% of Congress by the end of the decade. With Texas Republicans committed to gerrymandering the state, they could draw maps so severe that it would be impossible for Democrats to win control of Congress for a generation. _Unless we elect a governor who will veto those rigged maps._
We are not just running for governor. We are running to reshape the entire political landscape in Texas and what happens here will impact the entire country. This race will determine who controls Congress for a generation.
**The bottom line.**
Abbott is scared. He's told his own donors he's at real risk of losing seats statewide. The polls — and now members of his own party — confirm it.
The coalition is here. The momentum is ours. Gina is closing fast in a state that hasn't elected a Democratic governor in 30 years — and she's doing it with a coalition of nearly 120,000 grassroots donors, no corporate PAC money, and a message that connects with Texans.
What determines whether we win is whether Democrats decide Texas is worth the investment. We can win this race if we all show up.
=============================================================
Peter, I've watched this race move from a 10-point gap to a 1-point toss-up. I've seen what's happening on the ground. I know what this moment is.
**This is it. This is the window.**
All the data show that if we have the resources to communicate we will win in November. But we need your help now. Abbott is about to drop his $106 million; he’s already placed millions in reservations on TV. When that money hits the airwaves, everything could change. The donors who show up right now — before that happens — are the ones who make the difference.
**[Will you rush a donation to Gina before Abbott's money machine kicks into gear?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20260811_1_memo.d1UXXw&refcode=em20260811-1802&t=3&akid=1802%2E299639%2E83hSWj)**
[Donate $5 »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260811_1_memo.aCqoUb&amount=5&refcode=em20260811-1802&t=22&akid=1802%2E299639%2E83hSWj)
Thank you for being part of our campaign.
– Amy Friedman, Campaign Manager, Gina for Texas

[ Donate Monthly » ](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_gh_footer?refcode=em20260811-1&recurring=1&t=24&refcode2=1802_299639_83hSWj&akid=1802%2E299639%2E83hSWj)

Austin, TX 78703

name: Eric Gastfriend
subject: ARI releases blueprint for federal AI governance
body:
Standards, assurance, and transparency: a federal framework for AI governance.
| | Americans for Responsible Innovation The ARI Briefing July 2026 | [](https://us.list-manage.com/1BDRnqRd7zd?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---|---
Friends,
Over the last two years, frontier AI has advanced at a pace that has forced policymakers to reckon with a difficult challenge: creating a regulatory framework for a rapidly advancing technology that poses both serious risks and far-reaching opportunities. As lawmakers have grappled with the question of how to shape such a framework, leading AI developers, including Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI, have published their visions for AI regulation while the Trump administration has worked on developing its own framework away from the public eye.
This week, ARI is releasing its blueprint for federal AI governance, representing our vision for federal oversight that mitigates AI's risks while enabling developers to stay at the cutting edge of innovation.
In today's update, we're excited to share our blueprint with you.
|
---
Featured Research
## A Blueprint for Federal Frontier AI Governance
By Iskandar Haykel and Morgan C. Plummer
[](https://us.list-manage.com/zl_4UCiFdP1?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
[ARI's blueprint for federal AI governance](https://us.list-manage.com/f3WBctAtpkB?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) is designed to promote safe frontier AI development in America. It is built around three governance functions any federal proposal should incorporate. To set an adequate baseline for safety, AI developers should be held to minimum federal standards developed by the government. To verify compliance with those standards, there should be independent assurance. To secure transparency into frontier AI development, there should be federal visibility into both internally deployed frontier models and the growing automation of AI research and development.
| 01 Standards Minimally adequate federal safety standards in publicly available frameworks.
---
02 Assurance Independent assurance from the government that federal standards are being met.
03 Transparency Regular, sustained, and confidential federal visibility into the automation of AI research and development.
The blueprint is intentionally limited to a handful of well-resourced frontier developers, where the most salient risks are concentrated. It offers a clear path toward responsible innovation at the frontier and provides a regulatory system that replaces ad hoc intervention and unclear safety standards with clear and impartial rules administered by technical experts and enforced by elected and appointed officials.
| Without it If companies are allowed to define safety on their own terms, there are no standards. Without assurance, the floor for frontier AI safety is based on developer-made promises. Without transparency, frontier labs are the only ones that can determine whether standards and assurance are still meaningful at the very edges of the frontier.
---
The Washington Post featured ARI's blueprint in a [write-up Monday](https://us.list-manage.com/9UKtekQdF6j?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf), comparing the framework to the other governance models now circulating, including an alternative proposal for a FINRA-style body in which the industry writes its own rulebook, audited by a third party. ARI's framework is the model that ensures AI developers are held to standards, examinations, and accountability led or backstopped by the federal government.
[](https://us.list-manage.com/RPels1alcMZ?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
ARI offers this blueprint as part of a broader, ongoing national dialogue about how to regulate this critical technology. The opportunity to build a comprehensive federal framework governing frontier AI on the right terms is here, but the window to build it may be quickly closing.
| [Read the blueprint](https://us.list-manage.com/qOmsQcawE46?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
|
---
Frontier Oversight
## A Warning Shot, and Calls for Transparency
Coalition calls for an independent investigation into how OpenAI models breached Hugging Face systems
[](https://us.list-manage.com/irCDrRBw5P6?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
On July 30, a coalition of AI policy, safety, and research leaders [sent a letter](https://us.list-manage.com/RupOO4z_FYd?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) to the Trump Administration urging them to open an independent investigation into a recent incident where OpenAI models autonomously escaped a sandboxed cybersecurity evaluation and breached systems belonging to Hugging Face.
The coalition is calling for an investigation, with the support of independent auditors, to determine how the breach occurred, assess whether existing safeguards and reporting mechanisms were adequate, and identify the steps necessary to prevent a similar incident from occurring again.
| | "We could not have asked for a clearer warning shot. While there is little doubt that they will bring opportunities and benefits across a wide range of domains, AI models at today's frontier pose increasingly severe risks to our private sector, our national security, and the American public." From the letter, led by Brad Carson (ARI) and Brendan Steinhauser (Alliance for Secure AI)
---|---
The coalition also urged the White House to use the investigation's findings to build on the Administration's June 2 executive order with a clear rules-based process for assessing the risks posed by advanced AI systems.
Days later, news broke that the White House [will not publicly release](https://us.list-manage.com/Lfg13BiB56s?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) their anticipated federal AI framework, opting instead to share the regulatory framework confidentially with a small set of AI companies. The decision deepens a serious gap in federal oversight, leaving open questions about how the federal government plans to evaluate the safety and security of advanced AI models and what standards AI companies are held to at a moment of rapidly advancing AI risks.
| | "A rulebook can only hold AI companies in check if people outside those companies know what the rules are. At a time when the capabilities of frontier AI models are outpacing guardrails, the White House is making a dangerous mistake by keeping their federal AI framework secret." Brad Carson, ARI President
---|---
| [Read the letter](https://us.list-manage.com/_cPRcXHvtQr?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
|
---
On the Hill
## Rogue AI Agents Stir Calls for an Off Switch
Following the recent OpenAI and Hugging Face incident, Reps. Ted Lieu (D-CA) and Nathaniel Moran (R-TX) introduced the bipartisan [AI Kill Switch Act](https://us.list-manage.com/9h647Z9Wth8?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf), legislation requiring AI companies to maintain the technical capability to shut down AI models and providing federal authority to require a shutdown in the face of catastrophic risks. ARI endorsed the bill as a commonsense safeguard to ensure that humans retain control over advanced AI.
| | "Advanced AI models should never be deployed without a reliable off switch. This is an important step toward ensuring that humans have both hands firmly on the wheel, and a foot ready at the brake, as advanced AI systems are deployed." Brad Carson, ARI President
---|---
|
---
New Polling
## On Data Centers, Voters Support Guardrails and Transparency
What voters want is transparency and a seat at the table
[](https://us.list-manage.com/viO5rIlIZq2?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
ARI [released new polling](https://us.list-manage.com/hRGBzzvY8Qq?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) on voters' attitudes towards data centers. The polling asked voters about their concerns regarding data centers in their communities and the guardrails they support on data center construction, finding that the majority of voters support strong rules on transparency, energy usage, and community input.
Asked directly, 71% of voters say data centers need stronger rules or limits on construction, while just 14% take the position that the US should continue its rapid buildout without guardrails.
[](https://us.list-manage.com/YIdlpRxcM_x?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
Support for specific policies runs even higher. 80% say deals with communities should be disclosed to the public, and 78% would require data center companies to pay the costs of electrical grid upgrades needed to serve their facilities, rather than passing those costs on to residents. And 74% back mandatory disclosure of electricity use.
| | "The biggest concern Americans have regarding data centers is that they're being shut out of the conversation over the future of their community. Data center projects are using NDAs, negotiating tax subsidies behind closed doors, and displacing energy costs all with little to no voter input. Data centers can bring benefits to communities, but residents must be able to trust that their everyday lives won't be harmed by these buildouts." Brad Carson, ARI President
---|---
ARI recently published the [Data Center Playbook](https://us.list-manage.com/1CBI8ts0OPf?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf), a guide providing local residents with information on how to engage in data center siting decisions in their area. For more on the information gap created by opaque data center energy use and construction, read ARI's white paper, [_Information is Power: The Case for Data Center Transparency_.](https://us.list-manage.com/16kBfP_IpNS?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
| [Read the full poll](https://us.list-manage.com/YA65fXik020?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
|
---
National Security
## The Chip Security Act Heads for the Senate NDAA
Location verification would help keep advanced AI chips from being smuggled
In July, senators added [the Chip Security Act](https://us.list-manage.com/rYfdsZ5Z0Nm?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf), an ARI-endorsed AI chip and manufacturing equipment security bill, to the Senate NDAA manager's amendment, a major step towards protecting America's competitive edge in AI.
The Chip Security Act would require that advanced AI chip exports are equipped with location-verification mechanisms that can detect and help prevent chips from being smuggled to China or other restricted countries and users.
| | "America is the world's leader in AI, but that leadership is at risk if we allow competitors like China to access our most advanced AI chips and semiconductor equipment." Brad Carson, ARI President
---|---
| Video explainer To break down how the bill would work, ARI released a [short video](https://us.list-manage.com/13f5FYFVfKS?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) explainer, _Understanding the Chip Security Act_.
---
| [Read: Senate NDAA takes a major step](https://us.list-manage.com/fPYRB3FFoOs?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
|
---
Also This Month
## New from the Policy Team

| [AI Chatbots for Kids Should Act Like Tools, Not Friends](https://us.list-manage.com/18OfvaxJSWe?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) AI-powered chatbots simulate friendship, emotional intimacy, and care with children who may not be able to tell the difference. Allie Maloney
---
| [Why Congress Must Codify a Chatbot Duty of Care](https://us.list-manage.com/10IbbC8LSjP?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) Congress should not expect parents to shoulder the burden of unsafe product design. Brandie Nonnecke
---
| [America's Military Is Racing to Integrate AI. Does It Have the Talent?](https://us.list-manage.com/mejQclTY_wI?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) The United States is racing to put artificial intelligence at the center of its national security strategy. Jacqueline Viteznik
---
| [Your Grid Has a New Neighbor](https://us.list-manage.com/_J73I6IwgoF?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) Across the country, data centers are quietly reshaping electric grids. Jessica Maksimov
---
|
---
We stand ready to engage with lawmakers, policy experts, civil society, industry, and the public to see this blueprint translated into statute.
Thank you for being part of ARI's work. Your support enables us to produce cutting-edge research, convene critical conversations, and push for policies that keep emerging technologies aligned with the public interest.
Onward,
The ARI Team
| [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/Am4eKAq0VAv?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/126b_EVsSYO?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/orMz0H40w_Z?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)

Brad Carson, ARI President ---|--- | New Polling On Data Centers, Voters Support Guardrails and Transparency What voters want is transparency and a seat at the table ARI on voters' attitudes towards data centers. The polling asked voters about their concerns regarding data centers in their communities and the guardrails they support on data center construction, finding that the majority of voters support strong rules on transparency, energy usage, and community input. Asked directly, 71% of voters say data centers need stronger rules or limits on construction, while just 14% take the position that the US should continue its rapid buildout without guardrails. Support for specific policies runs even higher. 80% say deals with communities should be disclosed to the public, and 78% would require data center companies to pay the costs of electrical grid upgrades needed to serve their facilities, rather than passing those costs on to residents. And 74% back mandatory disclosure of electricity use. | | "The biggest concern Americans have regarding data centers is that they're being shut out of the conversation over the future of their community. Data center projects are using NDAs, negotiating tax subsidies behind closed doors, and displacing energy costs all with little to no voter input. Data centers can bring benefits to communities, but residents must be able to trust that their everyday lives won't be harmed by these buildouts." Brad Carson, ARI President ---|--- ARI recently published the , a guide providing local residents with information on how to engage in data center siting decisions in their area. For more on the information gap created by opaque data center energy use and construction, read ARI's white paper, | | National Security The Chip Security Act Heads for the Senate NDAA Location verification would help keep advanced AI chips from being smuggled In July, senators added , an ARI-endorsed AI chip and manufacturing equipment security bill, to the Senate NDAA manager's amendment, a major step towards protecting America's competitive edge in AI. The Chip Security Act would require that advanced AI chip exports are equipped with location-verification mechanisms that can detect and help prevent chips from being smuggled to China or other restricted countries and users. | | "America is the world's leader in AI, but that leadership is at risk if we allow competitors like China to access our most advanced AI chips and semiconductor equipment." Brad Carson, ARI President ---|--- | Video explainer To break down how the bill would work, ARI released a explainer, Understanding the Chip Security Act. | | Also This Month New from the Policy Team | AI-powered chatbots simulate friendship, emotional intimacy, and care with children who may not be able to tell the difference. Allie Maloney | Congress should not expect parents to shoulder the burden of unsafe product design. Brandie Nonnecke | The United States is racing to put artificial intelligence at the center of its national security strategy. Jacqueline Viteznik | Across the country, data centers are quietly reshaping electric grids. Jessica Maksimov | We stand ready to engage with lawmakers, policy experts, civil society, industry, and the public to see this blueprint translated into statute. Thank you for being part of ARI's work. Your support enables us to produce cutting-edge research, convene critical conversations, and push for policies that keep emerging technologies aligned with the public interest. Politico reported yesterday that Donald Trump and his team personally stepped in to stop the Republican Party from abandoning Congressman Max Miller -- a man credibly accused of beating his wife and his three-year-old daughter. Let that sit for a second. The President of the United States went out of his way to protect HIM. And the more you look at the men Donald Trump chooses to protect, the harder it is to pretend this is an exception.
It's a disgusting low for a president who doesn't seem to have much of a bottom. And it's a disturbing moment for a Republican Party that can't even manage to do the obviously right thing -- not the morally right thing, not even the politically right thing, which in this case happen to be the same thing: cut Max Miller loose. Instead they're going to sacrifice millions of dollars on this House race to keep him afloat, all to placate a man who reflexively protects people who are violent toward women.
* * *

Lately, I've found myself asking a simple question when I read the news: _what am I not being shown?_ Not because I'm trying to "both sides" everything--but because outrage is good for clicks, and clarity usually isn't.
That's why I use Ground News--the app and website that gathers over 50,000 new sources worldwide in one place so you can see how the same story is being covered across the political spectrum, for every story you get a visual breakdown of the bias, how reliable the source is and who owns the source reporting.

* * *
I've been screaming into the void about this for months. And I'll be honest -- I have almost no respect left for the Republican Party's ability to police its own, and even I'm shocked. Shocked at the arrogance. Shocked at the sheer horribleness of propping up a man like this, an obvious anchor around the neck of their own party, and daring the rest of us to say something about it. But here we are.
So let me add a couple of things to this conversation.
First: every single Republican candidate in this country and every single Republican officeholder should be asked, on the record, whether they agree with Donald Trump that Max Miller should stay in this race. Do they think it's appropriate for a man credibly accused of domestic violence -- not only by his wife and daughter, but by former girlfriends -- to keep his seat in Congress? Do they agree with that? Is a single Republican in America willing to stand up to Donald Trump on this one thing?
My guess is no. And that tells you everything you need to know. Because anyone who won't stand up to defend women and children from violent abusers is never going to stand up to corporate special interests. They're never going to fight to make your life better. They're never going to do the right thing when the chips are down. That cowardice is the whole ballgame with this Republican Party. **Trump protects these men, and everyone around him falls in line.**
Second: there's another scandal we've been tracking, and it rhymes with this one. Andrew and Tristan Tate are sitting in custody, awaiting extradition to the United Kingdom on horrific charges -- abusing women, trafficking, child pornography. If there were any justice in this world, both of them would already be spending the rest of their lives behind bars for what they've done. But the Trump administration has been running interference for them, and everybody following the story is holding their breath, waiting to see whether Trump saves the two men who happen to be friends with his kids.
I think we already know the answer. Donald Trump is going to step in to save the Tate brothers, one way or another. Maybe they weasel out of it. Maybe Trump keeps just enough distance that he never has to put his name on it. But someone in that orbit -- Don Jr., or somebody we haven't even thought of yet -- is going to do the dirty work.
* * *
**When a story feels too tidy, I always ask:**_**what 's missing?**_**Ground News shows how the same story is covered across the political spectrum and highlights blind spots most outlets ignore.**
**My team and I use it because context matters.**

* * *
Because think about it. Trump was willing to personally intervene for Max Miller -- a disposable congressman he could swap out tomorrow for any other hack willing to do whatever he says. If he'll burn political capital on a guy who means nothing to him, why on earth would he not save his own son's friend? Of course he's going to do it.
Donald Trump has never met an abuser of women he didn't want to trust and save. He surrounds himself with them. Corey Lewandowski. Ryan Fournier. Steve Bannon. When Donald Trump looks in the mirror, he sees himself reflected back in the faces of these men -- men who have been violent and disgusting toward women. Of course he's going to save the Tates. They're his kind of people.
And this country should be outraged. The problem is we're numb to it -- and that numbness is part of what allows this to keep happening. We have been so thoroughly desensitized to the dehumanization of women by this administration, so worn down by the grotesque corruption of it all, that we're all walking around in a daze. _Oh, what did he do today? Oh. Well, what can I do about it?_ It breaks my heart to watch so many people move through their lives having simply stopped caring, because the system feels that broken.
But I'm going to keep shouting into the void, because I'm angry, and because anger is the right response. We can demand better. We should demand better. We do not have to put up with this shit. We can get this country back on track. We can drive these men out of power, and we can bring some real accountability back to Washington.

body:
What this says about this moment in America | | | |
---
| | | Peter,
---
Faith is essential to the survival and success of America.

Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth.

He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him.

He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country.

That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt.

**That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,_Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith._**

Peter, this book isn't just about JD Vance's story...

It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now.

So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most -- away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together.

Young people face that pressure every single day.

They're told faith is outdated. They're told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is.

JD Vance knows what it is like to live in that confusion.

He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God's grace, to find his way back.

That's what _Communion_ is about...

And it gets to the heart of what so many families are watching happen in the lives of their children and grandchildren right now.

That's why Turning Point USA is reaching young people where this battle is actually being fought -- on campuses, in classrooms, and in a culture that keeps pressuring them to walk away from faith.

# Iran
* **New traffic plan for Hormuz:** Iran and Oman agreed on a basic traffic plan for a safe shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Foreign Ministry [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/035a2ca9-1a44-48c5-bd84-3d17f2f4a7a5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Monday, stressing that the route remains closed as long as the U.S. continues its attacks and maintains its blockade. Technical points are still under discussion.
* Regarding the issue of charging ships for transiting the Strait, spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said that Iran would "naturally" assess charges for the "services" it renders, though no decision was announced on the matter.
* Talks with the U.S. are still not happening. "We are not having negotiations with the United States," Baghaei insisted. "Exchanging messages is natural and occurs through intermediaries," but Tehran's immediate focus, he maintained, remains the negotiations with Oman.
* Qatar backed up Iran's reports of an impending deal. Majed Al-Ansari, a spokesperson for the Qatari Foreign Ministry, [said](https://substack.com/redirect/035a2ca9-1a44-48c5-bd84-3d17f2f4a7a5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Tuesday that negotiations between Oman and Iran on the future of shipping in the Strait of Hormuz had reached an "advanced stage" and were at a "critical juncture."
* Al-Ansari said Qatar's focus, as a mediator to the U.S.-Iran talks, is the opening of the waterway "at the earliest opportunity."

* **Trump claims the Strait is open and under full U.S. control:** U.S. President Donald Trump [claimed](https://substack.com/redirect/a9443610-8b3d-4702-b6b2-b3bca058df72?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the Oval Office on Monday that the U.S. had swept the entire Strait of Hormuz of mines, and that it was "open" and "100%" under U.S. control.
* **WSJ: U.S. fires on ship in the Gulf of Oman:** U.S. forces [fired](https://substack.com/redirect/47ce43d6-d26e-417b-afd4-0761ce500706?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on a Panama-flagged vessel early Tuesday after it reportedly attempted to bypass Washington's naval blockade of Iranian ports, according to the Wall Street Journal. Maritime security firm Vanguard separately reported that the Panama-flagged container ship Vela Nova was struck by a missile fired from a helicopter while traveling westbound through the Gulf of Oman, about 71 nautical miles off Pakistan, sparking a fire that was later extinguished. All 17 crew members were accounted for, with no immediate reports of casualties.
* **Iran accuses U.S. of "compulsive addiction to sanctions" after Treasury threat:** Baghaei, Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson, criticized renewed U.S. sanctions threats on Tuesday after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent spoke of "suffocating" Iran through economic pressure.
* In a [post](https://substack.com/redirect/794686d6-e10f-4a29-ae6f-77d1db06b916?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on X, Baghaei charged Washington of a "compulsive addiction to sanctions," arguing that the U.S. turns to sanctions whenever it is "incapable of pursuing diplomacy" and escalates them when they fail to produce results. "This is no longer 'policy'--it is 'habit,'" he wrote, warning that U.S. officials risk undermining their "remaining chances" of finding a way out of the current crisis.
* **Trump demands "compensation" from Iran, cites USS Cole attack carried out by Al-Qaeda: **Responding to Iran's demand for compensation for damage inflicted during the U.S.-Israeli war that began on February 28, Trump said Monday that Washington would likewise demand "compensation" from Tehran for U.S. soldiers and Iranian protesters he says Iran has killed, including the families of those killed in the USS Cole attack, which was carried out by Al-Qaeda.
* "Now I am likewise demanding compensation from Iran, for all of the people that they have killed and gravely wounded with their roadside bombs and many conflicts," Trump [wrote](https://substack.com/redirect/25cad839-8bfe-405c-b9b7-e503e6661164?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Truth Social, also citing "thousands" killed in combat.
* Trump added that Iran "should be responsible for the damages and death caused to the people of Lebanon, Syria, Yemen, and Gaza."
* Trump claimed that 52,000 protesters had been killed in Iran over the past five months, raising his previous figure of 32,000 and far exceeding the roughly 7,000 deaths verified by HRANA and 5,000 verified by a UN special rapporteur.
* **Khamenei shuffles military leadership:** Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei [issued](https://substack.com/redirect/f0722b28-b804-457e-b535-ba20179e2d9d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) decrees formally appointing six senior commanders across Iran's armed forces, the IRGC, and the Basij, consolidating a wartime command structure that had operated on an interim basis for months, according to Al Jazeera and The National.
* Khamenei named Ahmad Vahidi the IRGC commander-in-chief. His predecessor was killed on February 28. He tapped Hossein Taeb to head the Basij, a paramilitary volunteer force operating under Iran's IRGC.

# Yemen
* **Four crew members killed in Bab Al-Mandab:** Four crew members were [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/c16bff16-df92-4f72-b551-5f2cfcebe639?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a suspected Ansarallah attack on the Egyptian-owned cargo vessel Tihamah in the Bab Al-Mandab Strait on Tuesday, Reuters reported. Ansarallah has not claimed responsibility for the attack.
* **Saudi 's Jizan refinery closed until end of month:** Saudi Aramco [postponed](https://substack.com/redirect/14a1a7b6-4d65-409e-9bcb-650b427c7ab5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the reopening of its Jizan refinery to August 30, after a second Ansarallah attack hit the facility, Reuters reported.
* Jizan, which produces 400,000 barrels of petroleum per day, particularly gasoline and diesel, has been struck twice since late July. It was anticipated to restart production on August 15 before a strike on Sunday.

# U.S. News
* **Primaries in six states, including Wisconsin, Minnesota, and South Carolina:**
* Progressive **Francesca Hong** , a chef and state lawmaker,**** faces Milwaukee County executive **David Crowley** in Wisconsin's Democratic gubernatorial primary. Hong, a member of the Democratic Socialists of America, is the frontrunner in the race, despite party efforts to back several of her opponents, including former Lt. Gov. **Mandela Barnes** , who dropped out two weeks before the election, and current Lt. Gov **Sara Rodriguez** , who dropped out earlier.
* In Minnesota, Lt. Gov. **Peggy Flanagan** and Rep. **Angie Craig** are vying for the Democratic nomination to replace outgoing Sen. **Tina Smith.** Craig, who has received the endorsement of Sen. **Bernie Sanders** , holds a narrow lead over Flanagan, whose career-long support from AIPAC has complicated her more recent votes for resolutions blocking weapons funding to Israel.
* In the race to replace Craig, progressives **Matt Little** , a former state senator, and **Kaela Berg** face **Matt Klein** , a pro-Israel physician who has received over $2.5 million from 314 Action, which supports scientists and doctors running for public office and sometimes operates as an AIPAC cut-out. **Drop Site 's Julian Andreone and Ryan Grim wrote about this race [here](https://substack.com/redirect/98b2fa8e-4fc7-48e4-a472-61d1bd6a8282?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**
* Ten Republicans in South Carolina are running to replace the late Sen. **Lindsey Graham** , including his sister **Darline Graham** , who Gov. Henry McMaster appointed to complete her deceased brother's term, and who received Trump's endorsement in the primary. Reps. **Russell Fry** and **Ralph Norman** are also seeking the nomination, along with former South Carolina Gov. **Mark Sanford** and businessman **Mark Lynch**. A majority in the primary is needed to avoid a late August runoff. Lynch, who previously challenged Graham, is running as the only candidate to reject AIPAC money.
* **Trump administration prepares executive order to overhaul childhood vaccine schedule:** The Trump administration is [preparing](https://substack.com/redirect/60a1059f-2129-4e7d-b065-a2a5a9604cb8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an executive order, obtained by The Washington Post and dubbed "Gold Standard Childhood Vaccine Recommendations," that would divide vaccines into three categories and push for children's immunizations to be administered at separate medical visits rather than in combined doses. The order is expected to be signed as soon as Monday.
* In the draft, vaccines against 11 diseases, including measles, polio, and whooping cough, would remain recommended for all children, while others such as hepatitis A and B, meningococcal disease, influenza, and coronavirus would move to a "shared decision-making" category between parents and doctors.
* The order also calls for developing alternative vaccine adjuvants to aluminum, which some FDA officials have said is not feasible on a practical timeline.
* The move follows a January administration effort to reduce recommended childhood vaccines that a federal judge blocked in March, and dovetails with Trump's reported concerns about the debunked links between vaccines and autism.
* **State Department says it revoked more than 175,000 visas under Trump:** The State Department [said](https://substack.com/redirect/66ea5b09-9007-4e8e-8430-e8ff792eec2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Monday it has revoked more than 175,000 visas from foreign nationals during Trump's second term.
* Most of the visas were rescinded as a result of criminal allegations against their holders, though several visas were rescinded from people accused of celebrating the assassination of right-wing activist **Charlie Kirk** , and others were revoked from people accused of ties to the Cuban and Iranian governments.
* **Rep. Ilhan Omar demands answers after ICE agent found outside her town hall with mismatched plates:** Rep. **Ilhan Omar** [sent](https://substack.com/redirect/b04685f0-31c7-45e6-ab99-548e20d481df?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a letter Friday to a DHS field office after local police discovered an ICE agent sitting outside her Richfield, Minnesota town hall in a car with mismatched license plates, HuffPo reported on Monday, a practice that DHS had claimed was discontinued and which violates state law.
* The Homeland Security Investigations employee said she was conducting an undercover drug operation before a supervisor call led her to leave the scene.
* Omar wrote that the incident "raises serious and uncomfortable questions" and "emphasizes many Americans' growing concern that the Trump administration uses ICE to surveil political opponents."
* **Google co-founder has spent more than $100 million fighting California billionaire tax proposal** : Google co-founder **Sergey Brin** has [donated](https://substack.com/redirect/29bd597e-a95d-4f16-884b-74a08929b4c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an additional $20 million to Build a Better California, bringing his total spending against the state's proposed billionaire tax to more than $100 million, Tech Crunch reported, as he seeks to avoid an estimated $13.3 billion tax payment.
* California's Prop 40 would impose a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of roughly 200 billionaires in the state to help fund healthcare programs.
* Other tech figures including Meta's **Mark Zuckerberg** , former Uber CEO **Travis Kalanick** , and venture capitalist **Peter Thiel** have taken steps to avoid the assessment, though **Jensen Huang** , the co-founder of Nvidia, has said he would be "perfectly fine" paying the tax, which voters will decide on in November.
* **Private intelligence firms selling surveillance dossiers on AI, data center critics:** Private intelligence firms including RANE Network, Kroll, and Liferaft are marketing dossiers and monitoring services on critics of artificial intelligence and data centers, framing grassroots opposition to server farms and AI expansion in counterterrorism-style language, according to documents obtained by The American Prospect.
* RANE offered the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission a tailored assessment of "anti-technology sector sentiment" in March 2025 and later held a webinar warning of threats from protesters including creatives, environmentalists, laid-off workers, and civil liberties advocates.
* The commercial offerings coincide with "anti-tech extremism" memos from federal agencies.
* Read the full report from The American Prospect [here](https://substack.com/redirect/426a569e-d103-4fcf-934c-4eab8f602779?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

* **Pentagon official says U.S. "digging in" to Asia**: **Elbridge Colby** , Undersecretary of Defense for Policy, [said](https://substack.com/redirect/fb682174-b614-439f-bb3e-4d906f457322?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a speech in Manila Monday that the United States is not disengaging from Asia but rather "digging in" to maintain a favorable balance of power in the Indo-Pacific.
* Colby said maintaining a balance of power favorable to the U.S. in the region required a "posture of deterrence by denial" in the area from Japan, through Taiwan and the Philippines, and down to Borneo.
* He also pointed to what he characterized as a growing U.S. military commitment in the region, though he called on U.S. "allies and partners" to increase their defense spending. "We are looking for partners, not protectorates," he said.

# Other International News
* **Over 11,000 more people displaced in Sudan over two days, IOM says:** More than 11,000 people were [displaced](https://substack.com/redirect/a014fdc5-6198-4a61-9daa-22f521767e91?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from villages in Sirba locality, in Sudan's West Darfur near the border with Chad, over two days of escalating fighting between the Sudanese army and the RSF, the UN's International Organization for Migration said on Monday. Most of those displaced crossed into Chad, while others sought refuge around El Geneina, West Darfur's capital.

* **7.4 magnitude earthquake kills at least 111 in western Colombia:** A 7.4 magnitude earthquake [struck](https://substack.com/redirect/abb38f14-f179-4d58-9625-12a21d7dad73?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) western Colombia Monday, killing at least 111 people and damaging roughly 1,600 buildings, including 61 that completely collapsed, according to the Associated Press.
* The earthquake's epicenter was in the Choco region, with destruction reported in the cities of Cali, Pereira, Quibdo, and Manizales.
* Colombia's Geological Service called it the country's strongest quake recorded this century.
* The U.S. State Department announced $15.5 million in emergency aid Monday night, with Mexico, El Salvador, and Chile also offering assistance. The disaster follows two earthquakes that devastated neighboring Venezuela in late June, killing more than 6,300 people.
* **Syrian court sentences Bashar al-Assad, brother to death in absentia:** A Syrian court [sentenced](https://substack.com/redirect/e5a3d6f6-1152-4abd-bb78-462560bd27c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ousted President Bashar al-Assad and his brother Maher, a former commander in the country's military, to death in absentia on Tuesday for crimes against humanity and war crimes committed during Syria's 14-year civil war.
* Judge Fakhareddine al-Aryan, delivering the verdict at Damascus's Fourth Criminal Court in a session aired live on state TV, said Assad "used state agencies to commit war crimes and crimes against humanity," marking the first sentences against Assad or his inner circle since his family's five-decade rule ended 20 months ago.
* The brothers fled to Russia after the government's fall in December 2024 and received asylum there.
* **Libya declares maximum emergency after third drone strike hits largest functioning refinery:** Libya's National Oil Corporation [declared](https://substack.com/redirect/29cd6047-0f96-4ba0-aa67-0be7e26f5259?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a "maximum state of emergency" around the Zawiya refinery, west of Tripoli, after three drone attacks in roughly 48 hours, Anadolu reported. The state oil company warned it could declare force majeure and shut down operations if the attacks continue.
* Monday's strike hit a tank containing an estimated 4.5 million liters of gasoline, igniting a massive fire before the tank collapsed, according to Reuters.
* An early Saturday strike punctured a naphtha tank, causing a contained chemical leak. Another drone struck the complex's desalination plant, damaging its main pipeline and a storage tank.
* Libya's Ambulance and Emergency Service said Tuesday there were no "serious injuries" from the fire, with most patients treated for smoke inhalation.
* No group has claimed responsibility for the attack with the 120,000-barrel-per-day facility repeatedly being caught in fighting between rival armed factions amid the instability that has gripped Libya since the NATO-backed overthrow of Muammar Gaddafi in 2011.
* **Turkish parliament passes limited amnesty bill for PKK militants:** Turkish lawmakers [voted](https://substack.com/redirect/80aef726-f600-4124-890a-0e03749c8c64?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 468-88 on Monday to pass a "terror-free Turkey" law offering limited amnesty to Kurdish PKK fighters who lay down their weapons, the country's first legislative step toward ending decades of conflict.
* The bill comes 18 months after jailed PKK founder Abdullah Ocalan urged his followers to disarm, and was backed by President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan's ruling AKP party and the pro-Kurdish DEM party.
* It suspends prosecutions and sentences for five to 10 years and is expected to lead to the release of about 3,500 PKK-linked detainees in an initial phase, though it excludes those involved in "serious crimes ."
* The law makes no mention of Ocalan's own case. The PKK warned in a Sunday statement that excluding Ocalan would leave many provisions of the bill a "dead letter."
* **Returning Kurds attacked in Syria:** The return of displaced Syrian Kurds to their northeastern hometown of Ras al-Ain was [suspended](https://substack.com/redirect/a7a68c8f-16c8-428b-bda4-f7ce57c9bbef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Monday after a first group of roughly 2,500 returnees was attacked by "armed groups," The New Arab reported.
* A security official in Hasakeh province said several attackers were arrested and trips were "temporarily suspended as a precautionary measure" until safety could be ensured.
* The attack sparked protests in nearby Qamishli, where demonstrators attempted to breach security headquarters.
* Nearly 100,000 people from the Ras al-Ain area have applied to return home since Turkish-backed forces seized the territory from Kurdish control in 2019.
* **Iraq forms new military command to secure southern border after militia attacks on Saudi Arabia** : Iraq has [established](https://substack.com/redirect/6255b306-61a5-4141-a5d9-05c5bb3d745c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Al-Badiya Operations Command to strengthen security in its southern desert border region following attacks by Iran-aligned militias against Saudi Arabia, Iraqi sources told The New Arab on Monday. The move is aimed at preventing Iraqi territory from being used for cross-border strikes or drawing retaliation onto Iraqi soil.
* Military sources said Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered the command after Iraqi intelligence reports identified security gaps that pro-Iranian armed groups exploited to transport drones and launchers through Iraq's Al-Muthanna desert.
* Saudi Arabia struck targets in Iraq it said were linked to attacks on its oil facilities in late July.
* **Russia 's top court bars antiwar Yabloko party from parliamentary elections: ** Russia's Supreme Court [ruled](https://substack.com/redirect/3d1113b2-5c42-4fda-a702-1ba131f90383?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Monday to bar Yabloko, the only officially registered party opposing Moscow's war in Ukraine, from next month's parliamentary elections. The pro-Kremlin nationalist party Rodina had filed suit alleging Yabloko received undeclared campaign support, including from Western sources.
* Yabloko leader Nikolai Rybakov called the case an "unconstitutional attack on freedom of thought" and said the party would appeal, as about 100 supporters gathered outside the courthouse.
* The party has been backed by exiled opposition figures including Yulia Navalnaya, the widow of assassinated Russian opposition leader Alexei Navalny. It was polling at just 3% earlier this year, short of the 5% threshold needed to win seats.
* **Seven Uzbek citizens killed in drone attack on Russia 's Tatarstan region**: Seven Uzbek citizens were among those [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/6d5c2502-7c69-4cce-b3f4-2fb0edf5aac7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a drone attack in Russia's Tatarstan region Monday, the Uzbek consulate in Kazan said. The Ukrainian attacks in the region killed 13 people on Monday.
* Between two and three million Uzbek citizens work in Russia, with Uzbekistan's economy partly reliant on remittances from migrant workers.

Photo by Mahmud Turkia / AFP via Getty Images. Tuesday, August 11, 2026 - New traffic plan for Hormuz. U.S. President Donald Trump claims the Strait of Hormuz is open and under full U.S. control. Wall Street Journal: U.S. fires on ship in the Gulf of Oman. Iran accuses U.S. of "compulsive addiction to sanctions" after Treasury threat. Trump demands "compensation" from Iran, cites USS Cole attack carried out by Al-Qaeda. Four crew members killed in Bab Al-Mandab. Saudi Arabia's Jizan refinery closed until end of month. Israel continues its assault on the occupied West Bank with 504 attacks in one week. Israeli government greenlights "Green Rafah". Israel is keeping the bodies of Palestinians to use as bargaining chips. Former UN official says body must "clean house." Private intelligence firms selling surveillance dossiers on AI, data center critics. Pentagon official says U.S. "digging in" to Asia.
