Authors Eli Clifton and Ian Lustick join Ryan Grim and Murtaza Hussain live at 7pm ET, your questions answered on the spot. Paid subscriber exclusive. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran New traffic plan for Hormuz: Iran and Oman agreed on a basic traffic plan for a safe shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Foreign Ministry on Monday, stressing that the route remains closed as long as the U.S. continues its attacks and maintains its blockade. Technical points are still under discussion. Regarding the issue of charging ships for transiting the Strait, spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said that Iran would "naturally" assess charges for the "services" it renders, though no decision was announced on the matter. Talks with the U.S. are still not happening. "We are not having negotiations with the United States," Baghaei insisted. "Exchanging messages is natural and occurs through intermediaries," but Tehran's immediate focus, he maintained, remains the negotiations with Oman. Qatar backed up Iran's reports of an impending deal. Majed Al-Ansari, a spokesperson for the Qatari Foreign Ministry, on Tuesday that negotiations between Oman and Iran on the future of shipping in the Strait of Hormuz had reached an "advanced stage" and were at a "critical juncture." Al-Ansari said Qatar's focus, as a mediator to the U.S.-Iran talks, is the opening of the waterway "at the earliest opportunity." Trump claims the Strait is open and under full U.S. control: U.S. President Donald Trump in the Oval Office on Monday that the U.S. had swept the entire Strait of Hormuz of mines, and that it was "open" and "100%" under U.S. control. WSJ: U.S. fires on ship in the Gulf of Oman: U.S. forces on a Panama-flagged vessel early Tuesday after it reportedly attempted to bypass Washington's naval blockade of Iranian ports, according to the Wall Street Journal. Maritime security firm Vanguard separately reported that the Panama-flagged container ship Vela Nova was struck by a missile fired from a helicopter while traveling westbound through the Gulf of Oman, about 71 nautical miles off Pakistan, sparking a fire that was later extinguished. All 17 crew members were accounted for, with no immediate reports of casualties. Iran accuses U.S. of "compulsive addiction to sanctions" after Treasury threat: Baghaei, Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson, criticized renewed U.S. sanctions threats on Tuesday after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent spoke of "suffocating" Iran through economic pressure. In a on X, Baghaei charged Washington of a "compulsive addiction to sanctions," arguing that the U.S. turns to sanctions whenever it is "incapable of pursuing diplomacy" and escalates them when they fail to produce results. "This is no longer 'policy'--it is 'habit,'" he wrote, warning that U.S. officials risk undermining their "remaining chances" of finding a way out of the current crisis. Trump demands "compensation" from Iran, cites USS Cole attack carried out by Al-Qaeda: Responding to Iran's demand for compensation for damage inflicted during the U.S.-Israeli war that began on February 28, Trump said Monday that Washington would likewise demand "compensation" from Tehran for U.S. soldiers and Iranian protesters he says Iran has killed, including the families of those killed in the USS Cole attack, which was carried out by Al-Qaeda. "Now I am likewise demanding compensation from Iran, for all of the people that they have killed and gravely wounded with their roadside bombs and many conflicts," Trump on Truth Social, also citing "thousands" killed in combat. Trump added that Iran "should be responsible for the damages and death caused to the people of Lebanon, Syria, Yemen, and Gaza." Trump claimed that 52,000 protesters had been killed in Iran over the past five months, raising his previous figure of 32,000 and far exceeding the roughly 7,000 deaths verified by HRANA and 5,000 verified by a UN special rapporteur. Khamenei shuffles military leadership: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei decrees formally appointing six senior commanders across Iran's armed forces, the IRGC, and the Basij, consolidating a wartime command structure that had operated on an interim basis for months, according to Al Jazeera and The National. Khamenei named Ahmad Vahidi the IRGC commander-in-chief. His predecessor was killed on February 28. He tapped Hossein Taeb to head the Basij, a paramilitary volunteer force operating under Iran's IRGC. Yemen Four crew members killed in Bab Al-Mandab: Four crew members were in a suspected Ansarallah attack on the Egyptian-owned cargo vessel Tihamah in the Bab Al-Mandab Strait on Tuesday, Reuters reported. Ansarallah has not claimed responsibility for the attack. Saudi 's Jizan refinery closed until end of month: Saudi Aramco the reopening of its Jizan refinery to August 30, after a second Ansarallah attack hit the facility, Reuters reported. Jizan, which produces 400,000 barrels of petroleum per day, particularly gasoline and diesel, has been struck twice since late July. It was anticipated to restart production on August 15 before a strike on Sunday. Palestine Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, one Palestinian was killed after succumbing to wounds sustained in earlier attacks, and one was injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,387 killed, with 174,257 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,259 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 4,146, while 807 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble. Israel continues its assault on the occupied West Bank with 504 attacks in one week: Israeli forces and settlers continue to escalate attacks on the occupied West Bank, with 504 reported attacks in the past week alone, according to the Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission. Hebron: Israeli authorities the demolition of an elementary school and several homes in Masafer Yatta on Tuesday, WAFA reported. In the Bedouin community of Yatta, Israeli forces a Palestinian house and filled in a water well. Ramallah: An Israeli attack on the village of Al-Mughayyir six Palestinians on Tuesday, two of whom were women and three of whom were children, with Israeli forces firing tear gas on the village inhabitants as they plowed their fields, according to WAFA. Jenin : Israeli authorities summarily 12 warehouses in Anza on Tuesday, WAFA reported. On Monday, an Israeli military court Ata Rmeilat-Abu Rmeileh, a 67-year-old Fatah official from Jenin, to 42 months in prison and fined him more than $1,650, after detaining him without charge for nearly 3 years and with his health deteriorating. Nablus : Israeli forces six Palestinians during an incursion into Burqa on Tuesday morning, two of whom were children. In Tal, Israeli forces conducted a raid on Monday before the home of Farouq Ramadan, a Palestinian who, while being attacked late last month, grabbed a settler's gun before being shot dead by Israeli settlers. East Jerusalem: The Jerusalem Governorate announced on Tuesday plans by Israeli authorities to 650 new settlement units on 27 dunums of land in East Jerusalem near Umm Tuba. Israeli government greenlights "Green Rafah": Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz quietly infrastructure work for "Green Rafah," a residential zone on the Israeli-controlled side of Gaza's Yellow Line, Israeli Army Radio reported on Monday. Netanyahu's office has advertised "Green Rafah" as a pilot project backed by the UAE and has said it would offer temporary housing to Palestinians "free" of Hamas' influence. Palestinian workers at the site will be subject to intense Shin Bet scrutiny, and strict rules have been announced for residences at the site. Drop Site previously reported on plans for a "residential" zone for Palestinians in Rafah that would contain and control its residents through biometric surveillance, checkpoints, monitoring of purchases, and more. Israel is holding the bodies of 1,700 Palestinians to use as bargaining chips: Israel is the remains of approximately 1,700 Palestinians for possible use in future exchanges, Haaretz reported, citing two security sources, despite no Israelis being held captive by Palestinian resistance groups. Shin Bet chief David Zini and the Israeli military reportedly support retaining the bodies in case Israelis are captured or disappear in the future. Many of the bodies are held in freezers in military facilities. At least 13 of the bodies are of Palestinian citizens of Israel, the paper noted. Former UN official says body must "clean house": Former UN human rights official Craig Mokhiber on Monday that the UN must "clean house" after a Drop Site revealed senior UNICEF official Yahav Lichner repeatedly shared confidential UN information with Israeli officials during his time at the UN Population Fund in 2014 and 2015. Lichner later served as a senior aide to Sigrid Kaag while she coordinated Gaza aid. Kaag subsequently led the UN presence in Palestine and now sits on the executive board of the U.S.-Israeli "Board of Peace." Lichner was placed on administrative leave following the publication of Drop Site's investigation. MSF doctor discusses malnutrition in Gaza: James Smith, a doctor for Doctors Without Borders (Medecins sans Frontieres) working in Gaza, described the "slow and cumulative effect of...manufactured deprivation" in the Strip to the UK's Channel 4 on Monday, as Israel continues to restrict the entry of life essentials into Gaza. "Every month still, approximately 3,000 children are being admitted into acute malnutrition programs," Smith noted. His full interview is available . VIDEO: The family of 13-year-old girl killed in Khan Younis: Drop Site contributor Mohamed Ahmed spoke with relatives of Saba Al-Hashash, a 13-year-old Palestinian girl killed in Khan Younis on Saturday. "Last Thursday was the anniversary of her sister's death, and today the second sister was martyred," one told Ahmed. Al-Hashash's mother said her daughter was shot as she went to recite the Quran. "Everyone in the mosque was a child, no older than 15, along with their teacher," she told Drop Site. "Why target children? Don't they know where they're shooting?" Watch Ahmed 's video reports and . Lebanon Israel strikes ambulance, wounds two, and sets fire to fields in southern Lebanon despite ceasefire: Israeli forces to fields and orchards in Sarda and Wazzani in the Marjayoun district on Tuesday, Lebanon's National News Agency (NNA) reported. In Nabatieh, Israeli drones explosive and incendiary materials around the General Security center, the Imam Ali Mosque and the vicinity of the Lebanese army barracks in Nabatieh Al-Fawqa, igniting fires that were later extinguished by Civil Defense and local firefighting teams. A separate Israeli drone strike in Nabatieh two people, according to Lebanon's Health Ministry. The ministry said Israel struck the area a second time after an ambulance crew from the Al-Rissala Association arrived to assist the wounded, damaging the ambulance. U.S. News Primaries in six states, including Wisconsin, Minnesota, and South Carolina: Progressive Francesca Hong , a chef and state lawmaker,** faces Milwaukee County executive David Crowley in Wisconsin's Democratic gubernatorial primary. Hong, a member of the Democratic Socialists of America, is the frontrunner in the race, despite party efforts to back several of her opponents, including former Lt. Gov. Mandela Barnes , who dropped out two weeks before the election, and current Lt. Gov Sara Rodriguez , who dropped out earlier. In Minnesota, Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan and Rep. Angie Craig are vying for the Democratic nomination to replace outgoing Sen. Tina Smith. Craig, who has received the endorsement of Sen. Bernie Sanders , holds a narrow lead over Flanagan, whose career-long support from AIPAC has complicated her more recent votes for resolutions blocking weapons funding to Israel. In the race to replace Craig, progressives Matt Little , a former state senator, and Kaela Berg face Matt Klein , a pro-Israel physician who has received over $2.5 million from 314 Action, which supports scientists and doctors running for public office and sometimes operates as an AIPAC cut-out. Drop Site 's Julian Andreone and Ryan Grim wrote about this race . Ten Republicans in South Carolina are running to replace the late Sen. Lindsey Graham , including his sister Darline Graham , who Gov. Henry McMaster appointed to complete her deceased brother's term, and who received Trump's endorsement in the primary. Reps. Russell Fry and Ralph Norman are also seeking the nomination, along with former South Carolina Gov. Mark Sanford and businessman Mark Lynch. A majority in the primary is needed to avoid a late August runoff. Lynch, who previously challenged Graham, is running as the only candidate to reject AIPAC money. Trump administration prepares executive order to overhaul childhood vaccine schedule: The Trump administration is an executive order, obtained by The Washington Post and dubbed "Gold Standard Childhood Vaccine Recommendations," that would divide vaccines into three categories and push for children's immunizations to be administered at separate medical visits rather than in combined doses. The order is expected to be signed as soon as Monday. In the draft, vaccines against 11 diseases, including measles, polio, and whooping cough, would remain recommended for all children, while others such as hepatitis A and B, meningococcal disease, influenza, and coronavirus would move to a "shared decision-making" category between parents and doctors. The order also calls for developing alternative vaccine adjuvants to aluminum, which some FDA officials have said is not feasible on a practical timeline. The move follows a January administration effort to reduce recommended childhood vaccines that a federal judge blocked in March, and dovetails with Trump's reported concerns about the debunked links between vaccines and autism. State Department says it revoked more than 175,000 visas under Trump: The State Department Monday it has revoked more than 175,000 visas from foreign nationals during Trump's second term. Most of the visas were rescinded as a result of criminal allegations against their holders, though several visas were rescinded from people accused of celebrating the assassination of right-wing activist Charlie Kirk , and others were revoked from people accused of ties to the Cuban and Iranian governments. Rep. Ilhan Omar demands answers after ICE agent found outside her town hall with mismatched plates: Rep. Ilhan Omar a letter Friday to a DHS field office after local police discovered an ICE agent sitting outside her Richfield, Minnesota town hall in a car with mismatched license plates, HuffPo reported on Monday, a practice that DHS had claimed was discontinued and which violates state law. The Homeland Security Investigations employee said she was conducting an undercover drug operation before a supervisor call led her to leave the scene. Omar wrote that the incident "raises serious and uncomfortable questions" and "emphasizes many Americans' growing concern that the Trump administration uses ICE to surveil political opponents." Google co-founder has spent more than $100 million fighting California billionaire tax proposal : Google co-founder Sergey Brin has an additional $20 million to Build a Better California, bringing his total spending against the state's proposed billionaire tax to more than $100 million, Tech Crunch reported, as he seeks to avoid an estimated $13.3 billion tax payment. California's Prop 40 would impose a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of roughly 200 billionaires in the state to help fund healthcare programs. Other tech figures including Meta's Mark Zuckerberg , former Uber CEO Travis Kalanick , and venture capitalist Peter Thiel have taken steps to avoid the assessment, though Jensen Huang , the co-founder of Nvidia, has said he would be "perfectly fine" paying the tax, which voters will decide on in November. Private intelligence firms selling surveillance dossiers on AI, data center critics: Private intelligence firms including RANE Network, Kroll, and Liferaft are marketing dossiers and monitoring services on critics of artificial intelligence and data centers, framing grassroots opposition to server farms and AI expansion in counterterrorism-style language, according to documents obtained by The American Prospect. RANE offered the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission a tailored assessment of "anti-technology sector sentiment" in March 2025 and later held a webinar warning of threats from protesters including creatives, environmentalists, laid-off workers, and civil liberties advocates. The commercial offerings coincide with "anti-tech extremism" memos from federal agencies. Read the full report from The American Prospect . Pentagon official says U.S. "digging in" to Asia: Elbridge Colby , Undersecretary of Defense for Policy, in a speech in Manila Monday that the United States is not disengaging from Asia but rather "digging in" to maintain a favorable balance of power in the Indo-Pacific. Colby said maintaining a balance of power favorable to the U.S. in the region required a "posture of deterrence by denial" in the area from Japan, through Taiwan and the Philippines, and down to Borneo. He also pointed to what he characterized as a growing U.S. military commitment in the region, though he called on U.S. "allies and partners" to increase their defense spending. "We are looking for partners, not protectorates," he said. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Over 11,000 more people displaced in Sudan over two days, IOM says: More than 11,000 people were from villages in Sirba locality, in Sudan's West Darfur near the border with Chad, over two days of escalating fighting between the Sudanese army and the RSF, the UN's International Organization for Migration said on Monday. Most of those displaced crossed into Chad, while others sought refuge around El Geneina, West Darfur's capital. 7.4 magnitude earthquake kills at least 111 in western Colombia: A 7.4 magnitude earthquake western Colombia Monday, killing at least 111 people and damaging roughly 1,600 buildings, including 61 that completely collapsed, according to the Associated Press. The earthquake's epicenter was in the Choco region, with destruction reported in the cities of Cali, Pereira, Quibdo, and Manizales. Colombia's Geological Service called it the country's strongest quake recorded this century. The U.S. State Department announced $15.5 million in emergency aid Monday night, with Mexico, El Salvador, and Chile also offering assistance. The disaster follows two earthquakes that devastated neighboring Venezuela in late June, killing more than 6,300 people. Syrian court sentences Bashar al-Assad, brother to death in absentia: A Syrian court ousted President Bashar al-Assad and his brother Maher, a former commander in the country's military, to death in absentia on Tuesday for crimes against humanity and war crimes committed during Syria's 14-year civil war. Judge Fakhareddine al-Aryan, delivering the verdict at Damascus's Fourth Criminal Court in a session aired live on state TV, said Assad "used state agencies to commit war crimes and crimes against humanity," marking the first sentences against Assad or his inner circle since his family's five-decade rule ended 20 months ago. The brothers fled to Russia after the government's fall in December 2024 and received asylum there. Libya declares maximum emergency after third drone strike hits largest functioning refinery: Libya's National Oil Corporation a "maximum state of emergency" around the Zawiya refinery, west of Tripoli, after three drone attacks in roughly 48 hours, Anadolu reported. The state oil company warned it could declare force majeure and shut down operations if the attacks continue. Monday's strike hit a tank containing an estimated 4.5 million liters of gasoline, igniting a massive fire before the tank collapsed, according to Reuters. An early Saturday strike punctured a naphtha tank, causing a contained chemical leak. Another drone struck the complex's desalination plant, damaging its main pipeline and a storage tank. Libya's Ambulance and Emergency Service said Tuesday there were no "serious injuries" from the fire, with most patients treated for smoke inhalation. No group has claimed responsibility for the attack with the 120,000-barrel-per-day facility repeatedly being caught in fighting between rival armed factions amid the instability that has gripped Libya since the NATO-backed overthrow of Muammar Gaddafi in 2011. Turkish parliament passes limited amnesty bill for PKK militants: Turkish lawmakers 468-88 on Monday to pass a "terror-free Turkey" law offering limited amnesty to Kurdish PKK fighters who lay down their weapons, the country's first legislative step toward ending decades of conflict. The bill comes 18 months after jailed PKK founder Abdullah Ocalan urged his followers to disarm, and was backed by President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan's ruling AKP party and the pro-Kurdish DEM party. It suspends prosecutions and sentences for five to 10 years and is expected to lead to the release of about 3,500 PKK-linked detainees in an initial phase, though it excludes those involved in "serious crimes ." The law makes no mention of Ocalan's own case. The PKK warned in a Sunday statement that excluding Ocalan would leave many provisions of the bill a "dead letter." Returning Kurds attacked in Syria: The return of displaced Syrian Kurds to their northeastern hometown of Ras al-Ain was Monday after a first group of roughly 2,500 returnees was attacked by "armed groups," The New Arab reported. A security official in Hasakeh province said several attackers were arrested and trips were "temporarily suspended as a precautionary measure" until safety could be ensured. The attack sparked protests in nearby Qamishli, where demonstrators attempted to breach security headquarters. Nearly 100,000 people from the Ras al-Ain area have applied to return home since Turkish-backed forces seized the territory from Kurdish control in 2019. Iraq forms new military command to secure southern border after militia attacks on Saudi Arabia : Iraq has the Al-Badiya Operations Command to strengthen security in its southern desert border region following attacks by Iran-aligned militias against Saudi Arabia, Iraqi sources told The New Arab on Monday. The move is aimed at preventing Iraqi territory from being used for cross-border strikes or drawing retaliation onto Iraqi soil. Military sources said Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered the command after Iraqi intelligence reports identified security gaps that pro-Iranian armed groups exploited to transport drones and launchers through Iraq's Al-Muthanna desert. Saudi Arabia struck targets in Iraq it said were linked to attacks on its oil facilities in late July. Russia 's top court bars antiwar Yabloko party from parliamentary elections: Russia's Supreme Court Monday to bar Yabloko, the only officially registered party opposing Moscow's war in Ukraine, from next month's parliamentary elections. The pro-Kremlin nationalist party Rodina had filed suit alleging Yabloko received undeclared campaign support, including from Western sources. Yabloko leader Nikolai Rybakov called the case an "unconstitutional attack on freedom of thought" and said the party would appeal, as about 100 supporters gathered outside the courthouse. The party has been backed by exiled opposition figures including Yulia Navalnaya, the widow of assassinated Russian opposition leader Alexei Navalny. It was polling at just 3% earlier this year, short of the 5% threshold needed to win seats. Seven Uzbek citizens killed in drone attack on Russia 's Tatarstan region: Seven Uzbek citizens were among those in a drone attack in Russia's Tatarstan region Monday, the Uzbek consulate in Kazan said. The Ukrainian attacks in the region killed 13 people on Monday. | Peter,
This year, voters have a simple, moral choice.
Peace or war? Love or hate? Dignity or cruelty? Equality or segregation? Integrity or corruption?
Are we a nation that makes sure everyone has the basics required to live a life of liberty and truly ensures justice for all, or are we going to keep feeding this rigged system that creates classes of haves and have-nots?
I believe God is Love, and I doubt God is thrilled about the homelessness, bombs, illness, suffering, starvation, and incarceration of innocent people.
We say "WWJD," but I have to ask: Who would Jesus bomb, detain, or refuse healthcare to because their insurance provider doesn't want to cover them? Because the MAGA Extremists cloak themselves in faith, but then behave in such an evil, amoral way.
My Trump-backed opponent voted to strip people of their healthcare. She says that a president named in the Epstein files is the greatest president we have ever had. She voted to send more money overseas to foreign wars while cutting aid to starving children abroad?
What are we doing here?
I am a Christian, and I believe that Jesus would advocate for healthcare, livable wages, housing and shelter, care for the elderly, and schools that serve the needs of all children.
My name is Jamie Davis. I am a third-generation row-crop farmer who farms the same Delta soil my grandparents farmed as sharecroppers, and I'm the Democrat running for Senate in Louisiana against a Trump-backed opponent. We won the primary by a landslide and have outraised the opposition, but we need your help.
[Please rush what you can, $5, $10, $15, or $50, so that we can remind MAGA what real Christian values look like. **We have to fix what’s broken in Washington DC, and electing Roy in North Carolina is CRITICAL to making that happen.

Look, we always knew this was going to be a tough fight – no matter who our opponent was. With MI-08 being named the “tipping point” for control of the House by election experts, we know MAGA will be doing _everything_ they can to flip this seat.
And they’ve already started. The National Republican Congressional Committee (NRCC) has committed $2.5 million towards this race. | | _“Mark Warner here. My friend Tom Perriello is running for Congress to flip Virginia’s Fifth District, and I wanted to make sure you saw his message below:”_ Derek,

At this point in life, I do not get goosebumps as often, or butterflies in my stomach.

But with the start of the general election here in Virginia, my heart and soul tapped in my body to remind me how special it is to ask for people’s vote, to get that vote, and to earn a nomination to represent hundreds of thousands of people in Congress.

I am truly grateful that tens of thousands of people across 24 counties believed in me and in this campaign enough to do their part. I am proud of the fact that voters in all 24 counties and municipalities of this district voted overwhelmingly to make me the Democratic nominee. And I was particularly moved to see our watch party dominated by young people determined to reclaim their district, their democracy, and their future.

For me, this mission is not the nomination. It is not just reclaiming VA-5 for the people who live here. It is a project of reclamation and reimagining. **In the shadows of the Blue Ridge where I was born and raised, in the seat first held by James Madison, we must meet this moment of defending the best of our past and dreaming of an even better future.**

Like generations of Americans before us, we must protect our defining aspirations of a more perfect Union, of an inalienable right to life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness. And, like the generation of young people driving this campaign’s energy, we must dare to look beyond the constraints of stale politics to meet this moment of AI and emerging powers. We must face down the attacks on our Constitution and communities, and also set a new North Star of an American dream that leaves no region, race or generation behind.

Since I launched this campaign, I've sat down for more than 500 listening sessions across this region. In living rooms, union halls, and church basements, on stoops and sidewalks, at county fairs and homecomings, I have heard the same refrain. A harmony of sorts. People want to get costs down, paychecks up, and common sense back to DC. They also want a system that treats humans with dignity and decency, and they want the powerful to play by the same rules as everyone else.

**Nobody I meet expects the folks in Washington to solve every problem in their life. But they have EVERY right to a representative who doesn't go and make things worse.**

Folks around here want a representative who fights for us. They are sick of sell-outs who let dark money donors tell them what to do. McGuire has clearly broken that trust, and busted the wallets of so many families in the district. But voters want more and deserve more than a chance to fire John McGuire. They need a real alternative — a fighter who cares more about right and wrong than right and left and is not afraid to stand up for it.

_You have given the people of Virginia’s Fifth that alternative. I take this nomination as a mission. As a sacred chance to restore faith in our democracy, return our Constitutional freedoms and common sense, and reimagine an American dream for an era that will be dominated by AI._

_As a good friend noted to me recently, the path to freedom passes through this district. The path back to sanity passes through this district. The path to hope rooted in reality passes through this district._

**I know we can do it, because I've won this seat before by spending time in every precinct and outperforming in every nook and cranny of the district. This time, against a much weaker and more extreme opponent, we already have the momentum. But we cannot rest.**

body:
Let's keep the momentum going
---
| |
---
Our home has been overlooked as "too red to bother" for decades. But last week, the National Democratic party posted about our hard-fought wins multiple times.
---
|
---
They're right to pay attention and celebrate these victories. We flipped the Knox County school board to a Democratic majority when Brandy Jenkins flipped D9 in South Knox, typically thought of as a Republican stronghold. And commissioner-elect Brandon Huckaby flipped a commission seat with a campaign focused on affordability and infrastructure. Of course, last Thursday, we had some disappointing losses, too. But here's the map I can't stop thinking about:
---
|
---
Map source: Don Johnson. Data sources: Knox county election commission 2026 (unofficial), TN Secretary of State (2024 Presidential election by precinct).
---
**In TN-02 's biggest county, nearly every single precinct shifted blue from the 2024 presidential election.** The suburbs, the rural areas, the places too many people have overlooked as unshiftable and unwinnable. We accomplished that with a strong ground game and talking to our neighbors about what we'll work for when given the chance. Healthcare we can afford. A government that represents us, not just the wealthy and well-connected. Infrastructure investments in our region. name: Han Jones
subject: Virginians need to see this before they vote
body:
https://va4reprofreedom.org/ [https://va4reprofreedom.org/]
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/vaforrepro-em?refcode=081126 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/vaforrepro-em?refcode=081126]
Friend, on November 3, you will have an opportunity to make history by voting YES on 1 to enshrine reproductive freedom into Virginia’s Constitution.
Advocates, health care providers, community leaders, volunteers and those from every corner of Virginia from every corner of the state have worked tirelessly to bring us to this historic moment.
We’ve shared personal stories, knocked on doors, organized in our communities, countered misinformation from extremists, and rallied support among family, friends, and neighbors.
With this crucial vote just a couple of months away, we’ve created this video to reach even more Virginians and explain why a YES vote on 1 will have a life-changing impact on generations to come.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-m38gEj6ZME [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-m38gEj6ZME]
>>Watch the video and learn why this vote is so important>> [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-m38gEj6ZME]
If we win in November, it means Virginians for generations to come will have the right to reproductive health care, including abortion, birth control, and fertility care in our state.
But history is made by the people who show up and fight in whatever way they can.
SPREAD OUR MESSAGE - YES ON 1 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/vaforrepro-em?refcode=081126]
Whether it’s watching and sharing this video [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-m38gEj6ZME] , talking with family and friends about what’s at stake on November 3, volunteering in your community [https://www.mobilize.us/va4reprofreedom/] , or making a contribution [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/vaforrepro-em?refcode=081126] to help us reach more voters, every action helps strengthen our fight for reproductive freedom in Virginia.
Thank you for being part of our history-making campaign!
In gratitude,
Han Jones
Campaign Manager
P.S. Please watch our video [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-m38gEj6ZME] and share it with your family, friends, and neighbors. And please make a contribution today [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/vaforrepro-em?refcode=081126] to help fuel our powerful movement in the critical weeks ahead.
Visit our website [https://va4reprofreedom.org/]
Virginians for Reproductive Freedom
600 Pennsylvania Ave SE Unit 15845
Washington, DC 20003

subject: Tim Walz Has Hit the Wall
body:
Last September, Tim Walz launched a bid for an unprecedented third term. Four months later, as MN's fraud scandals kept multiplying, he abandoned

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/d885530135f9/the-briefing-from-mpbc-13062119?e=baf210d431)

| | | | |

|
---
| | Dear MPBC Member, Last September, Tim Walz launched a bid for an unprecedented third term. Four months later, as Minnesota's fraud scandals kept multiplying, he abandoned it. This week, _The Wall Street Journal_ ran [**my column**](https://us.list-manage.com/r6aBMdrOI9V?e=baf210d431&c2id=93c61d534406ea5269257c101c1d1f83) on what that says about where Minnesota has been — and where it can go next. Minnesota used to be a state other states tried to copy: world-class companies, strong schools, safe communities, a broad middle class. The last eight years have cost us that reputation. The 2020 riots caused more than $500 million in damage and exposed a government that couldn't guarantee the most basic promise it makes to residents: public order. The damage hasn't faded — the state recorded 170 murders in 2024, up 45% from 2019. Then came the fraud. Feeding Our Future alone diverted roughly $250 million meant for feeding hungry kids. Investigators have since found suspected fraud in Medicaid, autism services and housing aid. Minnesota's own acting U.S. attorney put the state's total fraud exposure north of $9 billion. The economic numbers complete the picture: 2.8% job growth here since 2018, versus 7% nationally. One of the heaviest state and local tax burdens in the country. And in 2023, one-party rule in St. Paul spent through a $17 billion surplus and put the state on track for a deficit approaching $6 billion. None of that is abstract. It shows up in the decisions of every entrepreneur, family business and employer trying to build something here. But I remain genuinely optimistic. I spend my time with the Minnesotans actually running this state's economy — entrepreneurs, farmers, doctors, manufacturers, engineers who show up and build, election cycle after election cycle. That Minnesota is bigger and better than the headlines. Tim Walz leaves office in January with the worst approval rating of his tenure. Democrats have endorsed Sen. Amy Klobuchar to succeed him, and she's already distancing herself from his handling of the fraud scandals. The real question isn't whether the next governor sounds different. It's whether Minnesota demands a government that acts different. Minnesota's fall is recent. It isn't permanent. [**Read the full column: “Tim Walz Has Hit the Wall”**](https://us.list-manage.com/hSKDi7Blspf?e=baf210d431&c2id=93c61d534406ea5269257c101c1d1f83) Working with you, **Jim Schultz** President & CEOMinnesota Private Business Council **P.S.** For $100 a year, you stop watching from the sidelines.****[**Main Street Members of the Minnesota Private Business Council**](https://us.list-manage.com/_rMAL4wS2fu?e=baf210d431&c2id=93c61d534406ea5269257c101c1d1f83)**** get real-time alerts on legislation, insider polling on Minnesota's political landscape, and principled advocacy showing up in St. Paul when you can't.**** That's less than $10 a month to be part of the organized private-sector counterweight this state desperately needs — at the exact moment it needs it most.****[**Join MPBC here**](https://us.list-manage.com/uRnM9zpKDF1?e=baf210d431&c2id=93c61d534406ea5269257c101c1d1f83)**.**

body:
Kamala is right. What happens here decides whether MAGA gets away with the assault on the rights of black voters in this state and across the nation.
| | | | | [](https://wkfbo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001LhGq1sy2XIUTYOTgSkcMbGU9GfZru6_aOE64_feImHVCZmW6tUk9BdYfxxKDYBrIiB-FXU5NgCuqkq1mwXPh_H7TQv2yAZUlrZbRXEcYhny_ZmWwrqQTfvRl62eunPovy2to_rr3NLbcS20y7_o3Sre7iqY_tV6gULOjaa8LBWsPimUrEtLE8jQPN93qgprPkYDVd9vuqouvzysBsKJ_f3rbdNFjQp7d&c=eujp2z8JMmZ9AjAp2MKCiDsHkpT_lqxLOcc8cSNo7bNX2GP5e8Hxng==&ch=SEqg6SsENFCL2kFjyPR2lMoFSDFq9Vy1QsvE7X4PlhhRKbDBcZ_SlA==)
---
|
Peter,
Things looked bleak.
The Supreme Court gutted the Voting Rights Act. MAGA Governor Jeff Landry canceled our congressional elections to jam through a map that erased one of our majority-Black districts.
But then something happened that MAGA didn't see coming. Louisiana rose up and fought back. In May, voters rejected every single Landry-backed constitutional amendment by double digits. GOP Senator Bill Cassidy became the first incumbent senator in 14 years to lose his own primary.
So we hit the road to keep the momentum going.
We launched No More Silence: Road to the Polls, an 18-city tour to register voters, recruit No Party voters, and make sure every Louisianian knows how, when, and where to vote. The tour ended this weekend at our annual Masquerade Sneaker Ball, where Vice President Kamala Harris took the stage.
---
| | [](https://wkfbo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001LhGq1sy2XIUTYOTgSkcMbGU9GfZru6_aOE64_feImHVCZmW6tUk9BdYfxxKDYBrIiB-FXU5NgCuqkq1mwXPh_H7TQv2yAZUlrZbRXEcYhny_ZmWwrqQTfvRl62eunPovy2to_rr3NLbcS20y7_o3Sre7iqY_tV6gULOjaa8LBWsPimUrEtLE8jQPN93qgprPkYDVd9vuqouA8sC9XiXDjKyMfS3w_Q63&c=eujp2z8JMmZ9AjAp2MKCiDsHkpT_lqxLOcc8cSNo7bNX2GP5e8Hxng==&ch=SEqg6SsENFCL2kFjyPR2lMoFSDFq9Vy1QsvE7X4PlhhRKbDBcZ_SlA==)
---
"Louisiana, you are ground zero," she told the crowd.
Kamala is right. What happens here decides whether or not MAGA gets away with a brazen assault on the rights of black voters in this state and across the nation. What they can get away with here, they will ship across the country.
And Kamala did not mince words about what it will take to stop them. Democrats need to get comfortable with what she called "a certain kind of ruthlessness." Not cruelty, she was careful to say. But the kind that refuses to back down from injustice.
That's why our fight is so important not just Louisiana, but for Democrats everywhere. We have just 85 days until the midterm elections. We need to knock doors. We need to call voters. We need to register voters. We need to turn this energy into the largest blue wave Louisiana has ever seen.
[If you believe in fighting back against the injustice MAGA is unleashing across the nation with a ruthlessness that meets this moment, we cannot do this without you. Can we count on you to rush a donation of $50, $25, or whatever you can spare to help build an unprecedented blue wave in Louisiana?](https://wkfbo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001LhGq1sy2XIUTYOTgSkcMbGU9GfZru6_aOE64_feImHVCZmW6tUk9BdYfxxKDYBrIiB-FXU5NgCuqkq1mwXPh_H7TQv2yAZUlrZbRXEcYhny_ZmWwrqQTfvRl62eunPovy2to_rr3NLbcS20y7_o3Sre7iqY_tV6gULOjaa8LBWsPimUrEtLE8jQPN93qgprPkYDVd9vuqotQN0K6mwXXsVRP8HN75CbY&c=eujp2z8JMmZ9AjAp2MKCiDsHkpT_lqxLOcc8cSNo7bNX2GP5e8Hxng==&ch=SEqg6SsENFCL2kFjyPR2lMoFSDFq9Vy1QsvE7X4PlhhRKbDBcZ_SlA==)

What happens here decides whether MAGA gets away with the assault on the rights of black voters in this state and across the nation. | | | | | == | Peter, Things looked bleak. The Supreme Court gutted the Voting Rights Act. MAGA Governor Jeff Landry canceled our congressional elections to jam through a map that erased one of our majority-Black districts. But then something happened that MAGA didn't see coming. Louisiana rose up and fought back. In May, voters rejected every single Landry-backed constitutional amendment by double digits. GOP Senator Bill Cassidy became the first incumbent senator in 14 years to lose his own primary. So we hit the road to keep the momentum going. We launched No More Silence: Road to the Polls, an 18-city tour to register voters, recruit No Party voters, and make sure every Louisianian knows how, when, and where to vote. The tour ended this weekend at our annual Masquerade Sneaker Ball, where Vice President Kamala Harris took the stage. | | == "Louisiana, you are ground zero," she told the crowd. Kamala is right. What happens here decides whether or not MAGA gets away with a brazen assault on the rights of black voters in this state and across the nation. What they can get away with here, they will ship across the country. And Kamala did not mince words about what it will take to stop them. Democrats need to get comfortable with what she called "a certain kind of ruthlessness." Not cruelty, she was careful to say. But the kind that refuses to back down from injustice. That's why our fight is so important not just Louisiana, but for Democrats everywhere. We have just 85 days until the midterm elections. We need to knock doors. We need to call voters. # [Trump signs order slashing childhood vaccines down to 11](https://substack.com/redirect/79e19d8e-744e-4000-820d-14fd48b6abd3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
President Donald Trump signed an executive order Monday **[calling for fewer childhood vaccines, reducing recommended shots to 11](https://substack.com/redirect/c07f8b35-1e89-417a-8a79-745f8c5b6cc6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/79e19d8e-744e-4000-820d-14fd48b6abd3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Schedule reduction target:** The order builds on efforts under HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. to reshape the childhood shot schedule, aligning the U.S. with other nations per Trump's remarks.
* **Separate MMR doses:** Trump directed splitting the measles, mumps and rubella vaccine into three single-disease shots given in separate visits.
* **Exemption enforcement push:** The Department of Justice must investigate states violating vaccine mandate exemptions for parental authority, disability accommodations, religious and medical reasons.

What will you do on **[June 18, 2027](https://substack.com/redirect/ce7621d4-7e76-4cbb-bada-76fe5af5e098?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** ... When your Medicare card stops working?

# [Florida's savage billboard: NYC mayor is our economic hero](https://substack.com/redirect/574d503c-3da8-404d-ac44-a4d83a8323db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The Florida Chamber of Commerce launched a Times Square billboard naming New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani **[Economic](https://substack.com/redirect/13c6d9f1-5b90-4fd2-8f98-8107c4218193?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** **[Developer of the Year for driving jobs, businesses and families to Florida.](https://substack.com/redirect/13c6d9f1-5b90-4fd2-8f98-8107c4218193?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/574d503c-3da8-404d-ac44-a4d83a8323db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Migration income stats:** Florida gains approximately $2.4 million in net taxable income every hour while New York loses about $1.1 million per hour according to Chamber-cited IRS data.
* **Resident flow numbers:** The Sunshine State gains a net 551 residents daily compared with New York losing 115 residents daily amid progressive tax and policy differences.
* **Budget contrast cited:** New York's state budget more than doubles Florida's, and New York City's municipal budget exceeds the entire Florida state budget by over $8 billion.
* **Free enterprise focus:** Chamber CEO Mark Wilson said the campaign highlights free enterprise versus socialist policies and aims to refocus America on liberty and lower taxes.

* * *
* * *
# [Treasury's big Trump Account win: Pre-tax deductions from pay](https://substack.com/redirect/574d503c-3da8-404d-ac44-a4d83a8323db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Treasury and IRS proposed regulations Tuesday[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/4a5408c2-6b25-467c-b63e-5ccbe6de8515?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[allowing pre-tax paycheck contributions to children's Trump Accounts](https://substack.com/redirect/4a5408c2-6b25-467c-b63e-5ccbe6de8515?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and employer matches up to $2,500 tax-free annually for dependents.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/574d503c-3da8-404d-ac44-a4d83a8323db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Payroll deduction access:** Employees can fund dependents' 530A Trump Accounts with pre-tax dollars straight from paychecks under the new guidance from Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.
* **Contribution caps detailed:** Annual limit reaches $5,000 from family members until age 18, with employers able to add up to $2,500 per worker tax-free within that total.
* **Pilot seed deposits:** Children born 2025 through 2028 receive a one-time $1,000 Treasury deposit, with roughly 7 million already signed up according to Bessent.
* **Corporate adoption rises:** Over 50 companies committed to contributions, some matching the $1,000 seed, as guidance clarifies the framework and may boost interest.

* * *
* * *
# [OpenAI wraps $7B share sale as $852B valuation holds firm](https://substack.com/redirect/574d503c-3da8-404d-ac44-a4d83a8323db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
OpenAI completed a secondary share sale totaling roughly $7 billion, **[letting current and former employees sell stock](https://substack.com/redirect/9c3fdb46-0a10-46c2-ae8a-8d01c8e7818b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** at the company's $852 billion valuation ahead of a potential IPO.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/574d503c-3da8-404d-ac44-a4d83a8323db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Employee liquidity provided:** The tender offer eases near-term pressure so staff can cash a portion of holdings after the record $122 billion funding round closed in March.
* **Prior sales pattern:** Secondary deals include a $6.6 billion tender at $500 billion valuation in October and a $1.5 billion offer in 2024 as pre-IPO strategy.
* **SEC filing status:** The company confidentially filed its prospectus with the Securities and Exchange Commission in June but has disclosed no official debut timeline.
* **Growth since launch:** OpenAI became one of the fastest-growing private companies after ChatGPT's 2022 debut, with rival Anthropic in a similar position.

# [Huang's $500B AI financing plan gets full Wall Street endorsement](https://substack.com/redirect/574d503c-3da8-404d-ac44-a4d83a8323db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang **[unveiled a big concept for AI infrastructure financing](https://substack.com/redirect/b3342972-f392-429c-b820-9b64076ec468?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** with Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, Blackstone, KKR, Apollo and Brookfield willing to raise $500 billion or more.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/574d503c-3da8-404d-ac44-a4d83a8323db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **New asset class view:** Huang called AI systems revenue-generating, productive, long-lived, fungible and flexible assets unlike PCs or phones that can be securitized.
* **Third-party capital push:** The firms signed memos of understanding to mobilize over $500 billion of third-party capital for construction of new AI factories.
* **Nvidia loan backstop:** Nvidia will have the option of backstopping 25% of every loan, potentially delivering more favorable rates for borrowers.
* **Risks openly noted:** Financiers acknowledged excesses and pullbacks will occur, comparing the early stage to the beginnings of mortgage-backed securities markets.

# [Goldman: Optical stocks are the clear next winners in AI boom](https://substack.com/redirect/574d503c-3da8-404d-ac44-a4d83a8323db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Goldman Sachs Asset Management's Sung Cho picks Lumentum and Coherent **[as the AI trade rotates from GPUs toward optical connectivity](https://substack.com/redirect/7212ce89-a32a-492c-b409-6913e4b2a0db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** driven by the shift from training to inference.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/574d503c-3da8-404d-ac44-a4d83a8323db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Inference drives new needs:** The transition requires more data centers closer to customers and optical links for chip-to-chip and server-to-server communication as copper reaches limits.
* **Capacity hard to scale:** Optical demand accelerates with the change yet bringing new capacity online is extremely difficult, providing longer trade duration than prior cycles.
* **Lumentum strong performance:** Cho highlights Lumentum, which has risen 600% in one year, alongside Coherent as leadership evolves with the architecture shift.
* **ETF and memory context:** A semiconductor ETF is up 80% year to date but down 20% from highs, while memory stocks have tripled in recent years.

* * *
* * *
# [Zuckerberg's radical promise: Personal superintelligence for every human](https://substack.com/redirect/574d503c-3da8-404d-ac44-a4d83a8323db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg **[released a 14-page letter proposing broadly distributed personal super-intelligence](https://substack.com/redirect/114f543d-6c76-49b0-bf36-4917aaaba842?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to empower individuals and prevent concentrated power in governments or businesses.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/574d503c-3da8-404d-ac44-a4d83a8323db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Three-part philosophy:** He bases the approach on individual empowerment as prosperity's source, invention as superintelligence's purpose, and balance of power as safety's foundation.
* **Open source resumes:** Meta is releasing Muse Glimmer, a 30-billion-parameter model that runs on a laptop or single consumer GPU, and soon Muse Spark 1.2 weights.
* **Billion-dollar community fund:** The $1 billion Future is for Everyone Fund will invest in U.S. communities with Meta data centers, after teachers received $50,000 bonuses in Louisiana.
* **Avoid concentrated control:** Power held by a small number of individuals, businesses, governments or AI itself would produce less favorable outcomes for everyone else, he argued.

* * *
* * *
# [Chipflation creates clear winners: Morgan Stanley backs hardware stocks](https://substack.com/redirect/574d503c-3da8-404d-ac44-a4d83a8323db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Morgan Stanley analyst Erik Woodring says memory chipflation is a multi-year structural headwind, with enterprises accelerating PC, server and storage purchases, **[creating further upside for select hardware names.](https://substack.com/redirect/877c4d1e-f232-44cb-8ea2-6f427160364a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/574d503c-3da8-404d-ac44-a4d83a8323db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Fear of missing procurement:** Enterprises prioritize locking in favorable prices and limiting shortages rather than delaying hardware buys until pricing cools, boosting near-term demand.
* **Bullish stock picks:** Woodring favors Hewlett Packard Enterprise, Everpure, TD Synnex and Lenovo for exposure to durable server and storage infrastructure spending.
* **Valuation caution issued:** Hardware stocks have risen over 100% since early 2025 and trade at aggregate 25x P/E, nearly double prior peaks, nearing cycle end.
* **Shortage duration view:** JPMorgan's Jay Kwon sees the memory supply-demand shortage continuing for at least two years with demand broadening from GPU to CPU.

* * *
* * *
# [The Iconic Beverly Hills 90210 school is in a full enrollment crisis](https://substack.com/redirect/574d503c-3da8-404d-ac44-a4d83a8323db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Alexander Hamilton High School in West Los Angeles, **[the filming location for Beverly Hills, 90210,](https://substack.com/redirect/b9bd00db-2647-4d2f-bfbb-553fee68c525?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** has enrollment down from nearly 3,000 students pre-pandemic to 2,000 amid rising costs and pressures.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/574d503c-3da8-404d-ac44-a4d83a8323db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Enrollment decline continues:** Community representative Jsane Tyler, in her 12th year, watches numbers fall year over year, with magnet programs the only factor helping balance them.
* **Infrastructure challenges mount:** A roughly $400 million modernization project is behind schedule and one building's basement floods when it rains at the 90-year-old campus.
* **Bond documents reveal woes:** LAUSD's $222 million debt sale this week highlights empty classrooms, shrinking revenue, new labor contracts, wildfires, immigration enforcement and FBI probe.
* **Cash risk by 2027:** Los Angeles County officials warn the district could run short of cash as soon as November 2027 amid national enrollment and aid expiration pressures.

We scored a major victory in our fight against the illegal Nexstar/Tegna merger:
Last month, I filed a motion raising concerns about the shocking actions Nexstar took to take control of Tegna, violating a court order that stops the merger from taking place while our case proceeds. Now, the court has agreed and demanded that the companies comply.
This is great news for consumers, and a big win as we continue fighting this case in court!
Here’s what’s at stake: If this merger goes through, Nexstar Media Group and Tegna — two massive broadcast TV companies — would consolidate their power into a behemoth that covers 80% of TV households in the country. This mega-merger would significantly lessen competition, drive up costs, and impact how Americans get their news.
This is a clear violation of the federal antitrust law known as the Clayton Act.
That’s why earlier this year, I led attorneys general across the nation in filing a lawsuit to challenge the unlawful merger, and the court put a preliminary injunction in place while the case proceeds.
But Nexstar has been openly violating the order by placing current and recent personnel on Tegna’s Board of Directors. We called it out, and the court agreed — calling Nexstar’s actions brazen and shocking , and ordering them to comply with the law.
We are not done yet. I’m suing Nexstar and Tegna to block this merger, make sure antitrust laws are enforced, and protect consumers in California and across the country.
If you’re with me, will you help power our work with a contribution to my re-election campaign right now? No amount is too small — anything you can give will make a real difference in what we can accomplish together. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26]

# Join Our Autism Support Group
---
|
---
| This August, we are taking a break from our Monthly Educational Webinar and focusing on something equally important: **supporting and connecting our parents.** **Please note:** Our **August Parent Support Group has been rescheduled**. Please disregard the previously announced date. We invite you to join us on **Wednesday, August 19th at 5:00 PM PST / 8:00 PM EST** via Zoom for an evening of encouragement, connection, and support. We know that caring for a child or loved one with autism can bring both incredible joys and significant challenges. Sometimes one of the most valuable resources is simply having a community of people who understand. Our Parent Support Group provides a space to learn from one another, discuss what is working for your family, hear the experiences of other parents, and build meaningful connections. **Advance registration is required to attend the Parent Support Group.** Please register using the Zoom link below to reserve your spot and receive the meeting information. We look forward to spending this time together and continuing to build a strong, informed, and supportive Autism Health community.

# Early Bird Registration for the Autism Health Summit
---
|
---
| The countdown has begun for the **2027 Autism Health Summit** , taking place **April 29 through May 1, 2027** , at **The Legacy Center Resort & Spa** in **San Diego, California**. Join parents, physicians, researchers, healthcare professionals, educators, and advocates from around the world for three inspiring days of education, collaboration, and hope. We're excited to announce that our **headline speakers** include **Del Bigtree** and **Dr. Henry Ealy** , with many more nationally recognized experts to be announced in the coming months. Attendees will gain valuable insights into the latest research, innovative therapies, integrative medicine, environmental health, and practical strategies to support individuals with autism and related neurological conditions. We're also pleased to offer **Continuing Medical Education (CME)** and **Continuing Education Unit (CEU)** credits for eligible healthcare professionals, making the Autism Health Summit an outstanding opportunity to expand your knowledge while earning valuable continuing education credits. **Now is the best time to register!** Secure your ticket before prices increase and receive **$50 OFF** your registration during the month of **August** by using promo code **AHS50** at checkout. name: Office of U.S. Senator Angela Alsobrooks
subject: Senator Alsobrooks Newsletter -- August 11, 2026
body:
|

---
Dear Friends and Neighbors, We are facing serious public health challenges across our nation. Thousands of Americans have fallen ill in a Cyclospora outbreak that has yet to be contained, and the source remains unknown. We are also seeing the resurgence of preventable diseases, including the largest measles outbreak in 35 years, while some newborns are being put at risk because parents are afraid to give them Vitamin K shots that can prevent dangerous bleeding. At the same time, families continue to confront devastating diseases like cancer and Alzheimer's, while RFK Jr. and this Administration have canceled research that could lead to critical breakthroughs. We are also in the midst of an unauthorized war that this President has dragged our country into with no clear objective and no clear path out. I continue to pray for the service members who have been killed and injured in this war, and for their families. Every day, our sons and daughters--our heroes--are paying the price with their lives, while the President and his family continue to get richer. Meanwhile, families are already stretched thin. Groceries cost too much. Housing costs too much. Gas costs too much. Health care costs too much. For millions of Americans, there isn't some giant cushion in the household budget waiting to absorb another price increase, another medical bill, or another economic shock. So how are my colleagues on the other side of the aisle working to address affordability, confront the Cyclospora outbreak, or hold President Trump accountable for this war of his own creation? Americans have every right to ask what the strategy is, what the endgame is, and what it will take to finally bring this [war to an end](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15407.19808324.6328303.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fx.com%2fSen_Alsobrooks%2fstatus%2f2084346491338998124%3fs%3d20&redir_log=653840017003361)--a war whose costs are being borne by the American people. Those are difficult questions. They require governing. But Dr. Fauci is easier. It's easier for them to attack an [85-year-old](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15407.19808324.6328303.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fx.com%2fSen_Alsobrooks%2fstatus%2f2085844714406719825%3fs%3d20&redir_log=438099816612361) retiree, haul him in front of a Senate committee, turn on the cameras, and try to elicit outrage. It's easier for my colleagues on the other side of the aisle to spend another week arguing about 2020 instead of demanding answers about 2026. That's the distraction, and I urge you not to fall for the [Jedi mind trick](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15407.19808324.6328303.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fx.com%2fSen_Alsobrooks%2fstatus%2f2085380354345414713%3fs%3d20&redir_log=418506737706360). Dr. Fauci served our country honorably, and I was honored to work with him to save Maryland lives in 2020 and 2021 when I was Prince George's County Executive. Look at what is happening to your grocery bill. Look at what is happening to our public health. Look at the people struggling to get by. Look at a war that still has no end in sight. Those are the problems we should be talking about. I will continue fighting for answers and action. I have voted 13 times to end this war, and I will continue demanding that President Trump and Republicans stop sacrificing American lives and livelihoods to pointless aggression. In the weeks and months ahead, I ask you to remain vigilant and exercise discernment. There will be plenty of chaos, outrage, and distraction designed to pull our attention away from the challenges that directly affect our families and communities. Our country's well-being depends on our ability to separate those distractions from what truly matters--and to demand that our leaders focus on the work the American people sent us here to do. **Fighting Through Legislation **
It has been a busy few weeks here on Capitol Hill and I have been fighting hard by introducing and cosponsoring critical bills. From ensuring dental care for children and adults, to providing seniors with the tools they need to age in their homes, to protections for victims of domestic violence, I continue to fight for legislation that will help Maryland families thrive.

These are the bills I have introduced:

Ensuring Kids Have Access to Medically Necessary Dental Care Act: This bill would prohibit lifetime or annual dollar limits on dental benefits under the Children's Health Insurance Program. It would also require dental-only supplemental, or wraparound, coverage for certain children rather than leaving that coverage as a state option.

Medicare Dental Benefit Act of 2026: This bill would add routine, basic, major, and emergency dental coverage to Medicare Part B, reducing the disparities that leave half of all Medicare beneficiaries without dental coverage today.

Medicaid Dental Benefit Act of 2026: This bill would make adult dental care a mandatory Medicaid benefit rather than a state-by-state option, with full federal funding for the first three years.

Modal Parity in Permitting Act: This bill would allow transit and passenger rail project sponsors to acquire 'real property interest' and parity during the federal permitting process.

Senior Accessible Housing Tax Credit Act of 2026: This legislation would create a new tax credit for seniors to install essential, aging-related modifications to their homes.

These are the bills I have cosponsored:

Lainie Jones Comprehensive Cancer Survivorship Act of 2026: This legislation would create a more coordinated standard of care for cancer survivors from diagnosis through treatment, recovery, and long-term survivorship, including Medicare coverage for cancer care planning and coordination services, a survivorship-focused alternative payment model, employment assistance grants, a comprehensive survivorship program, Medicaid and Children's Health Insurance Program coverage for certain fertility services, and an Office of Cancer Survivorship within the National Cancer Institute. The bill would create new coverage, grant, program, and federal office responsibilities.

Right to IVF Act of 2026: This bill would establish an enforceable nationwide right for individuals to receive assisted reproductive technology, including in vitro fertilization, for providers to offer those services, for insurers to cover them, and for manufacturers to provide related drugs and devices. The updated version expands beyond the prior Protect IVF framework by adding coverage and access provisions for service members, veterans, Federal Employees Health Benefits Program enrollees, private insurance plans, Medicaid, and Medicare, while also clarifying that assisted reproductive technology should be protected as distinct, evidence-based medical care and not replaced by so-called restorative reproductive medicine alternatives.

Women Add Resourcefulness and Resilience to Improve Operational Readiness (WARRIOR) Act: This bill would update outdated provisions of federal law to align with current DOD policy, ensuring that military occupational standards are based on validated job requirements and applied equally to all qualified service members. This bill codifies what more than two decades of experience has already proven: maintaining rigorous, gender-neutral standards strengthens our military readiness.

Lori Jackson-Nicolette Elias Domestic Violence Survivor Protection Act: This bill would address the stalking and ex parte loopholes that allow people subject to domestic violence court orders to avoid prohibitions on firearm possession and the stalking and boyfriend loopholes that allow people convicted of domestic violence misdemeanors to avoid the same prohibitions. It would also establish a grant program for removal of firearms after the issuance of a domestic violence court order.

Reducing the Effects of the Cyberattack on OPM Victims Enduring Response and Protecting Identifiable Information Act (RECOVER PII Act): This bill would amend language in the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2017 so that victims of the 2015 Office of Personnel Management breaches are provided continuous protection services and reimbursements to federal employees and contractors for privacy-enhancing services.

Next Generation Shipping Act: This bill would establish a $1 billion program within the Department of Transportation's Maritime Administration (MARAD) to support the research, development, demonstration, deployment, and commercialization of zero-emission and clean alternative maritime technologies and infrastructure.

A bill to amend the Public Health Service Act to streamline the review of new prescription drugs to market and lower costs. This bill would consolidate duplicative regulatory efforts and ultimately lower costs for Americans.

Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia Act of 2026: This legislation would impose primary and secondary sanctions against Russia and actors supporting Russia's war in Ukraine. The sanctions target Russian officials, oligarchs, their family members, foreign persons, Russian banks and financial institutions, and the Russian Shadow Fleet.

A resolution designating the week of August 2 through August 8, 2026, as "National Farmers Market Week." **(Agreed to in the Senate) **

A concurrent resolution recognizing the significance of equal pay and the disparity in wages paid to men and to Black women.

A resolution directing the Senate Legal Counsel to bring a civil action in the name of the Senate to enforce the Foreign Emoluments Clause contained in clause 8 of section 9 of article I of the Constitution of the United States. **In the Community **
Maryland is proving what's possible when education, business, and government work together. I was grateful to join NAF to discuss how we're preparing students for success through career pathways, workforce development, and expanded opportunities. Nothing beats the energy at the Prince George's County [Senior Line Dance Party](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15407.19808324.6328303.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fx.com%2fSen_Alsobrooks%2fstatus%2f2078535661603135750%3fs%3d20&redir_log=57523486651360)! It was a joy to join some of Maryland's coolest seniors for a morning of music, dancing, and community. Thank you to the Parks & Recreation Department for creating opportunities that keep our seniors active, connected, and thriving.

I joined Governor Moore and Team Maryland for a firsthand look at the progress on rebuilding the Francis Scott Key Bridge. We are rebuilding in honor of the six Marylanders we lost while restoring a vital link for our state's economy and our nation's supply chain. A stronger, safer bridge is taking shape.

Maryland's veterans have served our nation, and we must ensure they have every opportunity to succeed. I was proud to join Senator Van Hollen and the Montgomery County Chamber Community Foundation to celebrate a $2 million investment that will expand opportunities for veteran entrepreneurs and small businesses.

It was an honor to welcome Jack and Jill of America to Baltimore for its 47th National Convention. For generations, the organization has empowered young people to lead, serve, and make a difference in their communities--leadership that matters now more than ever.

I had the opportunity to speak at Semafor's World of Work about the future of work and how we ensure innovation creates opportunity for everyone. From AI to digital assets, we must embrace new technologies while protecting workers, expanding pathways to wealth, and keeping America competitive. I was honored to accept the Blossom Award at The White Dress Project's Night in White Gala alongside my friend Lupita Nyong'o. We wore white in solidarity with the women who couldn't because of the pain and challenges they have silently endured from uterine fibroids. **** I was excited to welcome leaders from SURVICE Engineering and BAE Systems FalconWorks to my office. Maryland is leading the way in defense innovation, and partnerships like these strengthen our national security while creating new opportunities for our state's workforce and economy. **Grant Spotlight **

I wanted to remind you of a few grant opportunities for nonprofits, public, and private institutions that will go a long way to help Maryland families. **[Bureau of Justice Assistance - BJA FY 2026 Enhancing Security Measures for Houses of Worship Synopsis 1](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15407.19808324.6328303.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.grants.gov%2fsearch-results-detail%2f363280&redir_log=119831822432340)** provides grants to enhance security and law enforcement capabilities at faith-based institutions and houses of worship to prevent and respond to bias-motivated crimes. Projects will strengthen partnerships between religious communities and local law enforcement, implement evidence-based security measures, and build institutional capacity to report incidents and assist in criminal investigations. (Posted July 22, 2026 - September 2, 2026 deadline)

**[Department of Agriculture Rural Housing Service _Rural Housing Preservation Grant Synopsis 4_](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15407.19808324.6328303.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.grants.gov%2fsearch-results-detail%2f363400&redir_log=675580516052339)** which provides qualified public agencies, private nonprofit organizations, which may include but not be limited to, Faith-Based and Community Organizations, and other eligible entities grant funds to assist very low- and low-income homeowners in repairing and rehabilitating their homes in rural areas. In addition, the HPG program assists rental property owners and cooperative housing complexes in repairing and rehabilitating their units if they agree to make such units available to low- and very low-income persons. It would also require dental-only supplemental, or wraparound, coverage for certain children rather than leaving that coverage as a state option. Medicare Dental Benefit Act of 2026: This bill would add routine, basic, major, and emergency dental coverage to Medicare Part B, reducing the disparities that leave half of all Medicare beneficiaries without dental coverage today. Medicaid Dental Benefit Act of 2026: This bill would make adult dental care a mandatory Medicaid benefit rather than a state-by-state option, with full federal funding for the first three years. Modal Parity in Permitting Act: This bill would allow transit and passenger rail project sponsors to acquire 'real property interest' and parity during the federal permitting process. Senior Accessible Housing Tax Credit Act of 2026: This legislation would create a new tax credit for seniors to install essential, aging-related modifications to their homes. These are the bills I have cosponsored: Lainie Jones Comprehensive Cancer Survivorship Act of 2026: This legislation would create a more coordinated standard of care for cancer survivors from diagnosis through treatment, recovery, and long-term survivorship, including Medicare coverage for cancer care planning and coordination services, a survivorship-focused alternative payment model, employment assistance grants, a comprehensive survivorship program, Medicaid and Children's Health Insurance Program coverage for certain fertility services, and an Office of Cancer Survivorship within the National Cancer Institute. The bill would create new coverage, grant, program, and federal office responsibilities. Right to IVF Act of 2026: This bill would establish an enforceable nationwide right for individuals to receive assisted reproductive technology, including in vitro fertilization, for providers to offer those services, for insurers to cover them, and for manufacturers to provide related drugs and devices. The updated version expands beyond the prior Protect IVF framework by adding coverage and access provisions for service members, veterans, Federal Employees Health Benefits Program enrollees, private insurance plans, Medicaid, and Medicare, while also clarifying that assisted reproductive technology should be protected as distinct, evidence-based medical care and not replaced by so-called restorative reproductive medicine alternatives. Next Generation Shipping Act: This bill would establish a $1 billion program within the Department of Transportation's Maritime Administration (MARAD) to support the research, development, demonstration, deployment, and commercialization of zero-emission and clean alternative maritime technologies and infrastructure. [Folks come up here, puff their chest out on TV, act like they’re in some big fight... and then they slip behind closed doors and cut deals that grow the same bloated government they promised to shrink.](https://trk.email.tim-burchett.)
Different jerseys. Same playbook: [Spend more. Grow the machine. Protect their own.](https://trk.email.tim-burchett.-Du9AE0OQPDidggB-rcg)
You’ll see Republicans vote for the same big spending mess they campaign against back home.
But have you ever seen Democrats meet us halfway on conservative priorities? Not in your lifetime.
That’s how the swamp keeps rolling - like a broken-down carnival ride nobody wants to fix because everybody’s making money off the tickets.
[I don’t fit in with that crowd, and I don’t plan to. I didn’t come up here to join the club. I came here to fight it.](https://trk.email.tim-burchett.)
But standing up to that kind of machine? That ain’t cheap, and it sure ain’t easy.
They’ve got lobbyists, donors, backroom deals - the whole setup. I’ve got a backbone... and I’ve got patriots like you, Peter.

**Derek, with just 85 days until Election Day, our organizers are burning shoe leather to reach voters across the country. Will you join us in saying a huge THANK YOU to them?** [](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/20260811_organizer_thank_you/?refcode=em_20260811_8441_fr&akid=8441%2E22930333%2EL4AVtB) Our Democratic organizers are on the ground from coast to coast, _every day_ , knocking on doors, registering new young Democrats, and having meaningful conversations with voters about what’s at stake this year. All so they’re prepared to show up to the polls in droves this November to elect Democrats up and down the ballot. They’re walking miles and miles no matter the weather, having difficult but important conversations with Americans all across the political spectrum, and building the lasting community infrastructure our party needs to win. [**The last three months of election year are the most intense of the cycle,_especially for organizers_ , so we’re putting together a Thank You card to show our deep appreciation for their hard work. Derek, it would mean the world if you’d join us in thanking them by signing this card with a short note →**](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/20260811_organizer_thank_you/?refcode=em_20260811_8441_fr&akid=8441%2E22930333%2EL4AVtB) **[SIGN THE CARD](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/20260811_organizer_thank_you/?refcode=em_20260811_8441_fr&akid=8441%2E22930333%2EL4AVtB)** Thank you for all of your support, The Democrats
