name: Wes Moore
subject: “Service United”
body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1727%2E1086043%2Ey7Q-1y)
Peter, I want to share a longer message about what I’m thinking about as I become chair of the National Governors Association, but if you don’t have time to read it all, I would deeply appreciate **[a contribution to power our campaign.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260811-1.mkX5Uo&refcode=em-20260811-1&t=2&akid=1727%2E1086043%2Ey7Q-1y)**
When I was young, the world saw me for the little boy I was. But as each year passed, the world stopped seeing me as a harmless kid and started seeing me as something entirely different. Intimidating. Threatening.
**That shift had a profound effect on me.** I thought that, _maybe, I was destined to become what society expected me to be._
For a while, I seemed to give in to those expectations. Didn’t pay attention in school. Got into trouble.
I ended up finding my own path, but only because I had the right support system -- one that lifted me up on its shoulders. I had mentors and ministers who ushered me into manhood. Today, too many young men and boys lack that kind of support. And because of it, we’re watching an entire generation lose its way.
The data says this too. We’re seeing a warning sign too big to ignore, with declines in everything from educational attainment and employment to mental health for our young men and boys.
That’s why my administration has taken steps to chart a better way forward. In 2023, we created the Thrive Academy to identify youth at highest risk of perpetrating or being a victim of gun violence. We have equipped them with the support to gain access to housing, jobs, and food, as well as physical and mental health plans.
One year after launching Thrive, we saw a massive movement in the right direction. The program succeeded by redirecting those youth to a path beyond the justice system, with 80% avoiding rearrest.
It has been a mission of my life -- in my work before politics and now leading Maryland -- to intervene before that faux first chance is used, and lost.
That is why we’ve made record investments across the state to make sure our communities are stronger than ever. We’ve empowered families by making life more affordable, bringing new businesses to Maryland, and strengthening our public schools.
We’ve worked to get more men in the classroom as educators and in hospitals as nurses and doctors, invested in apprenticeship programs, and provided new opportunities for people who have mistakes in their past and deserve a real second chance.
And we’re continuing to support our graduating seniors beyond the classroom with our service-year option for every high school graduate -- the first of its kind in this country.
Our recent graduates can choose to work in any field that may interest them, from education to healthcare, and environmental protection. This program gives our students the opportunity to find their passion, as they give back to their communities.
We’ve seen the massive success of this program since its launch, and now we’re taking it to the next level. **As the new chair of the National Governors Association, I will be launching “Service United,” a national program to expand paid service opportunities for young people.**
**Because I know that service will save us.**
My commitment to our young people across our state remains consistent: I will always invest in them, because they are our future.
**[If you believe in what we’re building together, I would appreciate a contribution to our re-election campaign today so I can continue this important work.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260811-1.mkX5Uo&refcode=em-20260811-1&t=3&akid=1727%2E1086043%2Ey7Q-1y)**
**And if there’s one message to take away, it’s this: Our young men and boys are not problems to be fixed, but people to be uplifted.**
Onward,
Wes

Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

# A correction to today's newsletter: MN Senate primary
### Today's Daily has been corrected.
| | Aug 11
---|---
In this morning's newsletter, our item about the Minnesota Senate Democratic primary mistakenly inverted the two candidates. Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan has the endorsement of Sen. Bernie Sanders, while Rep. Angie Craig has the support of AIPAC. The [newsletter has been corrected](https://substack.com/redirect/f0c5c9f6-5d68-49d4-8b38-6d28cddb1267?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* **Primaries in six states, including Wisconsin, Minnesota, and South Carolina:**
* Progressive **Francesca Hong** , a chef and state lawmaker,**** faces Milwaukee County executive **David Crowley** in Wisconsin's Democratic gubernatorial primary. Hong, a member of the Democratic Socialists of America, is the frontrunner in the race, despite party efforts to back several of her opponents, including former Lt. Gov. **Mandela Barnes** , who dropped out two weeks before the election, and current Lt. Gov **Sara Rodriguez** , who dropped out earlier.
* In Minnesota, Lt. Gov. **Peggy Flanagan** and Rep. **Angie Craig** are vying for the Democratic nomination to replace outgoing Sen. **Tina Smith**. Craig, whose career-long support from AIPAC has complicated her more recent votes for resolutions blocking weapons funding to Israel, holds a narrow lead over Flanagan--who has received the endorsement of Sen. **Bernie Sanders** --according to the [latest poll](https://substack.com/redirect/59277370-afcb-4df1-a18c-c20dda6212c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* _Editor 's note: This has been corrected to amend an earlier version which said Sanders endorsed Craig instead of Flanagan._
* In the race to replace Craig, progressives **Matt Little** , a former state senator, and **Kaela Berg** face **Matt Klein** , a pro-Israel physician who has received over $2.5 million from 314 Action, which supports scientists and doctors running for public office and sometimes operates as an AIPAC cut-out. **Drop Site 's Julian Andreone and Ryan Grim wrote about this race [here](https://substack.com/redirect/99b08aaf-609d-4e59-a4f7-6f372493b8a5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**
* Ten Republicans in South Carolina are running to replace the late Sen. **Lindsey Graham** , including his sister **Darline Graham** , who Gov. Henry McMaster appointed to complete her deceased brother's term, and who received Trump's endorsement in the primary. Reps. **Russell Fry** and **Ralph Norman** are also seeking the nomination, along with former South Carolina Gov. **Mark Sanford** and businessman **Mark Lynch**. A majority in the primary is needed to avoid a late August runoff. Lynch, who previously challenged Graham, is running as the only candidate to reject AIPAC money.

_To read today 's full Daily [click here](https://substack.com/redirect/f0c5c9f6-5d68-49d4-8b38-6d28cddb1267?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_

| | Right now, families and children seeking asylum are being locked up at the Dilley detention center in Texas. This isn't by some accident or oversight. The Trump Administration brought back family detention on purpose, betting that most Americans wouldn't notice or wouldn't care. **I'm fighting back because children don't belong in detention.** In June 2018, during Trump's first term, when I heard Trump's Attorney General talking about mistreating children to discourage immigration, I traveled to the border in Texas to see what was happening. What I found was stunning: CBP agents separating children from their parents and holding them in chain-link cages inside a warehouse. I spoke out, and that moment helped force the country to confront what the Trump Administration was doing to kids. **Now they are detaining kids again. Different facility, similar cruelty.** My experience at the border is why I introduced the Children's Safe Welcome Act to shut facilities like Dilley down for good and end family detention nationwide. Here's what my bill does:
* Closes Dilley and any facility like it
* Bans locking up children and families for immigration violations
* Replaces detention with community-based alternatives that are cheaper, more humane, and actually work

I visited those facilities in 2018. I saw the cruelty. And we know similar cruelty is happening right now at these facilities, and I'm not going to let it happen without a fight. **Kids don't belong in detention.** I'll keep pushing this bill until it's law. body:
[1]LeftNet

It’s Zohran Mamdani. A few months ago, we wound down our campaign
operations to focus on delivering results over the first few months of
this term.

We’re back.
Here’s why:

Progressives often use political campaigns as a tool to solely win (or
lose) elections. We build grassroots donor networks. We engage volunteers.
And come Election Day, we leave the campaign behind and start preparing to
govern. The emails stop coming.

But that is not how the big-money interests operate. Their work is
constant and prolific. In closed-door meetings, insider operatives
consider how to influence our politics year-round. That’s how our
opponents secured the resources to spend $83 million against our movement
last year.

There is a cynicism that our politics is permanently broken, that our
democracy can only favor the wealthy and well-connected. But I know that’s
not true. We just have to be willing to fight for it.

That’s why we’re making investments in our movement starting right now.

[ https://act.leftnet.org/go/22925?t=1001&akid=1704%2E2118727%2EFvZvrL ]Will you sign up today so I can send you updates about how to help
defend our movement?

SIGN UP ››

We can expect that our opposition will be better funded, better organized,
and ready to spend earlier than before.

But now, we’re going to be ready.

By joining this movement, you’re helping us build an operation strong
enough to meet the fights ahead.

[ https://act.leftnet.org/go/22925?t=1002&akid=1704%2E2118727%2EFvZvrL ]I would be incredibly grateful if you would join our campaign
today. 🙏🏽

In solidarity,

Zohran Mamdani

body:
I’m proud to launch our Seniors for Mackenzie coalition.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/18VW9eit3Nu?e=5ccada9200&c2id=772b190546f65300d48df506f9534e27)
|
---
| | | | | | Friends,I want to take a moment to talk about the work I’m doing every day to Deliver for Seniors across the Greater Lehigh Valley.More importantly, I’m proud to launch our **Seniors for Mackenzie** coalition. I’m honored to have so many incredible local seniors step up to lead this coalition to help spread the word about the positive work I’m doing in Washington.When I arrived in Congress a year and a half ago, we got to work immediately on the issues that matter most to our senior community.We led the charge on tax relief for seniors by passing **No Tax on Social Security** , helping ensure that **88% of seniors now pay no federal income tax on their Social Security benefits**.I kept my promise to never vote for a Social Security or Medicare benefits cut – while working to make sure these programs are there for today’s seniors and future generations.I listened to seniors right here in the Greater Lehigh Valley who told me about the challenges they were facing with Medicare Advantage. I took those concerns directly to Washington and led the effort for increased Medicare Advantage reimbursement rates — and **we got it done.** I’ve also been working on ways to combat the scams and fraud that increasingly target seniors and their hard-earned savings.And recently, I hosted a **Breakfast with Seniors** as part of my ongoing effort to meet directly with different constituencies throughout the Greater Lehigh Valley. I want to hear directly from seniors about their concerns, their priorities, and what more we can do in Washington to improve their lives.My message to older residents across the Greater Lehigh Valley is clear:**I hear you. I’m fighting for you. And I’ll continue to deliver for you.** I’m incredibly grateful to the seniors who have stepped up to lead **Seniors for Mackenzie** , and I look forward to working alongside them as we continue this fight.**Together, we’ll keep delivering.** Ryan Mackenzie
---

The House passed the SAVE America Act three times. Senate Democrats have blocked it every single time.

name: Heidi Ganahl
subject: The Mountain Minute: 8/11/2026
body:
Colorado utilities said a regional grid would strengthen reliability. July 20 tested it.
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hey friends,
Want your full news breakdown? Listen to the Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).
Here's a summary of today's top stories:
**🏔️ Here in Colorado...** House Majority Forward launched a [$15M Spanish-language ad blitz](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) attacking Rep. Gabe Evans. An RMV report found the [western grid hit an emergency alert](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) July 20 after Colorado utilities joined the Southwest Power Pool — with the state PUC admitting no oversight or insight into the cause. And DHS Secretary Mullin toured Colorado's ICE offices before meeting privately with Evans and Hispanic faith leaders to [counter "false rumors" about enforcement](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).
**🇺🇸 On the National Stage...** Trump signaled a [shift to economic pressure over military strikes](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) to end the Iran war, citing Iran's inflation and empty coffers.
**🗣️ Commentary Spotlight...** Tina Peters urges DOJ to [seize Fulton County, PA election machines](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) before destruction. Joondeph cites a Rasmussen poll showing [54% now call Trump's Iran decision wrong](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Gaines flags Colorado's budget paying up to [$11,200 per UPK preschooler](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) vs. an $8,900 K-12 base rate. Armstrong [critiques Weiser's "blueprint"](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) as pro-business talk paired with tax and spending hikes.
This is your Mountain Minute for Tuesday, August 11, 2026.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Colorado utilities said a regional grid would strengthen reliability. July 20 tested it.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
On April 1, Colorado Springs Utilities and Platte River Power Authority, two of the utilities that initiated SPP’s western expansion effort, joined other Colorado utilities in the Southwest Power Pool, a regional grid operator headquartered in Little Rock, Arkansas. Neither utility was legally required to join. Both chose to.
Jason Frisbie, Platte River’s general manager and CEO, said the move would help his utility “maintain the reliability and affordability that our communities and their customers expect.”
One hundred and ten days later, Frisbie was asking those same communities to hold off on running their dishwashers.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[A four-year-old is worth more than a fifth grader to Colorado schools](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [COLORADO ACCOUNTABILITY PROJECT](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
_A funding quirk in Colorado's school finance system pays districts more for a part-time preschooler than a full-time K-12 student — creating incentives worth watching._
* **A striking funding gap:** Colorado's Universal Pre-K program pays districts roughly $11,000 for a 30-hour-a-week four-year-old, compared to the new statewide base K-12 per-pupil funding of $8,900.40 for 2026-27 — meaning a preschooler brings in about $2,200 more than an older student.
* **Even part-time preschool outpaces full-time K-12:** Cory Gaines notes that a standard 15-hour UPK slot generates roughly 70 cents on every dollar a full-time K-12 student brings in, despite the preschooler attending only part-time.
* **An incentive colliding with declining enrollment:** With Colorado public schools already losing students, Gaines argues this funding disparity is driving growing district interest in running UPK programs — raising the question of what happens when government-run preschool competes directly with private providers.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---

---
**ONLY ON ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE ⤵️**
**[Denver’s chief security officer quit July 2, alleging punishment for raising concerns](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**BY SHAINA COLE | LOCAL | AUGUST 5** _The chief security officer of the Denver Security Office sent a resignation email to more than a dozen recipients at 12:57 p.m. on July 2 — the day after his seven-year anniversary with the city — and used the letter to accuse General Services leaders of punishing him for raising concerns._
**[A union pipeline DSA built on college campuses](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** **BY SHAINA COLE | STATE | AUGUST 4**
_DSA’s youth section trains students to organize on campus. What happens after graduation is its own story, one its own members describe directly. “YDSA’s job is to train socialists on campus and create a pipeline into DSA,” Dare Cima, a University of Louisville YDSA member, said at the organization’s national conference this spring._
**[Two measures. Two opposite answers. One Colorado income tax rate.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**BY SHAINA COLE | STATE | AUGUST 3** _Colorado voters may face a choice in November between two measures that couldn’t disagree more about the state income tax. One would replace the flat rate with a graduated system and raise close to $2 billion a year. The other would make it illegal to raise the rate at all._

A federal judge refused to block Donald Trump’s executive order to create a federal voter list and limit mail voting.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
That means the fight to protect free, fair, and accessible elections just suffered a blow — and the stakes could not be higher.
Trump and his allies are still trying to sow distrust in our elections, restrict access to the ballot box, and give the federal government unprecedented control over how Americans vote. They’re targeting vote-by-mail even after repeated audits, and investigations confirmed there was no widespread fraud in the 2020 election.
And make no mistake: this is exactly why we need everyone on board, fighting back harder than ever to save our democracy and the rule of law.
In Oregon, we know vote-by-mail works. We’ve spent decades building a system that is secure, accessible, and trusted by voters across the political spectrum. But national attacks on voting rights don’t stop at state borders.
As Secretary of State, I’ll do everything in my power to protect Oregon voters, defend election workers from political intimidation, and ensure our elections remain free from partisan interference.
But I can’t do this alone. So today, I'm asking you to stand with me. Add your name to send a clear message that our elections will operate freely and without political intimidation or partisan interference. [https://secure.ngpvan.com/l9G-ythIzUy6NmRZVqVW8g2] [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]

The courts may not have stopped this latest attack yet — but voting rights advocates are continuing the legal battle, and we must continue organizing, mobilizing, and preparing for what comes next.
This campaign is about protecting democracy itself. And it will take all of us working together to win.
Thank you,
Tobias Read
Oregon Secretary of State

We’ve spent decades building a system that is secure, accessible, and trusted by voters across the political spectrum. But national attacks on voting rights don’t stop at state borders. As Secretary of State, I’ll do everything in my power to protect Oregon voters, defend election workers from political intimidation, and ensure our elections remain free from partisan interference. ## **Call To Action**
The Washington State Republican Party (WAGOP) is urging concerned voters to file a complaint with the Commission on Judicial Conduct at [https://www.cjc.state.wa.us/index.php?page=filing_a_complaint§ion;=file_online](https://the.news.wagop.org/link.php?AGENCY=FACT&M=14158524&N=32523&L=16619&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuY2pjLnN0YXRlLndhLnVzL2luZGV4LnBocD9wYWdlPWZpbGluZ19hX2NvbXBsYWludCZzZWN0aW9uPWZpbGVfb25saW5lJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNVFF4TlRnMU1qUSUzRA==&hash=8cb71983474320bf6ba702cbe45755f61c009a2e1d6e256f7121dd1bae76df58) following Thurston County Superior Court Judge Chris Lanese’s conduct last Friday in connection with a legal challenge to the attorney general’s false and misleading Public Investment Impact Disclosure (PIID) for I-645, the initiative to repeal the state income tax.

"Lanese dismissed Let’s Go Washington’s legal challenge WITHOUT A HEARING after hearing a separate challenge to I-645’s PIID brought by open-government activist Arthur West," says WAGOP Chairman Rep. Jim Walsh. "Lanese's speech and mannerisms during the West hearing were highly unusual and even hysterical. The judge acted more like a radical activist than an impartial jurist."

Adds Chairman Walsh: "But the most problematic violation of judicial standards that Lanese committed was setting a trap for West (who is not an attorney and was representing himself in his case) that tricked West into stating he was also representing Let's Go Washington's case—which he was not. Lanese then pounced on West's error and dismissed BOTH challenges to the misleading PIID."

“We came prepared to make our case,” Let’s Go Washington founder Brian Heywood said in a statement after the ruling. “Instead, a civilian who does not represent us was invited to argue issues from our challenge, and then the court shut the door.”

Jason Rantz wrote: “Washington Democrats wrote the income tax with a necessity clause specifically to block a referendum. The state Supreme Court blessed it. The attorney general then wrote the warning label. Public sector unions, funded by your tax dollars, are [bankrolling the campaign against repeal](https://the.news.wagop.org/link.php?AGENCY=FACT&M=14158524&N=32523&L=16618&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly9zZWF0dGxlcmVkLmNvbS93YXNoaW5ndG9uLXN0YXRlL29wcG9zaXRpb24tdG8td2EtaW5jb21lLXRheC1yZXBlYWwtbGFyZ2VseS1mdW5kZWQtYnktcHVibGljLXNlY3Rvci11bmlvbnMvNDExOTU0OD91dG1fY29udGVudD1DTVRReE5UZzFNalElM0Q=&hash=4950142041ef3bfd32aaa8127c650618271d8568cd9fb38a55543e91b5a5dc59). And now a judge has decided the sponsors of a citizen initiative do not need a hearing.”

The misleading PIID reads: “This measure would decrease funding for public K-12 education, higher education (including universities and community colleges), and human services (primarily healthcare).” That claim is impossible: the Democrats’ income tax scheme will not take effect until 2028, so repealing it cannot decrease funding that does not yet exist.

The Wall Street Journal Editorial Board likewise rebuked Attorney General Nick Brown’s description: “Enter Mr. Brown, who has written a misleading description of the initiative that will appear on the ballot: ‘This measure would decrease funding for public K-12 education, higher education (including universities and community colleges), and human services (primarily healthcare).’ Huh? The Democratic income tax hike won’t take effect until 2028. Pre-empting it and future increases can’t ‘decrease funding’ that doesn’t exist.”

More than 500,000 Washington voters signed petitions to qualify I-645 for the November ballot. Now all Washington voters must protect their voices by filing a complaint about Judge Chris Lanese's unethical and unprofessional behavior. Again, here’s the link: [https://www.cjc.state.wa.us/index.php?page=filing_a_complaint§ion;=file_online](https://the.news.wagop.org/link.php?AGENCY=FACT&M=14158524&N=32523&L=16619&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuY2pjLnN0YXRlLndhLnVzL2luZGV4LnBocD9wYWdlPWZpbGluZ19hX2NvbXBsYWludCZzZWN0aW9uPWZpbGVfb25saW5lJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNVFF4TlRnMU1qUSUzRA==&hash=8cb71983474320bf6ba702cbe45755f61c009a2e1d6e256f7121dd1bae76df58). When filing the complaint with the Commission on Judicial Conduct, refer to the case as "Let's Go Washington Challenge to I26-645 PIID." Make your voice heard! #

Our primary is today. President Trump is not on the ballot this November. And Republicans need to play defense in states like Ohio, Maine, North Carolina, and even Texas. |
---

Fellow Conservative,

Minnesota's U.S. Senate seat is open.

No incumbent. No decades-long war chest to outspend. Just a real opportunity for Republicans to flip a seat that's been out of reach for a generation.

That's exactly why I got in this race.

As a former Navy SEAL, I know what it takes to win when the odds say you shouldn't: preparation, discipline, and showing up when it counts. Right now, what counts is today, August 11 - our primary.

| | Hey, my opponent went on NBC News last week and was asked a simple question: _“...have you ever voted against the President's policies? Do you disagree with him anywhere?"_ _She couldn't come up with ONE._ Her voting record backs it up. **This Congress, she’s voted with Trump’s position 100% of the time.** **Here's what that has cost the people of this district:**
* Kiggans voted for the budget bill that stripped healthcare and food assistance from thousands of Virginians.
* She voted with Trump on the federal workforce cuts that hit Hampton Roads families directly.
* She also stayed silent while Trump's tariffs raised costs for the small businesses in this district.

Here's the choice in November, as plainly as I can put it: **A vote for Jen Kiggans is a vote for cowardice.** More rubber stamps. More silence. Join us as we have an in depth conversation with Apostate Ari a transitioned individual who is fighting back after his non reversible surgeries have brought him to where he is today. This brave individual had a come to God moment where he said I can't live like this and decided to research the history of where the trans-movement began. The more he learned the madder he got. Today Ari is working to educate anyone and everyone on the dangers of transitioning, who is behind the movement and what to do after the fact. For more about Ari and his work you can find him at his YouTube Channel [https://www.youtube.com/@ApostateAri](https://substack.com/redirect/8fc54a80-31b6-4405-9bd9-54f9e9373ac1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) also find his outlets at [https://linktr.ee/transphobichistorian](https://substack.com/redirect/3a00409e-5348-47e0-a365-5681e87cf6ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

What's the best kind of Testimony Tuesday? _The status update_. This week, I want to share a testimony from Chicago a year-in-the-making. Last year, a man went viral for being baptized in the back of a pickup truck. And this weekend, he was back, and had an amazing update on his year walking with Jesus!
This is the pick-me-up you need today!

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: Our 6-point gap has closed to 1
disclaimer_text: Paid for by McBride for Delaware
body:
We’ve got to give this everything we’ve got, Texas.
Friend, look at this:
[](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=partner_ms_gh_em_mcbride_20260811.lhTUOG&refcode=em20260811-3671&t=1&akid=3671%2E21716%2EAsQdg6)
Eight weeks ago, this same poll had us trailing Greg Abbott by 6 points. **Today, that gap is down to 1.**
This is a completely separate survey than the Fox News poll that broke last week — Texas Pulse, conducted by Texas A&M’s Bush School for Government — _and it found the exact same thing:_ **Abbott 46%, me at 45%.**
Two different pollsters showing identical results in the same week is not a fluke. It’s a trend. [**Split a donation right now between Sarah McBride and my campaign to help us take the lead in this race.**](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=partner_ms_gh_em_mcbride_20260811.lhTUOG&refcode=em20260811-3671&t=2&akid=3671%2E21716%2EAsQdg6)
Here's what’s changed since the June poll showing us down 6: Texans are getting to know me. In June, more than half of voters didn’t know enough about me to have an opinion. Now it’s less than a third. And the more they learn, the more they like what they see. **My favorability has climbed from a net +13 to a net +18 in just two months.**
Meanwhile, Abbott’s numbers are going the other way. His approval rating is underwater, 47-51%. His favorability is underwater, 46-50%. Twelve years as governor, and Texans are done.
I don’t need to tell you why. You’re living it. Rising grocery bills, rising premiums, rising property taxes. Data centers flooding our state. And a governor who’s spent over a decade protecting the people at the top instead of the Texans footing the bill.
**We have momentum. We do not have the resources to match it — not yet, not without your help.** Abbott’s campaign has nearly $70 million sitting in the bank, and they are going to spend every dollar of it trying to make sure Texans who are ready for change don’t show up in November.
[**Can you split a $5 donation right now between Sarah McBride and my campaign to help us keep closing this gap and finally defeat Greg Abbott in November?** ](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=partner_ms_gh_em_mcbride_20260811.lhTUOG&refcode=em20260811-3671&amount=5&t=3&akid=3671%2E21716%2EAsQdg6)
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=partner_ms_gh_em_mcbride_20260811.lhTUOG&amount=5&refcode=em20260811-3671&t=22&akid=3671%2E21716%2EAsQdg6)**
Two pollsters had us down one single point this week. We can win this, I feel it in my bones. Now let’s make it happen.
Gina

Now, the GOP and AIPAC are already raising money from their corporate and right-wing megadonors to prop up his Trump-endorsed MAGA opponent and flip this seat red — but they can’t stop a people-powered movement that knows what it’s fighting for. Justin is running to be an unapologetic champion for working families and bring real change home for South Memphis. He knows that people are tired of settling for Do-Nothing politicians on both sides of the aisle selling them out to corporate interests while they struggle to get by. He’s the fighter that Tennessee needs in Congress — and he’s ready to dismantle the status quo on day one. But to win on November 3rd, Justin needs you now, Peter. ---

Peter,

Minnesota's U.S. Senate seat is open.

No incumbent. No decades-long war chest to outspend. Just a real opportunity for Republicans to flip a seat that's been out of reach for a generation.

That's exactly why I got in this race.

As a former Navy SEAL, I know what it takes to win when the odds say you shouldn't: preparation, discipline, and showing up when it counts. Right now, what counts is today, August 11 - our primary.

https://rokhanna.com [https://rokhanna.com]
Peter,
Big Tech companies are pushing data centers into communities across the country—and making working families pay the price.
AI companies bypass environmental reviews, run backup generators as private power plants, strain local water supplies, and drive up infrastructure and electricity costs for residents.
I believe in the potential of AI. But technological progress cannot come at the expense of the communities asked to host it.
Local residents deserve the power to say no. And when communities do welcome data centers, they deserve strong protections for their homes, farmland, water, and utility bills.
Sign if you agree: Local communities have the right to reject data centers. I’m introducing a Data Center Bill of Rights [https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/06/khanna-to-introduce-data-center-bill-of-rights-in-ai-power-plants-fight.html], a resolution that:
✅ Bans data centers in residential areas and farmland
✅ Gives communities the right to oppose data center projects through a transparent public process
✅ Allows communities to demand that utility bills do not increase
✅ Protects statewide moratoriums on data center construction until protective measures can be put in place to prevent rising energy costs and protect local water supplies
✅ Requires data centers to use clean and reliable energy and meet pollution limits
No community should have to accept a data center it doesn’t want. No family should have to subsidize Big Tech’s AI boom.

# **[OpenAI loses another Altman insider as the $852 billion IPO machine keeps shedding talent](https://substack.com/redirect/5232fa4e-c2e9-4800-a6df-078b291a4f99?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Another one bites the dust at OpenAI. Brad Lightcap, eight-year veteran and former COO who scaled the go-to-market army from 50 to over 700, just walked after shifting to special projects. This is no isolated exit. Fidji Simo gone last month, three more in April. Sam's inner circle is thinning right as they try to justify that monster $852 billion valuation for the IPO.
* **Winners?** Denise Dresser inheriting the revenue throne and rivals vacuuming experienced operators who already know how to turn ChatGPT hype into enterprise contracts.
* **Losers?** OpenAI shareholders and IPO underwriters betting on rock-solid leadership while Altman's closest confidantes keep vanishing when the real money hits the table.
* **Next?** More exits before the roadshow. Pure-play AI labs keep bleeding talent while hyperscalers hoard the compute and the power.

This continues the pure-lab pressure I flagged OpenAI and Anthropic the cash-burning losers versus in-house hyperscalers. Building an $852 billion paper empire is one thing. Holding the operators when the ticker is about to light up is another. The easy money phase is over. Watch the door spin.

# **[Wall Street just greenlit Jensen's $500 billion AI factory money machine](https://substack.com/redirect/5232fa4e-c2e9-4800-a6df-078b291a4f99?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Jensen Huang just pulled the ultimate power move. He lined up Goldman, BlackRock, Blackstone, KKR, Apollo and Brookfield to raise $500 billion-plus of third-party capital for AI factories. GPU racks that cost $3 million apiece are now "revenue-generating assets" you can securitize. Hyperscalers already dumped over $150 billion this year. Nvidia can optionally backstop 25% of every loan. Classic.
* **Winners?** Nvidia first and last, plus every private credit shop collecting fees on the biggest infrastructure build-out in history while locking in CUDA architectures (Compute Unified Device Architecture.)
* **Losers?** Corporate balance sheets that were going cash-flow negative and any late-cycle AI lab still begging for equity at nosebleed valuations.
* **Next?** The first structured deals close, leverage piles on, and the money train keeps the GPU shortage alive longer than the bears want.

This is the logical next chapter after the _c_ orporate books were maxed. Now Wall Street takes the paper. Jensen turned the AI binge into an asset class overnight. The ones who control the factories and the financing win. Everyone else rents.

# **[Polymarket cleans house with Wall Street and FBI talent ahead of the fall volume boom](https://substack.com/redirect/5232fa4e-c2e9-4800-a6df-078b291a4f99?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Polymarket just hired Bird founder Travis VanderZanden as CGO, Robinhood compliance, Coinbase regs, Nasdaq risk and an FBI intel chief while ripping up the marketing playbook that triggered the CFTC probe. They're buttoning up the U.S. exchange for NFL kickoff in September and the November midterms after World Cup volumes died. Smart professionalization before the money flood.
* **Winners?** VanderZanden and the compliance crew who just got paid to turn a crypto casino into a real exchange before the volumes explode.
* **Losers?** The old cowboy promo partners who got cut and any rival still flying without regulatory armor.
* **Next?** September-November volume surge. Survive the CFTC and the $20 billion-plus raise prints hard.

This is how you graduate from sideshow to platform. Clean the marketing mess, stack grown-ups, then ride the two biggest event cycles of the year. The ones who get regulated before the stampede own the upside. Load the survivors.

# [Airbnb CEO](https://substack.com/redirect/5232fa4e-c2e9-4800-a6df-078b291a4f99?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[says one person can build a billion-dollar company and AI just made it real](https://substack.com/redirect/5232fa4e-c2e9-4800-a6df-078b291a4f99?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky just called AI the fourth and biggest computing window, bigger than the PC, the internet and mobile combined. He claims a one-person billion-dollar company is possible and maybe already exists while he's coding with Claude himself. Classic founder hype, but the leverage is real. Software agents collapse the headcount needed to scale.
* **Winners?** Solo technical founders and lean operators who weaponize AI agents instead of hiring armies. Airbnb if the super-app pivot lands.
* **Losers?** Bloated tech companies still paying for layers of middle management that AI just made redundant.
* **Next?** Capital floods toward ultra-lean AI-native startups while the old giants keep cutting.

When one sharp operator plus agents can replace a 50-person team, the cost structure of every software business resets. Chesky's right that the barrier just collapsed. The money flows to the ones who adapt fastest and fire the rest. Watch the one-man bands, some of them are about to print.
* * *
* * *
# **[Joby drops $500 million on defense tech while the air taxi dream takes a back seat](https://substack.com/redirect/5232fa4e-c2e9-4800-a6df-078b291a4f99?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Joby just spent $450 million cash and $50 million in stock to buy Resonant Sciences and its defense RF and mission systems. Stock dropped 6.5% premarket on the cash outlay. They're securing 1 million square feet of Ohio manufacturing and a dedicated defense unit while commercial eVTOL stays the long game. Wars are funding the bridge.
* **Winners?** Joby management locking real revenue pipelines and any shareholder who buys the dip for the dual-use upside.
* **Losers?** Pure commercial air-taxi dreamers who wanted no military dilution and the weak hands who sold the fear.
* **Next?** Deal closes first half 2027. Defense contracts start hitting and the dual-use story re-rates the stock higher.

The market hates cash leaving the building. Today. I love it. Commercial air taxis are still a multi-year science project. Pentagon budgets are real and growing. This is how a story stock becomes a business. Follow the money into defense, ignore the noise on the tape.

White excelled at basketball and recieved a scholarship to play basketball at the University of Minnesota, and later transferred to Iowa State. He would go on to make Dean's List while receiving All Big-12 first-team honors and many other basketball awards. After being selected 16th overall by The Houston Rockets in the NBA draft, White began to voice concerns about the NBA’s collective bargaining agreement (CBA), specifically regarding mental health policy, which at the time did not exist. body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
Recently I had my 56th birthday. And I have to tell you — I've never felt better in my life.
A year ago, I weighed over 360 pounds.
In late June, somewhere between knocking doors in the Louisiana heat, crisscrossing this great state from Lake Charles to Monroe, and putting in the kind of miles on my feet that I used to put on my tractor — I stepped on the scale at 290. That’s more than 70 pounds gone, y’all.
My doctor is happy. My team is happy. And I won't lie to you — I'm pretty happy too.
[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
But here's what's funny about this whole thing. When I decided to run for Senate, I didn't set out to get in shape. I set out to fight for Louisiana because somewhere along the way, they stopped fighting for us.
Every morning, I think about the people I met the day before. The farmer in northeast Louisiana who doesn't know how he'll make it through another season. The woman working two jobs who still can't afford her insulin. The young person who loves Louisiana but can't see a future here anymore.
My name is Jamie Davis, I’m the Democratic nominee for the US Senate in Louisiana. I'm 70 pounds lighter. I'm healthier than I've been in years. I won the runoff by a landslide. They are calling our campaign “the miracle on the Mississippi ” and I wake up every single morning with a fire in my belly I haven't felt since I was a young man working alongside my father on our farm.
I'm not a man who asks for much on his birthday. But today I'm going to ask for one thing.
Will you drop a donation to my campaign and Resist Reclaim Rebuild like I've been dropping these pounds out on the campaign trail? Chip in $56 for my 56th birthday, or $70 for the 70 pounds I’ve dropped! And if that’s too much, a donation of $5 or $10 will go a longgg way towards flipping this seat. The amount doesn’t matter because they will add up. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
DONATE TODAY TO HELP US WIN! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
Thank you for everything you’ve done to get this campaign to where it is today. I couldn’t have asked for a better birthday week.

clean_body: [] Recently I had my 56th birthday. And I have to tell you — I've never felt better in my life. A year ago, I weighed over 360 pounds. In late June, somewhere between knocking doors in the Louisiana heat, crisscrossing this great state from Lake Charles to Monroe, and putting in the kind of miles on my feet that I used to put on my tractor — I stepped on the scale at 290. That’s more than 70 pounds gone, y’all. My doctor is happy. My team is happy. And I won't lie to you — I'm pretty happy too. [] [] But here's what's funny about this whole thing. When I decided to run for Senate, I didn't set out to get in shape. I set out to fight for Louisiana because somewhere along the way, they stopped fighting for us. Every morning, I think about the people I met the day before. The farmer in northeast Louisiana who doesn't know how he'll make it through another season. The woman working two jobs who still can't afford her insulin. The young person who loves Louisiana but can't see a future here anymore. My name is Jamie Davis, I’m the Democratic nominee for the US Senate in Louisiana. I'm 70 pounds lighter. I'm healthier than I've been in years. I won the runoff by a landslide. They are calling our campaign “the miracle on the Mississippi ” and I wake up every single morning with a fire in my belly I haven't felt since I was a young man working alongside my father on our farm. I'm not a man who asks for much on his birthday. But today I'm going to ask for one thing. Will you drop a donation to my campaign and Resist Reclaim Rebuild like I've been dropping these pounds out on the campaign trail? Chip in $56 for my 56th birthday, or $70 for the 70 pounds I’ve dropped! And if that’s too much, a donation of $5 or $10 will go a longgg way towards flipping this seat. The amount doesn’t matter because they will add up. [] DONATE TODAY TO HELP US WIN! >> [] Thank you for everything you’ve done to get this campaign to where it is today. I couldn’t have asked for a better birthday week. (via RRR) [] Resist Reclaim Rebuild is an organization committed to helping Democrats win up and down the ballot, nationwide. Campaigns should be a space for friendship, creativity, and courage.
Like Joel said at our concert after we sang Arlo Guthrie and Pete Seegerʼs "The Garden Song,” when you plant a garden you usually donʼt get to choose what soil youʼre working with, but you show up and you work it anyway.
You take it inch by inch and row by row, and thatʼs exactly what weʼre doing in this campaign. Weʼre writing postcards, knocking on doors, making phone calls. **And inch by inch, row by row, we are making this garden grow.**
Each of us has a place in this work. Weʼve been told a different story in politics for a long time. A story that politics is for people at a table in some far-away room, but itʼs not. Itʼs for this room, and this table, and for all the people sitting around it.
**Thereʼs a place for us and thereʼs a time for us, and that place is Washington, D.C. and that time is _NOW_.**
Iʼve got four days to raise $10,000, so I can get another mailer out to the district. We want everyone to see and hear and feel what an incredible group of courageous and creative friends can accomplish when we work together.

subject: It’s a team effort
body:
You have an opportunity to make an impact today – not just on your own behalf but for the person who would like to, but can’t.
|
# [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1003&source=&t=1&akid=2661%2E124072%2E9Cm-_Y)
| | | |
---
Peter,
One of our team’s core beliefs is that not everyone can support Roy in the same way, _and that’s what makes a grassroots campaign so special._
Some folks knock doors on the weekends. Some make calls after a long shift. Some share Roy's plan to make stuff cost less with a neighbor, show up to an event or simply keep reading and staying informed. Some donate what they can, when they can.
All of those are real forms of support, and we're grateful for every ounce we get.
However, some people can't do any of those things right now. That’s okay. Maybe they're working two jobs. Maybe money is tight this month. Maybe life is just a lot at the moment. They still believe in this campaign – they just can't chip in today.
_That’s where you come in._
[**_If you’re one of the people who does have a few bucks to spare right now, we’re asking you to give $5 or anything you can: not just on your own behalf but for the person who can’t. Your contribution today will help carry the whole team across the finish line in November – the volunteer, the neighbor and the person rooting for us from the stands who wishes they could do more._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1003&amount=5&t=8&akid=2661%2E124072%2E9Cm-_Y)

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

_**by David Shuster**_
Donald Trump is cornered on Iran. And now, it's only a matter of time before the old rotting Orange man forces the United States into an epic economic catastrophe or geopolitical humiliation.
Regardless of whether Trump keeps bombing Iran or pulls U.S. forces out of the Persian gulf and declares victory, the results will not change. The Iranian regime is still there. The Strait of Hormuz, which was open before the war, is now an Iranian bargaining chip. The Iranian nuclear question remains unresolved. American weapons stockpiles have been chewed down. And the Republican party is approaching the midterm elections with all the joy of a skydiver who just discovered their parachute is decorative (or a tanker ship captain who has been told the Strait of Hormuz is safe).
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.VHx-GYeD7ikR2mhFqlRKGRTiPrNc7fX0Y8w9P4SwMtw?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=210674422)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/37c08491-da2e-46f7-8ad0-7ef5cab107c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
There is no way Trump can avoid the crash or fix any of this. If he keeps bombing Iran, the regime will keep the Strait of Hormuz blocked (and perhaps escalate across the Persian gulf) moving the globe closer to a massive energy shock. If Trump accepts Iran's terms for opening the Strait, including the regime collecting millions of dollars in tolls on each ship, Trump will own a historic loss.
Whichever path Trump chooses is not going to be a U.S. victory.
Trump went to war insisting that Iran's nuclear ambitions were intolerable. Trump's demand, repeated by all of his cabinet secretaries and GOP sycophants, was maximalist and magnificently simple: Iran must surrender.
Now, according to reports, Trump has told aides he may drop the nuclear demand in order to get out of the war.

body:

Hey Peter,
The Joint Economic Committee [https://www.jec.senate.gov/public/index.cfm/democrats/press-releases?ID=62244B52-3584-44FB-AA68-6062F0BBC9DE] found that American farmers have spent $1.4 billion more on diesel fuel alone since the start of the war with Iran for spring planting than they did last year. In North Carolina, it costs $260 more to fill up a typical tractor.
Out here in our district, farmers are feeling the effects of the senseless decisions in Washington. From the start of the current administration's term, tariffs have increased the prices for farm equipment and fertilizer. With the increase in fuel costs to run operations, the farm economy is in a tough spot.
Over the course of the campaign, I’ve heard a lot of different things from a lot of different folks. One thing that most everyone has agreed on, regardless of party affiliation, is that increases in the cost of living are making it hard to make ends meet.
Farming is a critical part of North Carolina’s economy. Farms and farmers feed our neighbors and provide us with the essentials we need.
Farmers (and all of us) deserve a government that will look out for their needs - and enact policies that make life more, not less affordable. When I get to Washington, I’ll be advocating for our farmers (and everyone else in NC-13) because I know that the decisions Congress makes have lasting impacts on every one of us.
I need your help to make sure I can get to Washington this November. With less than 3 months until Election Day, can I count on your donation to keep our momentum strong? The spending gap is only going to get bigger.
# [](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1&akid=8250%2E582294%2Ea9ZuKn)
This is bad.
**John Sununu and the Senate Republicans just launched _a new_ coordinated ad on TV in New Hampshire, and now we’re being outspent 3:1.**
But the worst part is they’re flooding the airwaves in media markets where our campaign can’t afford to be on the air – places where we need to reach key undecided voters.
Now we’re being forced to play catch-up.
**[If you’re invested in flipping the Senate blue, I need your help. Please rush $5 or whatever you can right now.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260811_3.RhU_ZM&refcode=em20260811-3&t=2&akid=8250%2E582294%2Ea9ZuKn)**

National Republican groups and outside organizations are all in to defeat me because they know this race could determine control of the Senate.
The spending gap is only going to get bigger. The attack ads are only going to get more unhinged. And the polls will continue to tighten.
**With so much on the line, we can’t let that happen.**
**[Will you chip in $5 today to help us reach these key voters and fight back against the barrage of outside Republican spending?](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260811_3.RhU_ZM&refcode=em20260811-3&t=4&akid=8250%2E582294%2Ea9ZuKn)**

There isn’t any time to wait. We need to close this gap now.
**[If you can please rush $5 or whatever you can today to help us get our message in front of Granite Staters, hold this Senate seat, and fight back against the GOP’s spending advantage.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260811_3.RhU_ZM&refcode=em20260811-3&t=5&akid=8250%2E582294%2Ea9ZuKn)**

We are kicking off another busy week on the trail and are excited to keep you in the loop with the latest updates and ways to stay connected. As always, don’t hesitate to reach out with any questions or if you want to learn more about how you can get involved. We’re happy to have you along for the ride. Onward to victory! | | | | | | | 🚓 Tom Kean Around NJ-07 on National Night Out 🚒 | | Nation Night Out last Tuesday was a busy one for Tom with stops in Watchung, Readington, Bernards Township, Long Hill, and Warren Township! It was a great opportunity to connect with residents and thank the local law enforcement officers and first responders who help keep our communities safe every day. In Bernards, Tom also presented the Township with $835,000 in federal funding for police communication upgrades. | | | | | | | | Field Update | | | | | | | One of the highlights of the week was visiting the Somerset County 4-H Fair with Mayor Moench and Councilman Kirsh. Tom had a great time catching up with residents, checking out the animals and events, and meeting some of the 4-H ambassadors. It was a wonderful opportunity to celebrate the dedication and commitment of all those who work so hard to keep this tradition alive! In the field, you might have seen some of our door knockers in Alexandria, Alpha, Bedminster, Berkeley Heights, Bernardsville, Bridgewater, Byram, Califon, Clinton Town, Hackettstown, Mountainside, Mine Hill, Phillipsburg, Pohatcong, Raritan Township, Roxbury, Scotch Plains, Somerville, Summit, Tewksbury, Washington Township, Westfield, orWharton this past week. subject: Door-Knocking Opportunities Across PA-14 fo Alan Bradstock
body:
| |
---
Dear Friend, If door-knocking is one of the ways you'd like to help elect Alan Bradstock to, there are two different canvassing programs available across PA-14: **Bradstock for Congress canvassing** and **PA Coordinated Campaign canvassing**. You can participate in either--or both--and there are options to knock with an organized group or on your own schedule. **Bradstock for Congress -- Persuading Voters** Our Bradstock canvasses focus on voters who have participated in recent elections but haven't firmly decided who they'll support for Congress. You'll meet a broader mix of Democrats, Independents, and Republicans. These conversations are about introducing Alan, listening to what matters to voters, answering questions, and earning their support. **This is the heart of our campaign's voter contact program and one of the most important ways you can help elect Alan.** **PA Coordinated Campaign -- Turning Out Voters** The PA Coordinated Campaign focuses primarily on Democratic and Democratic-leaning voters who are less likely to vote this November. These conversations are about making sure likely supporters understand what's at stake and turn out to vote. The two efforts complement each other: **Bradstock canvassing works to win over voters, while Coordinated canvassing works to make sure likely supporters vote.** Volunteers are welcome--and encouraged--to participate in both. **Canvass with a group or on your own schedule** Both campaigns hold organized canvasses throughout the district, generally on weekends. If you're new to door-knocking, these are a great place to start--you'll receive training, meet other volunteers, and learn how canvassing works. clean_body: | | Dear Friend, If door-knocking is one of the ways you'd like to help elect Alan Bradstock to, there are two different canvassing programs available across PA-14: Bradstock for Congress canvassing and PA Coordinated Campaign canvassing. You can participate in either--or both--and there are options to knock with an organized group or on your own schedule. Bradstock for Congress -- Persuading Voters Our Bradstock canvasses focus on voters who have participated in recent elections but haven't firmly decided who they'll support for Congress. You'll meet a broader mix of Democrats, Independents, and Republicans. These conversations are about introducing Alan, listening to what matters to voters, answering questions, and earning their support. This is the heart of our campaign's voter contact program and one of the most important ways you can help elect Alan. PA Coordinated Campaign -- Turning Out Voters The PA Coordinated Campaign focuses primarily on Democratic and Democratic-leaning voters who are less likely to vote this November. These conversations are about making sure likely supporters understand what's at stake and turn out to vote. The two efforts complement each other: Bradstock canvassing works to win over voters, while Coordinated canvassing works to make sure likely supporters vote. Volunteers are welcome--and encouraged--to participate in both. Canvass with a group or on your own schedule Both campaigns hold organized canvasses throughout the district, generally on weekends. If you're new to door-knocking, these are a great place to start--you'll receive training, meet other volunteers, and learn how canvassing works. To find upcoming canvassing opportunities, visit and search "Bradstock." You'll see nearby Bradstock and PA Coordinated Campaign canvassing opportunities. You also don't have to wait for an organized canvass. Fill out our form, tell us where you'd like to knock, and the Bradstock campaign will send you a walk list that you can complete whenever your schedule allows. subject: One. Point. Race.
body:
Taking back Texas this year is in our sights.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter, we just wanted to make sure you saw this message from Gina. With only one point separating Gina from Greg Abbott in the polls, there has never been a better time to show your support and help us take back Texas.
Read Gina’s message below — [**then chip in $5 to help her win the fight.**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260811_3_foxnewspoll.Qfsfdk&refcode=em20260811-1805&amount=5&t=1&akid=1805%2E299639%2EjjLNJ1)
— Original Message from Gina Hinojosa —
Peter —
I need you to sit with this number for a second: **one point.**
That's it. That's the entire gap between me and Greg Abbott right now, according to a brand-new Fox News poll — yes, Fox News.
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20260811_3_foxnewspoll.2_bIrb&refcode=em20260811-1805&t=2&akid=1805%2E299639%2EjjLNJ1)
In nearly twelve years as governor, through three elections, Greg Abbott has never faced a poll this close. _Not once._ His campaign has already spent over $54 million this cycle just to hang on to power. This poll says people aren’t buying what he’s selling anymore.
Here's why it's happening: Texans are falling behind financially, and they know exactly who's been in charge while it happened. Nearly 4 in 10 Texans say inflation is the top issue on their minds — **and after 12 years of Greg Abbott, they're done waiting around for things to get better.**
I'm not surprised. I've been hearing it at every stop — from Brownsville to Austin to Amarillo. Families are tired of watching their grocery bills and insurance premiums climb while Abbott hands billions to his donors.
**This 1-point poll shows that a new chapter for Texas is finally in reach.** But it’s not guaranteed. Turnout will decide this election. And Abbott's team knows it — they're going to spend the next 84 days doing everything they can to make sure Texans who are ready for change don't show up to the polls to vote. They will do anything to keep Texans from turning the page on his failed administration.
I can't outspend Greg Abbott, and I don’t need to. Our campaign can out-organize him, but that takes people like you stepping up right now to raise the resources we need to win this race.
**[Can you chip in $15 today to help us keep closing this gap and — finally — take back Texas?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1374?c0=em_ms_gh_20260811_3_foxnewspoll.i1o09D&refcode=em20260811-1805&t=3&akid=1805%2E299639%2EjjLNJ1)**
[Donate $15 »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1374?c0=em_ms_gh_20260811_3_foxnewspoll.i1o09D&refcode=em20260811-1805&t=22&akid=1805%2E299639%2EjjLNJ1)
We've never been this close. Let's make sure we don't waste this opportunity.
Gina

clean_body: A J6 patriot in desperate need of help, and wanted to pass it along... I received a heartbreaking message from Tyler Tew, a J6 patriot in desperate need of help, and wanted to pass it along. Peter, I received a heartbreaking message from Tyler Tew, a J6 patriot in desperate need of help, and wanted to pass it along. Tyler was a commercial pilot for 14 years... until Joe Biden 's TSA revoked his commercial pilot's license for "suspicion of terrorism" without even being charged with a crime. As a result of his lost pilot's salary, Tyler's family business is now in bankruptcy, and he, his wife, and their four kids are in desperate need of your support. I promised Tyler Stand in the Gap could help raise the funds he needs to get his company back on track, and Peter, Tyler's message absolutely broke my heart, and I'd like you to read it if you have a moment: My name is Tyler Tew. I was a commercial airline pilot for 14 years. I flew for SkyWest as a Captain and then Allegiant. I graduated from Utah State with an aviation degree and built my entire life around flying. I went to Washington on January 6 after being invited by friends. After President Trump's speech, I went to the Capitol. What I saw with my own eyes did not match what the news reported. On March 26, 2021, the TSA revoked my commercial pilot 's license for "suspicion of terrorism" and being a threat to the national airspace -- before I was ever charged with a crime and before any FBI interview.I spent $40,000 in legal fees. In June 2021, Allegiant fired me. Without my W-2 income, I could no longer sustain the construction company my wife and I owned. It is now in bankruptcy. We have four children. I now work 6-7 days a week in construction just to survive. I'm hoping Stand in the Gap can help us raise $25,000 to stabilize our family and our company during this bankruptcy and help us recover from the financial destruction caused by the sudden end of my aviation career. We have nowhere else to turn. Thank you for anything you can do. -- Tyler Tew Tyler's story is why we started our Fund Their Futures fundraising program, Peter. President Trump's pardons gave these patriots back their freedom... but that did NOT give them their lives, careers, businesses, or homes back. Tyler did everything right for decades... building a wonderful career, a small business, and a loving family. It all ended WITHOUT due process ... simply because the Far-Left wanted to punish him for supporting President Trump. Your gift today will give Tyler and his family breathing room. It'll help stabilize their company and help them keep a roof over their heads. Stand with the Gap exists specifically for moments like this... to when the legal fight is over, but the fight to survive has just begun. Too often, Stand in the Gap is the for the men and women who faced political persecution and financial ruin after January 6. We exist to share the burden and make it lighter ... and your generosity is quite literally the difference between families like Tyler's losing everything. That's why I hope you'll step forward, Peter. Even just a few dollars could make a critical difference. Thank you so much for helping them out. body:

Peter, it's
Election Day in Minnesota, and Ilhan is on the ballot.

Ilhan doesn't flinch. Not when Trump comes after her, not when his MAGA
allies pile on, not when billionaires work to silence her. She's one of
the fiercest fighters we've got in Congress.

She's in this fight for working families, for healthcare people can
actually afford, for reproductive freedom, for housing, for racial
justice. And Ilhan delivers.

Ilhan has brought over $65 million to Minnesota's Fifth for community
projects, delivered more than $550,000 in casework wins for her
constituents, and helped get the Inflation Reduction Act passed. She has
stood between the Liberian-American community and deportation, and has
never stopped speaking up for foreign policy rooted in justice.

That's what representation is supposed to look like. It's also exactly why
today's primary matters so much.

Showing up for leaders like her is the whole reason Squad Victory Fund
exists. We don't take corporate PAC checks, and that means progressive
champions like Ilhan win because grassroots movements like ours show up
for them. Today's one of those moments.

I voted to end the disastrous war in Iran.
Now, I'm asking you to say you’re with me by adding your name to my petition below: [https://go.marieforcongress.com/a/end-this-war-iran]
ADD YOUR NAME [https://go.marieforcongress.com/a/end-this-war-iran]
When I travel around Southwest Washington, I hear the same concerns over and over again.
* The cost of groceries
* Filling up their gas tanks
* Paying their bills and making ends meet
What I don't hear is people asking Congress to spend billions more taxpayer dollars on another prolonged war overseas.
Yet that's exactly what's happening.
Every day this conflict drags on, it risks costing American taxpayers billions of dollars while driving up the costs that working families already struggle to afford.
That's backward.
Our government should be focused on lowering costs, strengthening our communities, and solving problems here at home—not writing blank checks for an open-ended war with no clear strategy or end.
That's why I voted to end this war. And that's why I'm asking you to join me today.
If you agree that Congress should focus on lowering costs for working families instead of funding another endless war, add your name now: [https://go.marieforcongress.com/a/end-this-war-iran]
ADD YOUR NAME [https://go.marieforcongress.com/a/end-this-war-iran]
I have always believed that military action must be strategic, deliberate, and accountable to the American people.
This war is none of those things.
It's time to bring it to an end.
Thank you,
Marie Gluesenkamp Perez
P.S. If you'd like to take the next step, please consider contributing $10 or more [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?] to help me win re-election and take back Congress this November.

Peter,
Those were A.G. Holder’s words when he endorsed Democracy Defender Phil Weiser for governor in Colorado and denounced the Republican nominee. It takes a lot for him to throw shade like that. You should buckle up when we tell you exactly why.
Victor Marx, the Republican in the race, has boasted about his disturbing past. Besides being a conspiracist who believes the 2020 election was stolen, he has said that he “hunts demons.” He claims to have a black belt in “Cajun karate.” There are claims he participated in animal abuse and killed a man when he was a child.
**Peter, this isn’t normal.**
**Marx is a clear example of everything that’s wrong with the Republican Party. But he is also a good reminder of how crucial it is to elect strong Democracy Defenders with commonsense policies. name: Jane Fonda
subject: I’m alive because of science:
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jane Fonda Climate PAC, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee
body:
I won’t sit by while they attack science and truth.

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137056855/639492841/1328794144?refcode=ea.5227ed71-cf95-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ms=ea.5227ed71-cf95-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjUyMjdlZDcxLWNmOTUtZjExMS05YjMzLTAwMGQzYTExZmEzMCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=xr_IL7xujPmry-mgmSKkc64--AhrtWeYRxQVJ9BNZqQ=&emci=93c46ed8-cd95-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=5227ed71-cf95-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=4823105)
---
I know what it’s like to get the news. To sit in a doctor’s office, hear that awful “c-word” — cancer — and feel the ground shift beneath you. In 2022, I was diagnosed with non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma. I went through months of chemotherapy. But I was lucky. I had access to incredible doctors and effective treatments made possible by decades of medical research. I don’t take that for granted. Not for a second. This is why I can’t stay silent while Donald Trump and his administration work to tear down the protections that keep people from getting sick in the first place. Over the last 14 months, this administration has terminated roughly **2,300 National Institutes of Health research grants** — nearly **$3.8 billion** in funding erased, including at least **160 clinical trials** on cancer, HIV/AIDS, and chronic disease. Labs have closed. Scientists have been pushed out the door. And with every grant that disappears, so does our ability to turn discoveries into treatments that could save lives. What makes this worse? Trump and his allies’ war on science doesn’t stop at the laboratory door. They’re also giving Big Oil and corporate polluters free rein to pump more toxins into the air we breathe and the water we drink. I’m talking about reopening coal plants, weakening clean air protections, and reversing the foundation that’s allowed the federal government to regulate climate pollution for the last 15 years. **These decisions have consequences. They mean more people getting sick and more families forced to hear the kind of news no one ever wants to receive.** That’s why I’m not turning away from this fight. I know you’re tired, and it feels like hope is in short supply. I’m fighting those feelings, too, but _despair is not an option._ Cancer made me think even more about the time I have left and how I want to use it. I don’t want to look back with regrets. **I want to know that I did everything in my power to fight for the future — for our health and for the generations that come after us.** At JanePAC, we’re building the strongest possible defense by electing courageous leaders from utility boards all the way to Congress who believe in science and will fight like hell to protect our communities. **[We’re organizing in key states around the country to stop Donald Trump and his allies from pushing their deadly agenda at the state and local levels. clean_body: I won’t sit by while they attack science and truth. | I know what it’s like to get the news. To sit in a doctor’s office, hear that awful “c-word” — cancer — and feel the ground shift beneath you. In 2022, I was diagnosed with non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma. I went through months of chemotherapy. But I was lucky. I had access to incredible doctors and effective treatments made possible by decades of medical research. I don’t take that for granted. Not for a second. This is why I can’t stay silent while Donald Trump and his administration work to tear down the protections that keep people from getting sick in the first place. Over the last 14 months, this administration has terminated roughly 2,300 National Institutes of Health research grants — nearly $3.8 billion in funding erased, including at least 160 clinical trials on cancer, HIV/AIDS, and chronic disease. Labs have closed. Scientists have been pushed out the door. And with every grant that disappears, so does our ability to turn discoveries into treatments that could save lives. What makes this worse? Trump and his allies’ war on science doesn’t stop at the laboratory door. They’re also giving Big Oil and corporate polluters free rein to pump more toxins into the air we breathe and the water we drink. I’m talking about reopening coal plants, weakening clean air protections, and reversing the foundation that’s allowed the federal government to regulate climate pollution for the last 15 years. These decisions have consequences. They mean more people getting sick and more families forced to hear the kind of news no one ever wants to receive. That’s why I’m not turning away from this fight. I know you’re tired, and it feels like hope is in short supply. I’m fighting those feelings, too, but despair is not an option. Cancer made me think even more about the time I have left and how I want to use it. I don’t want to look back with regrets. I want to know that I did everything in my power to fight for the future — for our health and for the generations that come after us. subject: Primary Special Election Day
body:
Election Day is today. Help me reach every voter — and fuel the fight still ahead — before midnight. |
---

Fellow Patriot - Today is it.

The Primary Special Election for the United States Senate seat here in South Carolina, **[and I need your help in these final hours.](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=938e8d822e0f4750beeeb9d5fdd7ae0f&_e=irrPWeCRxmgPRMgPHzcw7NqCNL47nxG9yDpWATMKzZa58XZi_L9RDGwL1yGgjx7YsVLS1K3J78Ocdsrw3sir5sSGjOHhzYOJ_h2daXTtVICTTd6ienSOXr5fmMAa9-ZB9VgwG9yiuEmu4U6mlgOJRhJ8aGNhb4mTlcDxUeCp-LTbAawvr2mYku9JVOYPsJVfroG9cHDbJ6kBHlnpwRtvRnu8IgfRm8tBqejWqyq5iznOloU7E8oRlJzKwBtdX3hvq4hvtpLqYxuO_xrWK0QsgxP0oAmxb1lWkS-x9vzbNPXzJfRjxiiTkZtEsn2e9hPpg4wTdHzKbAFz4qjQSBP1D5MYyK3IZO9nrNn4hM7aGQl9VRA5g6fTWwmPzTsbtkrsdTSgL6nVZzN2x8OuRCbbBVLwSind90z6XG14OsMB-d3GhXnxGKfc2iYcMuAPU5OiUd7Km9IOmKJ_7dkwmECe2xzU9iwsdG5erPXWNek4lAiDtPyAZJOdb2xnBNG-RjZJfA9KQ2cYVvlHE5jCAm0DfCuNh1cD8XK6bje-SxGouj67CDA6iZ4EbHieB0cnjhkBTxO9a3jqaB5a7_FHjx6xW6YD9agj88_Ra1rQ6ySzx9HxvlcAvLiV6uTYPe7ixYi1doWxuTN_SALTw0YTw53taCxuP48hG7fhxoWp422EumCS4_26Lyku4aHs_D9uz16wadV8Wa_G7QbI7gbWAPd4iJVZegahazz5_8knCyOVROZM2uKW1vnJjAllLZTaKQoJLa9HQfsC2kvZv-VIeUuehA%3D%3D)**

I'm not a politician. I never expected to be running for office, and I never wanted to. I'm doing this because I'm answering President Trump's call to serve, and because I believe South Carolina deserves a fighter in the Senate.

Like Lindsey, I grew up in the back of a bar and liquor store, in one room. My parents worked every single day to make ends meet. There was no time for sickness and few vacations, because if the doors weren't open, no money was coming in.

That's the kind of work ethic I've carried my whole life, from running a state agency with 130 employees and a $90 million budget to turning it into a national model for helping people find work and live independently.
