clean_body: Election Day is today. Help me reach every voter — and fuel the fight still ahead — before midnight. | Fellow Patriot - Today is it. The Primary Special Election for the United States Senate seat here in South Carolina, I'm not a politician. I never expected to be running for office, and I never wanted to. I'm doing this because I'm answering President Trump's call to serve, and because I believe South Carolina deserves a fighter in the Senate. Like Lindsey, I grew up in the back of a bar and liquor store, in one room. My parents worked every single day to make ends meet. There was no time for sickness and few vacations, because if the doors weren't open, no money was coming in. That's the kind of work ethic I've carried my whole life, from running a state agency with 130 employees and a $90 million budget to turning it into a national model for helping people find work and live independently. I'm a mother, a grandmother, and a wife. I support the Right to Life. I believe in showing ID to vote. I oppose DEI. I stand for the national anthem, I believe our veterans are heroes, and I will always Back the Blue. President Trump wants a fighter in the Senate - that's why he's in my corner in this race, and why I'm asking you to be in it with me. Here's what I need from you right now, in the final hours before the polls close: If you live in South Carolina, make sure you vote today, and don't stop there. Call your friends, your family, your neighbors, your coworkers. Make sure they have a plan to get to the polls before midnight. Every vote we don't turn out tonight is a vote we can't get back. Every dollar raised today will help us build the momentum we need not only to win today but also to win in November. And I need to be honest with you: winning tonight is only the first step. After this Primary Special Election, we still have a long road ahead to the General Election, and this fight doesn't end when the polls close. I will need you again. But it starts with tonight. Help me finish strong. Thank you, Darline Graham P.S. I am the first woman United States senator in South Carolina history. Peter,

Lately, it feels like so many people have lost faith in our politics.

It's easy to understand why.

Too often, we see division instead of solutions. Politicians are looking for the next headline instead of the next opportunity to help working families. Powerful interests are looking out for themselves while everyday people are left behind.

That's not why I chose public service.

I ran for Congress because I believed families like mine, the daughter of Mexican immigrants who worked hard to build a better life, deserved a voice in Washington. And that's exactly what has guided me every day since.

I know we won't agree on every issue, but I believe we should always put the interests of our communities ahead of powerful special interests.

That's the kind of leadership I've tried to bring to Congress, and it's the kind of leadership I'll continue fighting for every single day. But I can't do it alone.

body:

Friend, the clock is ticking. **Republicans are making it clear they want to go after Social Security. **
In the name of “fixing” the Social Security benefits so many Americans rely on, they’re gutting it. Closing offices. Firing staff. Throwing up roadblocks that make it harder for older Americans to get the support they’ve earned.
**They’re trying trick after trick to keep seniors from getting the benefits from a program they’ve paid into for decades. And the GOP is hoping you won’t notice.**
I’m doing everything I can to fight to protect Social Security in the face of relentless Republican attacks, and I need to know where this team stands. I know you’re busy, but I wouldn’t reach out if this weren’t so urgent.

body:
Peter, it’s Peggy
Flanagan.

I’d like to tell you a story, but if you don’t have time, I’ll cut to the
chase: [ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/54783?c0=pj-em-20260811-1.9xxcmU&refcode=em20260811-6584&t=1001&akid=6584%2E420207%2EknSzTB ]Can you split a $15 donation between my campaign and Pramila
Jayapal to help us deliver for working families?

Growing up in Minnesota, my single mom and I relied on Section 8 housing,
SNAP, and Medicaid to get by.

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260811-1.CkXPTw&refcode=em20260811-6584&t=1002&akid=6584%2E420207%2EknSzTB ][IMG]

I still remember what it felt like to hand over that different-colored
lunch ticket at school, or to watch my mom stretch $20 to the end of the
month.

Back then, I didn’t realize that when my mom told me, “I already ate at
work,” it actually meant there wasn’t enough food for both of us.

I’ll never forget what that feels like — and I won't forget who I’m
fighting for.

Right now, the system feels rigged against working families. We are
looking at the first generation of young people who could be worse off
than their parents. To me, and to Pramila, that is unacceptable.

My Anishinaabe name means “Speaks with a Clear and Loud Voice Woman.” I’ve
spent my career trying to live up to that name by loudly taking on the big
fights to make life more affordable. If I’m privileged enough to be
Minnesota’s next Senator, I want you to know one thing:

I’m not going to Washington by myself — we’re all going together.

But crypto bros, AIPAC, and dark money groups don’t want to let us disrupt
the status quo. They are doing everything they can to defeat me.

They’re even spending $142,857 a DAY on ads attacking me and propping up
my opponent. I’m not afraid,
Peter. I’ve never backed down
from a challenge before.

But I don’t say this lightly,
Peter: If there’s ever been a
time I could use your donation, it’s today.

I exist because of the generosity and the grit of my neighbors. Now, I’m
humbly asking you for your help again. [ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/54783?c0=pj-em-20260811-1.9xxcmU&refcode=em20260811-6584&t=1003&akid=6584%2E420207%2EknSzTB ]Will you chip in $15 or whatever

Chi miigwech (big thank you)!

💚 Peggy

clean_body: Now he wants credit for fighting it. | | Peter, Last week we brought you the problem with Flock cameras and how they have exploded across the country under Trump and Keith Self's extremist Congress. The more we dig, the worse it gets. In 2025, a Texas sheriff's office ran a search across more than 83,000 of these cameras, reaching into states like Washington and Illinois where abortion is perfectly legal, to hunt down a woman who had self-managed her abortion. A cop in one state used a private company's camera network to chase a woman for something that is a basic human right where she was standing. That happened in May of last year, and the country is only now reckoning with what a tool like that can do to any of us. And if you thought that case was a one-off, think again. One eagle-eyed TikTok creator recently revealed a set of Flock cameras monitoring the access points of a local Planned Parenthood in Plano. | Now that public backlash against Flock is growing, my opponent is scrambling to take credit for fixing the very mess he made. Self just rolled out a bill he calls the PRIVACY Act, and it is a smokescreen. His bill does nothing to address the fact that last year he voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill that tried to bar states from regulating AI for a decade, the exact technology that turns a wall of cameras into a machine that tracks your every move. He cast that vote knowing full well how these camera networks were already being abused. There are already 600 of these cameras up across Dallas and plenty more going up all over TX-03. Keith Self helped open those floodgates, and a shiny new bill does not undo the votes that got us here. I have spent my whole career defending the Constitution, 20 years in uniform and every day since as a public advocate, and that oath does not expire. It covers your right to worship, your right to speak, and your right to move through your own life without the government logging everywhere you go. Keith Self forgot that promise. I never will. body:
In June, the National Capital Planning Commission voted 9 to 1 to advance Trump's arch
#
Peter, this is Paul Eaton, Major General, U.S. Army, Retired.
In June, the National Capital Planning Commission voted 9 to 1 to advance Trump's arch — 250 feet tall, planned for Memorial Circle, sitting directly in the sightline between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery.
The commission takes it up again next month. One more vote, and they give the green light.
I've spent enough of my life on the grounds of Arlington to know its gravity. My father, killed in action during the Vietnam War, is buried there. That sightline was designed on purpose — a quiet symbol of a reunited country. Trump wants to put a monument to himself in the middle of it, and he is almost out of hurdles standing between him and breaking ground.
So we're asking for $5.
$5 because the lead up to that next commission meeting is our next opportunity to make some noise about this arch and rally the public against it.
$5 because Vietnam veterans are already suing to stop this ridiculous arch, and they shouldn’t have to fight alone.
$5 because whatever you can give, right now, matters more than the amount itself.
[**Can we count on you? Chip in that $5 and help us raise enough hell that they think twice before handing Trump his arch.**](https://act.votevets.org/go/2927?c0=vv-pac-em-aug26.uvTq9l&refcode=em260811-1-360&t=1&akid=35451%2E3013755%2EEo_g1W)

Meet Joe Males:

**Joe Males is a Marine Veteran, small business-owner, city council member, and most importantly, a father. Throughout his life, he has put service to his community at the forefront of his life’s mission.

Shortly after turning 18, Joe enlisted in the Marine Corps. He attended boot camp in Camp Pendleton and later served overseas in the Philippines and Guam. After being discharged as a Sergeant, Joe remained committed to supporting his fellow veterans. He took on leadership roles in his local Elks Lodge and American Legion post, working to ensure veterans in the community had the resources and support they deserved.

Following his time in the Marine Corps, Joe carried his strong work ethic and discipline into the field of computer networking services. He started in an entry-level position, worked his way through multiple leadership roles, and in 1996, he built his own business from the ground up. Joe knows firsthand the hard work and sacrifice of this journey, and he’s determined to make it easier for hardworking Americans to do the same.

Joe’s entry into politics was deeply personal. After his son, a Marine who followed in his footsteps, was tragically murdered back home, Joe vowed that no parent should have to endure such a loss. Determined to take a stand for public safety and the rule of law, he ran for Hemet City Council to help ensure no other family would experience the same tragedy.

Thank you, Joe Males Meet Joe Males: Joe Males is a Marine Veteran, small business-owner, city council member, and most importantly, a father. Throughout his life, he has put service to his community at the forefront of his life’s mission. Shortly after turning 18, Joe enlisted in the Marine Corps. He attended boot camp in Camp Pendleton and later served overseas in the Philippines and Guam. After being discharged as a Sergeant, Joe remained committed to supporting his fellow veterans. He took on leadership roles in his local Elks Lodge and American Legion post, working to ensure veterans in the community had the resources and support they deserved. Following his time in the Marine Corps, Joe carried his strong work ethic and discipline into the field of computer networking services. He started in an entry-level position, worked his way through multiple leadership roles, and in 1996, he built his own business from the ground up. Joe knows firsthand the hard work and sacrifice of this journey, and he’s determined to make it easier for hardworking Americans to do the same. Joe’s entry into politics was deeply personal. After his son, a Marine who followed in his footsteps, was tragically murdered back home, Joe vowed that no parent should have to endure such a loss. Determined to take a stand for public safety and the rule of law, he ran for Hemet City Council to help ensure no other family would experience the same tragedy. During his tenure on the City Council, Joe has led numerous initiatives to improve infrastructure, drive business growth, and keep neighborhoods safe and clean. He takes pride in his ability to collaborate with fellow council members and get results, even when facing different perspectives. Joe is committed to bringing this same results-driven approach to Washington D.C., to ensure the voices of the American people are heard and their needs are met. Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

body:
https://elfrethformaryland.com/ [https://elfrethformaryland.com/]
Friend,

When far-right extremists brought H.R. 21—the Reproductive Health Care Surveillance Act—to the House floor, their intent wasn't to help families. It was to threaten doctors and nurses with prison time for providing life-saving healthcare.

As I stood on the House floor to vote NO, I didn't see an abstract policy debate. I thought of Emma.

Five months into her pregnancy, Emma and her husband Zach got the call every parent dreads: severe, life-threatening anomalies meant her pregnancy could not safely continue.

But because Republican politicians in her home state of South Carolina passed draconian abortion bans, Emma couldn't get medical care in her own community.

She was forced to flee hundreds of miles to Maryland just to find a doctor who could safely treat her.

I will not allow far-right politicians to strip away our fundamental freedoms. If you can, donate today to help me keep Maryland a safe state where everyone can get the care we deserve → [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/SEMD-03-Email-Aug2026-FR-ProtectingRepro?&refcode=E31088-20260811-ProtectingRepro-SL-2026Race&amount=25]

I am proud that Maryland stands as a sanctuary for reproductive freedom. I’m proud to have voted while in the Maryland Senate to make that vital protection become law. But anti-choice zealots in Washington won't stop until they outlaw care in all 50 states.

Just last week, President Trump nominee and Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche told faith leaders that he plans to make “the Dobbs decision permanent in every state,” implying that he would push to override states’ rights to decide what works best for them.

Extreme anti-choice politicians are determined to drag our country backward, but we have something stronger: a dedicated grassroots movement ready to hold them accountable.

If you are ready to help me defend access to abortion in Maryland, make a $25 contribution to our campaign today → [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/SEMD-03-Email-Aug2026-FR-ProtectingRepro?&refcode=E31088-20260811-ProtectingRepro-SL-2026Race&amount=25]

Thank you for standing with me in this fight.

Onward,

Sarah Elfreth

Millions of students are about to spend another year studying algebra, literature, and history without ever touching the one system that will follow every one of them for the rest of their lives: the tax code.

_Where do students learn what a tax bracket actually is?_
_Who explains the difference between a sales tax and an income tax before they ever see one on a receipt or a paycheck?_

Most schools simply don't have the time, and most curricula don't have the
material.

That's the gap Tax Foundation has spent years working to close.

I'm Daniel Bunn, President of Tax Foundation. Since 1937, Tax Foundation has been the nonpartisan, independent source lawmakers and journalists turn to when they need the facts on tax policy.

A student who understands the tax code has an advantage that most of their peers won't have.

They'll understand...
* Why a sales tax holiday isn't good policy
* That tax brackets don't work the way most people think
* How the tax choices made in state capitals and in Washington affect their own future paycheck, tuition bill, or small business

That kind of literacy shapes how someone votes, how they manage their finances, and how well they can distinguish sound policy from a political talking point.

Most students won't get any of that in a classroom.

Personal finance and economics requirements vary widely from state to state, and even where they exist, the tax code rarely gets more than a passing mention. Most of what students find is either buried in a textbook, locked behind a paid course, or shaped by whoever is doing the explaining.

Outside of TaxEDU, there are few, if any, no-cost, nonpartisan resources designed specifically to teach taxes.

clean_body: Friend, Millions of students are about to spend another year studying algebra, literature, and history without ever touching the one system that will follow every one of them for the rest of their lives: the tax code. Where do students learn what a tax bracket actually is? Who explains the difference between a sales tax and an income tax before they ever see one on a receipt or a paycheck? Most schools simply don't have the time, and most curricula don't have the material. That's the gap Tax Foundation has spent years working to close. I'm Daniel Bunn, President of Tax Foundation. Since 1937, Tax Foundation has been the nonpartisan, independent source lawmakers and journalists turn to when they need the facts on tax policy. We created TaxEDU, our free education initiative, to provide this same foundation to students, teachers, or anyone willing to learn more about taxes. TaxEDU puts a glossary of more than 100 tax terms, classroom-ready primers, and explainer videos--such as "How Do Tax Brackets Work?"-- in front of any student who wants to understand the system. None of it leans left or right, and none of it sits behind a paywall. But keeping it free depends entirely on people like you. That 's why I'm asking you to make a gift to Tax Foundation today. A student who understands the tax code has an advantage that most of their peers won't have. They'll understand... Why a sales tax holiday isn't good policy That tax brackets don't work the way most people think * How the tax choices made in state capitals and in Washington affect their own future paycheck, tuition bill, or small business That kind of literacy shapes how someone votes, how they manage their finances, and how well they can distinguish sound policy from a political talking point. Most students won't get any of that in a classroom. Personal finance and economics requirements vary widely from state to state, and even where they exist, the tax code rarely gets more than a passing mention. Most of what students find is either buried in a textbook, locked behind a paid course, or shaped by whoever is doing the explaining. Outside of TaxEDU, there are few, if any, no-cost, nonpartisan resources designed specifically to teach taxes. Your gift today helps make sure the next generation of taxpayers, business owners, and lawmakers has access to that resource. Please make a gift to support Tax Foundation today. Thank you, Daniel Bunn President and CEO Tax Foundation Tax Foundation is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit educational organization. Any donations made to Tax Foundation are tax-deductible to the full extent allowable by law.

name: Kailee for Congress
subject: Official invitation for Peter
body:
I want you beside me as we build this campaign from the ground up.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/DO1fUtWhjYg?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
Peter, I wanted to personally thank you for joining our campaign.
I grew up in Auburn in a blue-collar family. My dad spent 41 years working as a correctional officer. My mom is a nurse who cares for Alzheimer’s patients. I worked multiple jobs to put myself through school, became the first person in my family to earn a four-year degree, and spent years paying off my student loans.
_I know what it means to work hard, do everything right, and still wonder why it keeps getting harder to get ahead._
**That is why I’m running for Congress: to lower costs, protect our communities, defend our farmers and small businesses, and make Central New York a place where our children can build their futures.**
But this campaign doesn't just belong to me. It belongs to every New Yorker who is ready to fight for something better.
_That means you, too._
Because you joined us at the very beginning, I’m inviting you to become an official FOUNDING MEMBER of Kailee Buller for Congress.
---
| [ACCEPT YOUR FOUNDING MEMBERSHIP >> ](https://us.list-manage.com/1ABnn6IYxWw?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
---
| |
I want you to understand the responsibility that comes along with being a Founding Member.
These will be the people we rely on the most to share opinions and keep us in touch with every little thing that goes on in Central New York. We'll need to know who needs our help and who could use a yard sign, or a sticker, or anything like that.
We'll also be keeping you in the loop with all of the exclusive campaign-only memos and polls to keep you up-to-date on any important news the campaign receives.
_You'll be our best tool for sharing important updates with your friends and family._
Can I count on you to do that, Peter?
I hope so.
[**And I hope you accept the invitation to become an OFFICIAL Founding Member of the campaign.**](https://us.list-manage.com/e7Gx9FeYcwc?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
Once you do, keep an eye on your inbox for any exclusive news.
And Peter, heads up...
**This offer won’t last long. Our Founding Member invite is only going to our staunchest supporters, so make sure you sign up as soon as possible.**

Now it 's our turn to apply the pressure that removes her from office entirely. Here's what most people don't realize about this race. It's not just about who sits in the Governor's office in Phoenix. What happens next in Arizona determines what happens in America. Losing Arizona means statistically losing the next presidential race... Which means losing the census fight against the Democratic Socialist of America in 2030... Which means losing the country for the next 20-30 years, possibly for good. The talking heads on cable news want you focused on this week's headlines and next month's jobs report. clean_body: Election Day is today. Help me reach every voter — and fuel the fight still ahead — before midnight. | Peter - Today is it. The Primary Special Election for the United States Senate seat here in South Carolina, I'm not a politician. I never expected to be running for office, and I never wanted to. I'm doing this because I'm answering President Trump's call to serve, and because I believe South Carolina deserves a fighter in the Senate. Like Lindsey, I grew up in the back of a bar and liquor store, in one room. My parents worked every single day to make ends meet. There was no time for sickness and few vacations, because if the doors weren't open, no money was coming in. That's the kind of work ethic I've carried my whole life, from running a state agency with 130 employees and a $90 million budget to turning it into a national model for helping people find work and live independently. I'm a mother, a grandmother, and a wife. I support the Right to Life. I believe in showing ID to vote. I oppose DEI. I stand for the national anthem, I believe our veterans are heroes, and I will always Back the Blue. President Trump wants a fighter in the Senate - that's why he's in my corner in this race, and why I'm asking you to be in it with me. Here's what I need from you right now, in the final hours before the polls close: If you live in South Carolina, make sure you vote today, and don't stop there. Call your friends, your family, your neighbors, your coworkers. Make sure they have a plan to get to the polls before midnight. Every vote we don't turn out tonight is a vote we can't get back. Every dollar raised today will help us build the momentum we need not only to win today but also to win in November. And I need to be honest with you: winning tonight is only the first step. After this Primary Special Election, we still have a long road ahead to the General Election, and this fight doesn't end when the polls close. I will need you again. But it starts with tonight. Help me finish strong. Thank you, Darline Graham P.S. I am the first woman United States senator in South Carolina history. * 85% said that their local poll worker training left them feeling prepared to get the job done.

clean_body: Did you know about today’s holiday? | | | Here’s a fun fact: today is National Poll Worker Recruitment Day! In other words, it’s the perfect opportunity to sign up to be a poll worker for the November elections. Let’s face it: poll workers are heroes. They keep our elections running smoothly. They keep the process fair and efficient. And they help make sure everyone can cast their ballot and have it counted. But if a local elections office can’t find enough people who are able to serve, they might need to shut down voting locations, and voters might face longer lines at the ones that stay open. A study found that poll worker shortages contributed to longer lines for voters, with longer lines in precincts that had more people of color. To help close any gaps this year, we’ve launched an aggressive poll worker recruitment campaign alongside Power the Polls, a nonpartisan initiative which has driven over a million sign-ups and supported election administrators in thousands of precincts since its founding in 2020. People who’ve gotten involved through this organization have had overwhelmingly positive things to say: 95% said they had a satisfying experience. 88% said they’d be interested in serving again. * 85% said that their local poll worker training left them feeling prepared to get the job done. | In solidarity, The Fair Fight Action Team | = = | 1270 Caroline Street | Suite D120-430 | Atlanta, GA 30307 ©2026 Fair Fight Action - All rights reserved. Inside Scoop Issue: 8/11/2026
Primary Day in Minnesota
Minnesota Republicans head to the polls today in a governor's primary that has become a [proxy fight over](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0L3OozAQheGrMR0ID2CgcLENXbbdEk3GExgF_wg7YXP3q2jv4OtO9Ujn_XNbbyiHhO03eraS8-qiW5_8Sad4PIVz4VzK-fIJg3MrtGDqdqq1XpGKvHntsXJ2AD09poqtHifTzzAOutrtfRxnrWfkgV1HM7UPMsQG2m7QdxrmSuzXayetoRtmrRv9gGkGdv0AhAik-vaVHBZuJGRxnCnGlOIhRSg38dyqw-6lpKy6XwoWBct1Xc2FeZewlRj4L3oJfDYUvYIl8JUVLIQ-oWzhu3tjJtNpBcuTP7WXEDjHgvX__5_6ROJcl1hfWGhXsFSndemS45BsRtW3m0c5vn5VftrvbeFfAAAA__8rVYNR) President Trump's clout with the state GOP. Trump-endorsed MyPillow founder Mike Lindell leads a crowded field that includes House Speaker Lisa Demuth, with [polls open](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckLvOnDAQhZ8GOiM8mMsWLtLQ_WlToll72B3FF8QYyL59RPIGf3l0pHP0fb--li_kwOn1EyNZFll89stv-mw7R9yZpJCUsh9xw-T9Ai0Mqp2U1gu6wictBmtve9DTOtVk9TgN5gFjr-u3XZ9Go1txcCOANlM7wtjptu-eAF1nxprtvddOWkPXP7Ru9ArTA8ibHhwiuMq0x-axUMNJ2JO4nLctBy7spMn7qw72XcomVfejgrmC-bquZs1_El3SuBwrmAOfpO5cwfyf6qMokCuck6h_QJFTIskFlcsp3ZU7ijppjzkVdbG4nISTknyUt3K458AJFQZ8YsR6t367OASWYaxM-4rI4T6vy3eNnhb-BgAA__-qxotN) statewide alongside contests in Wisconsin, Connecticut, Vermont and Alabama. The state party establishment openly resisted the [Lindell endorsement](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0L2S3CAQBOCnQRkqMYu0KCBwouycOlTNwkg7dfwVcCvf27vWfgNnHXVXf78-9g_kwOn8iZEst7b77PdP-i6VI1am1qn1Xr9iweT9DhMscjJSqR1d5xftGgdvZ1DmMANZdTeLXuE-q-FpHXl3aKTHbA66O1j14h6Lct4_Hn5Vx8D23TcZpeA2r0qN6gCzAnk9g0MEJ_T0VTx2Gjk19tRczqXkwJ1dG3M9h2CfvZcmbj8EbAK267rGC9uT09lzot8YOVEdXY4CtkRXE7A5jAX5TO_cOnYSsOnFqEXdBGx_z8rIKVHLHeWZX1RTrvIfybeM_EkycPIUgqTkc20UKXUB21CtLxeHwG25Cz2dETm8x4f-v7gvC38CAAD__8kakBA), warning he is poorly positioned against Democrat Amy Klobuchar in November. Record absentee turnout suggests unusual midterm-year intensity, and the winner inherits a Republican bid to flip a reliably blue seat in one of the party's top targets this cycle. ★★★
Iran Blockade Escalates
The standoff over the Strait of Hormuz sharpened Tuesday as U.S. Central Command reported it has redirected 55 commercial vessels, disabled three and boarded two while [enforcing the blockade](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0D2OpDAQxfHTQGZEVWM-AgebkPWmG6Jqu6BLa7Blm2ZmTj_qOcKEL_lJ7__vvtxJvBzbX9rZSM6LC275z58xyU5JOBfOpaRzj3Q4t2CLvWpHBbCQLfLipaPaGY0wrmPNBoax7yYcNNRP08GDUPfrBDRpDZYfbuCHHdER6Am7Wszba0cAvOkJoIEVxwnZdRotEdqqa8_oqHAjRxbH2YYQY_BSxOYmpK325llKzNXtT4VzhfN1Xc0aPg6-cmPDXuHs5cXqvSucJdGhLkrq55GSnIi9eoa0n1-Kzu3MRQHUybh4ifeS-6Hq2m0n8W-tLr9N9DL4HQAA__8mSXnv) on Iranian ports. Trump declared himself "number one" on Tehran's target list, and an adviser to Iran's supreme leader invoked the Carter-era hostage crisis in a pointed warning. Military analysts note the waterway's [strategic weight](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0DGS4yAQQNHTQGYVNAihgGATZd50Q1ULWnbXSoIS2Jq5_ZSvMAf4P3j_7vMdeePj8Rd3ClzrnHKa_9N3OXnHk6k2qq2dr73gkdIMCtxN-ZvWM8bGb5otyhR60H71koIevLMjDL2Wz7AqR9pgIrsuMDrvBjRuQB-XxSzj4iSHz095rcH0o9adXsGPQMn2EBEhCqteJWGjjo_KiWrMuZS8ceNYu3w-5BaerZUqzB8Bk4Dpuq5uzV8HXbWLeRcwvTlRFjA5q4yyo-mt1iDPkMrF28bVDcKqx468fQLZfqvwDvATAAD__wvubOc), with roughly a fifth of the world's seaborne oil normally transiting it. The administration continues to frame Iran's financial collapse as leverage, pressing Tehran to end the war it says began with [months of aggression](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckD1uhDAQRk8DnREz_JnCRRq6TZsSzeJhdxSDLdssSU4fkSOk_Jqn772P23wjcbI_3mljIynN1tv5k79DlI2icMqcco7HFmi3dsYae1VrBTDTkuXFc0ulNR2CXnXJBgbdtyMOHZRP09-5H1cGfdfYILcNtQ3cwYLVY0f9Woq5eLUGwKYbASpYUY_Itu1wIcKlaOsjWMpcyZ7Eclq8D8E7ybKkysdH6cwz55CK5q3AqcDpPM9q9V87n6la_Fbg5OTF6toFThJpVydFdST1J6VSjiRZ-VU9fdyOn0uuHtT1q4zGhlOck9QPRVs_NhJ3Qcv831Ivg78BAAD__9BcesA) against shipping and U.S. forces. ★★★
Deportation Numbers Climb
Fresh Homeland Security data shows arrests, detentions and self-deportations all [running higher](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0DGSrCAQgOHTQDYW3aBiQPASs3nphlYv4EzXolDC6O7tt-YKe4D_D76P-3InTrw__tMWHde6hByWr_hTDt7o4FhbrK0dr63QHsKCCoebsjeAhXzjMy6GZHA9gl2tjA5GO5gJxx7k04096ok-rfcweAoE4xpXo6AfzUqkg2T3_ikLgLqfADpY0U4Yg-nRE6EXRr1KoBY73iuHWH3OpeTEjX3t8vGQyT1bK1XofwJngfN1Xd2av_d41c7nTeB8cohZ4DwYpUErbRAA5eFCuTglrsMojHpsxOkdyPZXhdPhbwAAAP__IIRs-w) than a year ago, underscoring the enforcement machinery the administration has built out since the DHS shutdown ended. Yet the numbers arrive amid open friction on the right, where prominent MAGA voices argue Secretary Markwayne Mullin's [strong figures](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckDuupDAQAE9jMiPcY34BwSZkb9MNUQ_uB62HbeRuhp3br-YKm5dKpfrztXwhH5y23xhpYpEl5LD80PssHLEwiZKoliuemEJYoIHONoN1bsFV-UWLxypMLbjhe6hocv3Q-RH61lX75J0D3zypdb4L0IzPxwjtE8LwwNDDGiqePr5mcA4e7ehc7b5hGIGCb2FFhNX45joDKtWchAPJmvN55oOVV6lz2apj2lVPMY9fBmYD833f9Y2yc9o0J_qLkROVes3RwJzolg-zs5Ld8yVkYPZdP3bjaGCOWH5ufCey8ToOTnZHsaIlp80GOnNRVM7Jpis-qYhFtWEXG3FDG1i0XKJid44W0_vGt4G5KlM4bz4Olq43vtki8vGpqfR_b78m-BcAAP__RZeUuQ) still fall short of the mass-deportation pace the base demands. Supporters counter that thousands of newly hired officers and the end of sanctuary-driven slowdowns fueled a [record enforcement month](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckLvOnDAQhZ8GOiM8y8UULtJs96dNiSb2AKPgizxmyb59tFGeINU51Tn6vh9f6xfyyXH_joEsi6w--fUXvXPhgIVJKkmt5QoZo_cr9DCp3iitV3SVX7QO2Ho7gjabacnq2UzDAvOo28P2ZIbFuAVmwAX1No9j7x_LZGjaxhGgZfvZ643W8BgXrTu9gVmA_DCCQwTXDP2VPVbqOAp7EpdSzunkyk66VPb2tEetWZrHtwaeDTzv--629DvSLZ1LoYHnJQ08_xIo9IEjSy1YOUXFIfD-r-dLDrVddIpiR-on7ztJVVjKJ0KK9VC4U3RvdbDUVN5tsT7ffJ4s09wM_R6Qz89nW_9X5MvCnwAAAP__VE-IxA), and that internal impatience risks obscuring a genuine operational surge heading into the fall campaign.
Trump's Tele-Rally Playbook

The president is [doubling down](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckLGOpiAURp8GOwxcUfkLim3sZtstzQ3cX29WgQCOO2-_cR5h-i_nyzl_PtYP5IPj9htPclzrGlJY_9JXLnxiYaqNamvlOjPGEFZQMEllpdYr-saftBrsghtB27ftyOnZTuYF86i73QVlhhAsTd5aZcdRvd5WTzb4wQwTmLFj9_CU1RqG8aV1r99gX0DBjOARwQujrhywUc-xcqDqU8o5HdzY1z6VrTvc3lquYvglYBGw3Pfd31h3jltLkf7hyZFK79MpYIl012ezcyO5p6uSgMVMVs_zLGD51pRXDFRk20kWDFikxzMjb1HWVrDR9iW_I9BBvnGKD7ArLuSbj4PrNAujthP5eD679tOmnw7-BwAA__-gaYlP) on phone-in tele-rallies for downballot Republicans, logging dozens per cycle even as his in-person travel slows amid the Iran war and a packed governing calendar.

★★★
South Carolina Seat in Play

Voters also weigh a special primary for the late Lindsey Graham's Senate seat, with appointed Sen.
